articles.title: Mortality and disability after hospitalisation for injuries in low-income and middle-income countries: a cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Mortality and disability after injuries are high in low-income and middle-income countries (LMICs). Improving outcomes for injured patients requires knowledge of their associated factors. We aimed to assess post-injury mortality and disability and their associations with access to health care across LMICs with different injury burdens, health-care systems, and contexts.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Hospitalised patients in Ghana, Pakistan, Rwanda, and South Africa with moderate-to-severe injuries were recruited and followed up until 3 months after discharge or death. Injured patients of any age who were admitted to facilities for more than 12 h or died within 12 h of admission were included. Data were collected between Feb 17, 2023, and Aug 31, 2024, using the REDCap electronic data platform. Our primary outcome was a composite of 3-month mortality or moderate-to-severe disability (assessed using the WHO Disability Assessment Schedule). Secondary outcomes were disability at 3 months after discharge, mortality up to 3 months after discharge (including in-hospital mortality), and in-hospital mortality. In multivariable analysis, we tested the associations of these outcomes with access to health-care variables of previous health-care encounters, transport to the hospital (private vs ambulance vs other), delays in reaching the hospital, and hospital level (secondary vs tertiary), controlling for age, sex, education, wealth, and injury type and severity.

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: 9720 patients admitted to 19 hospitals capable of providing definitive care for injuries, serving urban and rural settings, were eligible for inclusion in the study. Of those, 8858 (91·1%; 6788 male, 2047 female, and 23 [<1%] with missing sex data; median age 31 years [IQR 20-43]) were enrolled and 8687 (89·4%) completed hospital follow-up, with 5835 patients followed up at 3 months. At 3 months, 2476 (47·6%) of 5199 patients with available primary outcome data had died or were disabled. In-hospital mortality was 6·1% (531 of 8687), 3-month mortality was 9·7% (616 of 6366), and 3-month disability was 40·6% (1860 of 4583). Higher odds of the primary outcome were associated with arrival by ambulance (odds ratio 1·86, 95% CI 1·51-2·29), and lower odds were associated with a previous health-care encounter (0·61, 0·52-0·71). Hospital level (1·14, 0·96-1·35) and delays in reaching the facility (0·86, 0·74-1·00) were not associated with the primary outcome.

abstract.label: INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: The high post-injury mortality and disability are associated with health system factors that must be better understood before potentially expensive service models are introduced or expanded. Investment in pre-hospital care, ambulance systems, and centralised specialist trauma centres is unlikely to achieve its intended benefits unless services are appropriately planned, integrated, coordinated, and staffed across the care pathway. High-quality routine data are also essential to guide service improvement and enable robust quasi-experimental evaluations of whether these investments improve patient outcomes, for whom, and under what circumstances.

abstract.text: National Institute for Health and Care Research.

articles.title: Multimorbidity and Acute-Care Use Among Older Decedents With Advanced Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Retrospective Population-Based Cohort Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Advanced chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is associated with substantial multimorbidity and hospital-based care near the end of life. We described multimorbidity, acute-care utilization, and documented palliative care exposure among older decedents with advanced COPD.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study using routinely collected data from an integrated health system. The cohort included eligible decedents aged 55 years or older with advanced COPD who died during 2016–2020 and 2022–2023; 2021 was excluded because the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted usual utilization patterns. Multimorbidity was characterized using the age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), comorbidity count, and individual conditions. Outcomes included total hospital admissions, hospitalizations per patient, emergency department visits, intensive care unit days, hospitalization duration, procedure burden, and documented palliative care exposure during the final year of life.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The cohort included 2261 decedents. Mean age at death was 77.75 years, mean age-adjusted CCI was 8.73, and mean comorbidity count was 4.05. A total of 9489 hospital admissions were recorded; the mean was 4.74 hospitalizations per patient. Only 167 patients (7.4%) had documented palliative care exposure. Women were older at death, whereas men had higher mean CCI scores, comorbidity counts, and recorded procedure burden.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Older decedents with advanced COPD experienced substantial multimorbidity and hospital-centered acute-care use, while documented palliative care exposure was uncommon. Survival analyses by palliative care exposure were excluded because exposure timing was unavailable and fixed retrospective classification would be vulnerable to immortal-time bias.

articles.title: Physician-level variation exceeds time-of-day variation in diagnostic resource utilization in low-acuity emergency department care.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency physicians working prolonged shifts may show temporal variation in clinical practice. We examined whether diagnostic resource utilization differed across scheduled shift periods in a structured low-acuity emergency department setting.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective observational study included 11 032 visits for upper respiratory tract infection, myalgia, abdominal pain, or headache across 12 nonconsecutive 24-hour shifts (5 December 2025-19 January 2026) in a high-volume tertiary emergency department in Turkey. Visits were classified as early (0-5 h; 08:30-13:30), mid (5-10 h; 13:30-18:30), or late (10-16 h; 18:30-00:30) based on elapsed time since the scheduled shift start at 08:30. Multivariable logistic regression with physician-level clustered standard errors (19 clusters) adjusted for age, sex, and diagnostic category.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Laboratory testing rates were 9.5% across all periods (P = .997); imaging rates were 13.5%, 12.8%, and 12.6% (P = .485). The composite utilization score did not differ significantly (P = .682). Late-period consultation was lower than in the early period (odds ratio = 0.541, 95% confidence interval: 0.306-0.957), although this finding was limited by the low event count (n = 82). Inter-physician variation substantially exceeded shift-period variation, with laboratory rates ranging from 3.5% to 21.5% and imaging rates from 6.3% to 28.7%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this low-acuity emergency department setting, scheduled shift period was not measurably associated with increased laboratory or imaging utilization. Physician-level variation appeared more prominent than shift-period variation, supporting prospective studies incorporating fatigue, workload, and decision-quality measures.

articles.title: Medical management of major incidents and mass casualty events during military operations: a consensus statement.
Prehospital Births in the Region of Southern Denmark-A Cohort From 2016 to 2024.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Unplanned births outside hospitals involve higher risks of complications for mothers and newborns and require special obstetric or pediatric skills. However, ambulance calls for childbirth are rare, making it difficult for ambulance staff to maintain their skills. In Europe, unplanned out-of-hospital deliveries constitute 0.10% to 0.61% of all births. The exact number of prehospital births in the Region of Southern Denmark remains unknown. The study aimed to determine the extent of unplanned prehospital births attended by the ambulance service outside hospitals in the Region of Southern Denmark from January 2016 through June 2024. We further aimed to identify where the unplanned pre-hospital births took place and to report any birth-related complications in the mothers or newborns encountered by ambulance staff.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The study was a cross-sectional study utilizing the pre-hospital electronic Patient Medical Record system over 8 years in a mixed urban-rural area with a population of 1.2 million people. All prehospital medical records for ambulance missions dispatched for childbirths were manually examined. The study period spanned from January 2016 through June 2024.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Out of 1,137,222 ambulance dispatches, 3543 cases (0.31%) involved a dispatch code related to childbirth. Many labor incidents were considered uneventful by the prehospital personnel. Of all ambulance runs related to childbirth, we identified 310 births in the Region of Southern Denmark in which ambulance staff assisted with complicated out-of-hospital deliveries. An additional 10 labor cases were regarded as sufficiently complex that obstetric manoeuvres aimed at delaying the delivery of the baby were performed prehospitally, while the mother was rushed to hospital for delivery.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Births outside the hospital while the mother is in the care of the EMS were rare, occurring in 0.03% of all ambulance missions. Most of the births took place without complications for both mother and neonate. In four cases, however, the neonate was in cardiac arrest and required resuscitation. Given the limited exposure to prehospital births, we suggest incorporating training in handling these rare events into routine training for prehospital caregivers.

abstract.label: EDITORIAL COMMENT
abstract.text: This cohort study presents obstetrical cases that have been managed first in the prehospital setting by ambulance personnel. Obstetrical outcomes related to this are presented, and there are considerations for what can be desirable as preparation and competencies for ambulance responses for these types of cases.

articles.title: Hospitalization and Death Acceptance: A Meta-Ethnography of Perceptions of Hospital as a Place of Death for Nursing Home Residents.
articles.journal_full: International journal of older people nursing

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Efforts to reduce hospital transfers from nursing homes at the end of life have received considerable attention. However, less is known about how hospitals are understood and experienced as places of death for nursing home residents.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To synthesize qualitative evidence exploring stakeholder perceptions of hospital as a place of death for older adults living in nursing homes.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: A meta-ethnography of qualitative evidence following the Meta-ethnography Reporting Guidelines (eMERGe). Four bibliographic databases (MEDLINE, CINAHL, PsychINFO and Scopus) were systematically searched to identify all studies published from January 2012 to March 2024.

abstract.label: REVIEW METHODS
abstract.text: Studies were included if they reported qualitative findings on nursing home residents dying in hospital. Following quality appraisal, first- and second-order constructs were extracted and translated across studies using reciprocal and refutational analysis to develop third-order interpretations.

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: Two overarching interpretive themes were generated: (1) Controlling Symptoms of Dying: Comfort and Discomfort; and (2) Acceptance of Death After All Efforts to Save Life Have Been Exhausted. Hospitals were perceived as both impersonal environments and medically resource-rich settings that legitimize death through medical authority.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Hospitals occupy a paradoxical position in end-of-life care for nursing home residents. While often viewed as clinically oriented and less personal, they are also perceived to provide symptom control and reassurance that 'everything possible' has been done. Addressing these perceptions-alongside strengthening palliative capacity within nursing homes-is essential to supporting residents' preferences and enabling high-quality end-of-life care across settings.

abstract.label: IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE
abstract.text: Nurses can support more person-centred end-of-life care by strengthening palliative symptom management in nursing homes, engaging residents and families in early advance care planning, and improving communication about dying and hospital treatment. These practices may help reduce avoidable hospital transfers and support residents to die in their preferred place.

articles.title: Ebola disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: challenges and opportunities for emergency and critical care.
articles.journal_full: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine

articles.title: Pediatric Rural Interfacility Transfers by Emergency Medical Services.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Interfacility transports (IFTs) are critical for the care of pediatric patients in the United States (US), particularly in rural areas that may have limited pediatric specialty resources. Given the paucity of data describing rural pediatric IFTs, we aimed to characterize pediatric rural IFTs in the US.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective, observational study using the 2023 National Emergency Medical Services Information System dataset. Rural IFTs involving patients aged ≥1 day to <18 years were included and stratified into the following age groups: infant (1 day to <1 year), toddler (1-2 years), preschooler (3-5 years), young child (6-11 years), and teenager (12 to <18 years). Using descriptive statistics, we analyzed patient demographics, clinical characteristics, emergency medical services (EMS) transport characteristics, medications, procedures, and transport time intervals.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We identified 29,992 rural pediatric IFTs (median age: 8 years [IQR: 2-14 years]; 52.9% male). Teenagers represented the largest age group transferred (38.8%). Respiratory diseases (12.3%) were the most common primary impression overall, whereas psychiatric and behavioral health conditions predominated among teenagers. Ground transport accounted for most IFTs (79.4%), and advanced life support units were the most common transport level of care (62.7%). Infants demonstrated the highest proportion of specialty critical care transports (32.1%) and longer median response and total call intervals across transport modalities compared with older age groups. Younger children more commonly received respiratory-focused medications and procedures, whereas teenagers more frequently received pain management and sedative medications.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Nearly 30,000 pediatric rural IFTs occurred in 2023, with substantial age-related differences in clinical presentations, transport characteristics, and EMS interventions. Infants more frequently required specialty critical care transport and experienced longer transport intervals, whereas psychiatric and behavioral health conditions represented a substantial proportion of adolescent transfers. These findings underscore the importance of pediatric-focused EMS preparedness, transport readiness, and clinical training initiatives to support safe rural pediatric interfacility care.

articles.title: Missed Opportunities for Prehospital Transfusion in Pediatric Trauma.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Prehospital blood transfusion has been associated with improved outcomes among pediatric trauma patients, but its utilization nationally remains poorly understood. We recently conducted a similar study that builds upon the findings of the investigation by Ramgopal et al. to identify potential missed opportunities for prehospital transfusion in pediatric trauma.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We utilized the National EMS Information System dataset from 2018-2023 to identify emergency medical services (EMS) responses for pediatric (<18 years of age) trauma patients. We identified trauma patients using the CDC Injury Mortality Diagnosis Matrix related ICD-10 codes. We identified patients at increased risk of benefiting from a transfusion using age-adjusted positive shock index thresholds. The outcome of interested was prehospital blood or blood product transfusion.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We found there were 1,663,601 total 9-1-1 EMS activations to a scene for pediatric trauma. There were 363,844 patients with a positive shock index who were considered to be at increased risk of benefiting from a prehospital transfusion, but only 287 (0.1%) of these patients received a prehospital transfusion. Only 10 (2%) of the 468 patients who experienced a cardiac arrest after the arrival of EMS to the scene received a hospital transfusion.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Together, our results indicate prehospital transfusion rates ranging from 0.1% to 1.01% among potentially eligible pediatric trauma patients. Although positive shock index does not confirm hemorrhagic shock, these findings suggest underutilization of prehospital blood transfusion among pediatric trauma patients.

articles.title: Evaluating Creative Cognition as a Risk and Resilience Factor for Burnout in Pediatric Emergency Medicine.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Burnout is common among pediatric emergency medicine (PEM) physicians, but the relationship between creative problem-solving (CPS) preferences and burnout is not well understood. This study examined associations between CPS mindsets and burnout in PEM.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This cross-sectional study included PEM (attending physicians and fellows) from 3 emergency departments. Measures: Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey for Burnout; FourSight for CPS preferences (clarifying, ideating, developing, implementing). The primary outcome was the association between burnout and CPS preferences, and the secondary outcomes were comparisons of burnout prevalence and CPS preferences in PEM compared with published norms.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Participation was 100%, with 96.7% providing complete data. Participants: female 58%; median age 41 years; 51% White, 23% Asian, and 83% married. High clarifying scores were associated with greater emotional exhaustion (EE; adjusted β = 0.67; 95% CI, 0.15 to 1.19), with a stronger association among women (adjusted β = 0.76; 95% CI, 0.03 to 1.48). Ideating was associated with higher personal accomplishment (PA; β = 0.31; 95% CI, 0.08 to 0.55). In univariate analysis, female sex (β = 5.03; 95% CI, 0.17 to 9.89) and educational debt (β = 5.46; 95% CI, 0.47 to 10.4) were each associated with higher EE. Compared with health care norms, PEM demonstrated higher PA scores (mean = 5.00; 95% CI, 4.84 to 5.15 vs. 4.30). PEM were more likely to show an implementing mindset (55% vs. 21%, P < 0.001) and less likely to show a Developing mindset (10% vs. 23%, P = 0.007).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A clarifying mindset was associated with higher EE, particularly among women, while Ideating was associated with greater PA. CPS self-awareness and targeted training may offer novel strategies to mitigate burnout among PEM.

articles.title: [From acute care to long-term management: reflections on models for stroke recurrence prevention].

abstract.text: Stroke is the leading cause of death and disability in China. In recent years, acute stroke care in China has improved substantially with the continued development of stroke centers and rapid advances in emergency reperfusion therapy technology. Nevertheless, the risk of stroke recurrence remains high, and long-term management has become a critical determinant of long-term prognosis of patients. Currently, a large amount of evidence has established the efficacy of secondary prevention strategies, including antithrombotic therapy, risk factor control, and lifestyle modification. The main challenge in preventing stroke recurrence is not the lack of effective interventions, but the lack of an effective delivery system to translate evidence-based interventions and guideline recommendations into sustained, standardized practice throughout the course of care. Drawing on experience in stroke prevention and chronic disease management at home and abroad, this article analyzes the problems of inadequate long-term risk factor control, declining medication adherence, and discontinuity of care. We propose that stroke recurrence prevention should further shift from a model centered primarily on acute-phase treatment to a systematic management that spans in-hospital and out-of-hospital settings and covers the entire disease course. We propose a model oriented toward reducing disability and disease burden, grounded in standardized assessment, aimed at comprehensive control, delivered through continuous management, and supported by multistakeholder collaboration. This article may provide reference for further improving China's stroke prevention and control system and advancing full-cycle health management of stroke.

articles.title: Bystander AED Effectiveness Despite Low Utilisation in OHCA.
authors: Korean Cardiac Arrest Research Consortium (KoCARC) Investigators

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Observational estimates of bystander automated external defibrillator (AED) effectiveness are inconsistent in settings with mature public-access defibrillation infrastructure but low utilization, partly because the conventional reference group pools emergency medical services (EMS)-shocked with non-defibrillated patients. We estimated bystander AED effectiveness against a partitioned no-defibrillation reference, tested effect modification by location, and quantified the deployment-utilization gap.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective analysis of a prospectively collected multicenter out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) registry (Korea, October 2015-June 2025; 23,918 adults of presumed medical etiology). A three-tier prehospital defibrillation-provider variable was defined: bystander AED applied (n = 383); EMS-delivered shock without preceding bystander AED (n = 5,975); and no prehospital defibrillation (reference; n = 17,560). Primary outcomes were survival to discharge and good neurological outcome (Cerebral Performance Category 1-2), analyzed by multivariable logistic regression with propensity-score, inverse-probability-weighting and location-stratified secondary analyses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Bystander AED application was associated with improved survival (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.60; 95% CI 1.19-2.14) and good neurological outcome (2.31; 1.65-3.23), comparable to that of EMS-delivered shock; the pooled-control specification attenuated estimates to non-significance (survival 1.09; neurological 1.14). Shock-delivered applications significantly exceeded EMS-delivered shock for neurological outcome (aOR 1.43; p = 0.03). Effectiveness did not differ by location (interaction p ≥ 0.15). Bystander AED was applied in 8.5% of Public-area versus 1.9% of Nonpublic AED-opportunity cases-a 4.5-fold gap.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Bystander AED was associated with improved outcomes when applied, comparable to or exceeding EMS-delivered shock; the dominant constraint was the deployment-utilization gap, greatest in residential settings. Residential rapid-activation infrastructure warrants policy priority alongside, not instead of, continued device placement.

articles.title: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis of Geographic Distance in Immediate Free Flap and Implant-Based Breast Reconstruction.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Patient proximity to a surgical center is an important consideration in the coordination and delivery of high-quality postoperative care. Implant-based and autologous breast reconstruction require different perioperative resources and may be impacted in a varying manner by distance from the health care center. This study evaluated the impact of geographic distance on clinical and financial outcomes in free flap and implant-based breast reconstruction.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective review was conducted of 176 free flap and 239 implant-based immediate breast reconstructions performed from 2017 to 2023 at a single academic center. Patients were classified by great-circle distance to the medical center as far (≥ 30 miles) or near (< 30 miles). Propensity score-matched cohorts were created for free flap (n = 70 pairs) and implant-based (n = 79 pairs) reconstruction, controlling for demographics, comorbidities, treatment variables, and laterality. Clinical outcomes, wound complications, revision procedures, opioid use, hospital resource utilization, and financial measures between near and far patients for each reconstruction type were compared using paired t-tests, McNemar's tests, and exact binomial testing for sparse outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In the flap cohort, near- and far-distance groups did not differ significantly in operative time, length of stay, intensive care use, postoperative communication, emergency department visits, opioid requirements, complication rates, revision procedures, or financial outcomes. Total flap loss and thromboembolic events were rare and did not differ significantly between groups. In the implant-based cohort, there were no significant differences in operative time, length of stay, postoperative communication, emergency department visits, opioid requirements, complication rates, revision procedures, or financial outcomes between groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Geographic distance was not associated with worse clinical or financial outcomes after immediate breast reconstruction. These findings suggest that high-volume academic centers can deliver consistent reconstructive outcomes across a range of patient proximities.

articles.title: An update on neuro-otology and neuro-ophthalmology - focusing on new developments in the last three years.

abstract.text: Vertigo, dizziness, and imbalance are among the most frequent presenting symptoms in primary care and in the emergency department (ED). The clinical diagnosis is based on a structured patient history and bedside examination of the vestibular system and the ocular motor system, looking especially for central ocular motor signs. Recent guidelines, such as the GRACE-3 guideline on acute vertigo and dizziness, the increasing availability of bedside diagnostic algorithms, and the use of quantitative vestibular and ocular motor testing in both the ED-setting and in the outpatient center have facilitated and standardized the approach to the dizzy patient. Here we review recent developments in neuro-otology and neuro-ophthalmology, covering the period after the latest neuro-otology update was published in this journal in 2023. Both new-onset acute, episodic and chronic vestibular conditions are discussed separately, highlighting advancements in disease characterization, diagnostic criteria, and treatment strategies. While major progress has been made in terms of the pathophysiology, etiology, genetics, and diagnostic criteria of peripheral, central, and functional vestibular diseases as well as ocular motor disorders, this knowledge has to be transferred into clinical practice. Systematic teaching of doctors to increase knowledge and to improve skills in applying the different tests in clinical practice on a high level are identified challenges. In terms of treatment, there is still a very great need for state-of-the art clinical trials applying approved therapies.

articles.title: Self-inflicted thoracoabdominal nail-gun injury presenting as STEMI: diagnostic challenges in a time-critical care pathway.

abstract.text: A 60-year-old male with a history of depression and a prior nail-gun thoracic injury was found in shock at home, with inferior ST-segment elevation on the paramedic electrocardiogram prompting pre-hospital ST-elevation myocardial infarction pathway activation. Initial high-sensitivity troponin was elevated, consistent with the presumed diagnosis. Normal coronary angiography and preserved ventricular function were discordant with the patient's ongoing haemodynamic instability. Four small anterior chest puncture wounds and radiopaque foreign bodies demonstrated on chest radiograph and angiographic imaging did not initially prompt consideration of penetrating injury. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography, performed to exclude pulmonary embolism, identified four nail-gun projectiles penetrating the heart and stomach. The patient underwent sternotomy and laparotomy with repair of cardiac, diaphragmatic, and gastric injuries. The case illustrates the challenges of situation awareness and diagnostic reassessment within time-critical, protocol-driven care.

articles.title: Just the Facts: Management of patients presenting to the emergency department following therapeutic abortion.
Skin and soft tissue infections clinical pathway concordance in pediatric emergency and urgent care sites.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Skin and soft tissue infections (SSTIs) are major drivers of antibiotic prescribing in pediatric emergency departments (EDs) and urgent care clinics (UCCs). Although guidelines recommend limited diagnostics and antibiotics, practice variation persists, and the influence of sociodemographic factors remains underexplored. We evaluated concordance with a pediatric SSTI clinical pathway (CP) and examined variation across sociodemographic factors.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study included children aged 6 months-18 years evaluated for SSTIs at 2 EDs and 3 UCCs in a Midwestern academic health system from July 2022 through June 2024. We defined concordance per national guidelines and institutional CP, including appropriate diagnostic, antibiotic selection, and antibiotic treatment duration. Generalized linear mixed model examined associations between concordance and patient/visit characteristics.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 4,190 encounters, overall CP concordance was 59.0%. Diagnostic concordance was high (86.0%), as was treatment duration concordance (87.8% when antibiotics were indicated). Antibiotic selection showed the lowest concordance (72.6%), largely driven by unnecessary prescribing for diagnoses not requiring antibiotics, such as paronychia. Overall concordance was highest in the younger age group (6 months-2 years) and UCC visits. Black non-Hispanic children had higher odds of concordant care compared with White non-Hispanic children (odds ratio [OR] 1.56, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.28-1.88). Return visits were uncommon (2.1% concordant vs 3.3% nonconcordant).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Standardized SSTI pathways support consistent diagnostics and appropriate treatment duration, but reducing unnecessary antibiotic prescribing remains a key stewardship opportunity.

articles.title: Inadequate empirical therapy and unnecessary broad-spectrum antibiotic use in community-onset bloodstream infection: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal_full: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate empirical antimicrobial therapy (EAT) adequacy, risk factors for inadequate EAT (IEAT) and multidrug-resistant (MDR) infection and unnecessary broad-spectrum use in emergency department (ED) patients with bloodstream infection (BSI).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort study of adults with community-onset BSI at a tertiary-care ED (2022-2024). Adequate EAT was ≥1 administered agent with in vitro activity. Logistic regression identified factors associated with IEAT, unnecessary broad-spectrum therapy and MDR infection. Cox regression assessed 7- and 30-day mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1716 BSI episodes, 464 (27%) received IEAT or no EAT. MDR organisms accounted for 370 cases (21.6%) and were associated with IEAT (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 7.40, 95% CI 5.55-9.93). Of 606 patients receiving broad-spectrum EAT, 490 (80.9%) regimens were unnecessary. Community-acquired infection was associated with unnecessary broad-spectrum therapy (aOR 3.96, 95% CI 1.65-11.79), and healthcare-associated infection with MDR infection (aOR 2.02, 95% CI 1.31-3.14). Seven-day mortality was associated with polymicrobial infection (aHR 2.14, 95% CI 1.39-3.30), long-term care facility residence (aHR 1.72, 95% CI 1.20-2.46) and vasopressor requirement (aHR 3.20, 95% CI 2.21-4.62).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: IEAT was associated with MDR pathogens, and unnecessary broad-spectrum use was common. Improved MDR risk stratification may optimize EAT by reducing inadequate coverage and avoidable broad-spectrum exposure in the ED.

articles.title: Beyond the Room: Bed-Level Isolation as Surge-Capable Infrastructure for Pandemics and Disasters-A Conceptual Framework.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.text: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed a structural limit of hospital isolation infrastructure: airborne infection isolation and protective-environment rooms are fixed assets that cannot be multiplied at the speed of a respiratory surge, and the constraint is more severe in field hospitals after disasters. Pandemic workarounds (ward conversion, portable negative-air machines, and modular container construction) each addressed part of the problem at the cost of bed capacity, sustained containment, or deployment speed. This concept paper aims to synthesize the failure modes of room-scale isolation into a device-agnostic set of clinical and engineering criteria for deployable bed-level single-patient isolation with switchable pressure polarity, in-enclosure air-quality monitoring, and on-board between-patient decontamination. These criteria are summarized in a requirements matrix, and one illustrative implementation is outlined. The intended contribution is a framework to guide future design, testing, and evaluation, not a validated solution; no validation data are presented, and none should be inferred.

articles.title: Effects of extreme environmental conditions on the skin barrier: a pilot study from the "Under The Pole" project with spectral and biometric measurements.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Under The Pole is an ambitious underwater exploration program in extreme environments, particularly in deep and polar regions. Diving in the cold and saline waters of the Arctic exposes the skin to intense thermal and osmotic stress, potentially altering its barrier function. This study aimed to evaluate both the acute and long-term effects of repeated cold-water diving on skin hydration and barrier integrity during a two-month Arctic expedition.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Seven healthy Caucasian male participants without facial skin lesions were monitored throughout the expedition. Skin appearance, hydration and transepidermal water loss (TEWL) were measured. Stratum corneum (SC) samples were collected by tape stripping and analyzed using Raman spectroscopy and Attenuated Total Reflection-Fourier Transform Infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy to assess molecular changes in lipids and proteins.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The findings reveal a dynamic, multiphasic adaptation process of the skin barrier under extreme polar conditions: (i) Immediate phase (hours): Acute hydration increase and transient barrier disruption due to immersion and temperature shock. (ii) Short-term phase (days): Adaptive homeostatic response, characterized by decreased water loss and lipid disorganization and protein structural rearrangement within the SC. (iii) Long-term phase (weeks): Gradual barrier fatigue with partial recovery of lipid order and protein structure, but persistent microstructural alterations evidenced by reduced hydration and elevated TEWL.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This study provides in situ evidence of dynamic skin adaptation to extreme Arctic conditions. Initial barrier disruption was followed by molecular reorganization and partial recovery, yet prolonged exposure led to cumulative dehydration and barrier fatigue. These insights improve understanding of cutaneous resilience and support the design of protective skincare strategies for extreme environments.

articles.title: Age-Related Differences in Asthma Recognition, Follow-Up and Home-Based Exacerbation Management among Children Hospitalized for Acute Asthma Exacerbations.
articles.journal_full: International archives of allergy and immunology

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The objectives of the study were to evaluate age-related differences in asthma diagnosis and management among children hospitalized for moderate-to-severe asthma exacerbations and to examine the relationship of regular follow-up and home-based exacerbation management with clinical outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective observational study included children aged 25 months to <18 years who were hospitalized for moderate-to-severe asthma exacerbations. Patients were categorized as preschool-aged (25-60 months) or school-aged (61 months to <18 years). Asthma diagnosis before hospitalization, regular follow-up, controller therapy use, caregiver education, initiation of home-based treatment, exacerbation history, and healthcare utilization were compared.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 104 children were included. Preschool children were less likely than school-aged children to have received an asthma diagnosis before hospitalization (56.5% vs. 83.3%, p = 0.008) and were more frequently managed with diagnoses such as bronchiolitis or bronchitis. Antibiotic use before asthma diagnosis was reported in 87.5% of the cohort. Patients attending regular follow-up had higher rates of controller therapy use, home-based exacerbation management education, and initiation of treatment at home (all p < 0.001). They also had fewer moderate-to-severe exacerbations (p < 0.001) and fewer emergency department visits (p = 0.036). Although children initiating home treatment had a greater previous exacerbation burden, they had fewer moderate-to-severe exacerbations during the preceding year than those who did not initiate treatment at home (p = 0.004). In multivariable analysis, regular follow-up remained independently associated with lower odds of recurrent moderate-to-severe exacerbations (aOR 0.03, 95% CI: 0.004-0.20; p < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Asthma was less often recognized before hospitalization in preschool children, and antibiotic use before diagnosis was common. Children attending regular follow-up more often received controller therapy and home-management education and had fewer moderate-to-severe exacerbations and emergency department visits. These findings highlight the importance of timely asthma recognition, regular follow-up, and practical caregiver education in children with recurrent wheezing or asthma, while the observational design precludes causal inference.

articles.title: Readmission Risk Coming Home After Rehabilitation in a Skilled Nursing Home With Dementia.
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Community dwelling people living with dementia (PLWD) are more likely to visit a skilled nursing home (SNH) after an acute hospital stay and have a high risk of readmission to the hospital. Staff in SNHs have familiarity with caring for PLWD that may mitigate readmissions, but dementia's role in readmissions for this high risk population remains unclear.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Using Health and Retirement Study data linked to Medicare claims between 2000 and 2019, this study aimed to investigate the role of dementia in hospital readmissions after a short rehabilitative stay (< 100 days) in the nursing home. Event-level data was analyzed for risk of 30-day hospital readmission following SNH discharge to the community using first Generalized Estimating Equations to estimate individual variables' association with readmission and then constructing a regression model to estimate the risk of readmission to the hospital using adjusted odds ratios.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 714 readmissions to the hospital out of 4527 discharges to the community following SNH stay (15.8%). A dementia diagnosis identified by Medicare claims, present for 42.2% of the population, was not associated with hospital readmission. Female sex, being married, and living in the Midwest or Western United States were associated with lower odds of readmission. Hospital or emergency department visits in the year prior to the index SNH admission and higher Charlson comorbidity scores were associated with higher odds of post-SNH discharge 30-day readmission.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A formal dementia diagnosis may serve as a signal to SNHs to provide enhanced support in their discharge processes. Intrinsic factors related to the patient's health status such as prior hospital use and comorbidity burden, in addition to social support factors such as marital status, play the greatest role in readmission risk. These characteristics should be recognized and mitigated by discharge planners, policy makers, and insurers making care coverage decisions.

articles.title: Opioid use, disability, and patient-reported cognitive impairment in migraine: Multi-country results from the Chronic Migraine Epidemiology and Outcomes-International Study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To characterize the population who do and do not use opioids to treat migraine in the Chronic Migraine Epidemiology and Outcomes-International (CaMEO-I) Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Opioids are not recommended for migraine treatment because of efficacy and safety limitations.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a post hoc analysis of CaMEO-I, an international, cross-sectional, observational, Web-based survey conducted in six countries from 2021 to 2022. Migraine status was determined by applying modified International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition, criteria, using a validated diagnostic questionnaire. Opioid users were defined as those who used opioids or kept them on hand to treat headache over the previous 30 days. Disability was assessed with the MIDAS, patient-reported cognitive impairment with the Migraine Cognitive Impairment Questionnaire (MCIQ), and acute treatment optimization with the Migraine Treatment Optimization Questionnaire (mTOQ). Multivariable binary logistic regression models evaluated the association between current opioid use and headache-related disability. Odds ratios (ORs) were adjusted for age, gender at birth, current consultation with a headache specialist, education, employment status, and treatment optimization.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 12,612 respondents with migraine who used prescription or over-the-counter medication for acute treatment of headaches (mean age, 41.8 years; 71.3% female) were included; 23.5% (2965/12,612) used opioids. Rates of opioid use for migraine ranged from 6.3% (127/2023) in Japan to 37.2% (814/2186) in France. The proportions of respondents with moderate to severe disability were higher among opioid users than nonusers at each level of treatment optimization on the mTOQ (very poor [64.7% {123/190} vs. 49.7% {373/750}], poor [62.6% {1110/1772} vs. 46.5% {2208/4747}], moderate [51.0% {338/663} vs. 35.6% {824/2314}], maximum [38.8% {132/340} vs. 19.9% {366/1836}]). Poorer treatment optimization was associated with significantly greater odds of moderate to severe disability (p < 0.001), and opioid use was associated with increased disability across all countries (p < 0.001). Opioid users had higher median (interquartile range [IQR]) patient-reported cognitive impairment scores on the MCIQ than nonusers (61.1 [44.4, 83.3] vs. 50.0 [33.3, 72.2], p < 0.001). Higher proportions of opioid users than nonusers had one or more doctor visits (49.3% [1462/2965] vs. 20.3% [1960/9647]), emergency department/urgent care visits (14.4% [426/2965] vs. 3.5% [336/9647]), and hospital stays (19.4% [571/2949] vs. 4.9% [472/9617]) for headache during the past 6 months (p < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Among CaMEO-I respondents with migraine, opioid users were more likely to have moderate or severe disability and patient-reported cognitive impairment, although causality cannot be determined from cross-sectional analyses. These results support the need for better treatment optimization.

articles.title: Prehospital Variables Do Not Reliably Identify Pelvic Fracture Morphologies Amenable to Pelvic Binder Application: A Retrospective Imaging Review.

abstract.text: BackgroundPelvic binders are used in prehospital settings for early stabilization when pelvic fractures are suspected. Although a rapid and cost-effective tool, uncertainties persist regarding their use prior to radiological confirmation of pelvic fracture.MethodsA review of adult patients with a pelvic fracture requiring trauma team activation who were admitted to a tertiary trauma center between 2020 and 2023 was conducted. The radiological studies were reviewed by four consultant orthopedic surgeons and were classified according to whether the application of a pelvic binder would be mechanically favorable, neutral, or potentially unfavorable. The area under the curve (AUC) was calculated to evaluate the ability of specific physiologic and injury-related variables (hypotension, tachycardia, shock index, Injury Severity Score (ISS), Glasgow Coma Scale, and mechanism of injury) to discriminate pelvic fracture morphologies for which pelvic binder application would be favorable.ResultsA total of 298 patients were included in the current investigation. Of these patients, applying a pelvic binder was favorable in 17% of cases (95% CI: 13%-22%, N = 50), would be mechanically neutral in 28% of cases (95% CI: 23%-33%, N = 82), and was potentially unfavorable in 56% of cases (95% CI: 50%-61%, N = 166) (P < .001). All investigated variables demonstrated limited discriminatory ability for identifying patients for whom pelvic binder application was favorable, with most AUCs <0.60. The highest predictive performance was observed for the ISS [AUC (95% CI): 0.65 (0.58-0.73)].ConclusionIn trauma patients with CT-confirmed pelvic ring injuries, readily available prehospital variables such as hemodynamic instability, associated injury patterns, and mechanism of injury appear to be insufficient for reliably identifying patients with a fracture morphology that could be amenable to pelvic binder application.

articles.title: Ethnicity is associated with variation in diabetes emergency outcomes: Findings from the DEKODE audit and feedback programme.
articles.journal_full: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Although ethnic disparities in diabetes prevalence and chronic complications are well recognised, their association with acute metabolic emergencies and outcomes is not well established. In this study, we investigated the association between ethnicity and clinical outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective multicentre study included adults (≥16 years) admitted with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state (HHS) and hypoglycaemia between 2020 and 2023 in participating centres of the Digital Evaluation of Ketosis and Other Diabetes Emergencies (DEKODE) surveillance programme. Ethnicity was grouped as White, Asian or Black. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models assessed associations between ethnicity and length of stay (LOS), episode duration and in-hospital mortality, adjusting for demographic, biochemical and clinical covariates.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 6859 episodes were analysed (4257 DKA; 191 HHS; 2411 hypoglycaemia). Across these, differences were observed in age at presentation, metabolic parameters, and LOS across ethnic groups. In DKA, Black and Asian ethnicities were associated with longer LOS than White ethnicity (p < 0.001). Black ethnicity was also associated with prolonged DKA duration (p = 0.006). In the HHS cohort, Asian ethnicity was associated with longer LOS (p = 0.014) but lower in-hospital mortality (p = 0.002). In the hypoglycaemia cohort, Black ethnicity was associated with lower mortality (p = 0.037).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Ethnic variation was observed in the presentation and outcomes of diabetic emergencies. After adjustment for demographic and clinical factors, ethnicity remained associated with several outcomes. These findings support further investigation into social, healthcare and pre-hospital factors that may contribute to observed differences.

articles.title: High Prevalence and Clinical Burden of Bleeding Disorder of Unknown Cause in Adolescents With Heavy Menstrual Bleeding: Application of New Definition by the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis.
articles.journal_full: Haemophilia : the official journal of the World Federation of Hemophilia

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Bleeding disorder of unknown cause (BDUC) is increasingly recognized in patients with clinically significant bleeding despite normal haemostatic testing. The International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH) recently proposed a standardized definition incorporating bleeding phenotype and validated assessment tools.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To determine the prevalence and clinical impact of BDUC in adolescents with heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB) using the ISTH definition for BDUC.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 205 adolescents, 57.6% met criteria for BDUC, including 86.8% of those without an established bleeding disorder using the ISTH paediatric bleeding assessment tool threshold ≥3, most with clinically significant HMB (PBAC >100). Adolescents with BDUC demonstrated similar bleeding severity, with comparable ISTH-BAT and PBAC scores (p = 0.95 and p = 0.62, respectively) as those with diagnosed bleeding disorders. However, BDUC was associated with higher rates of anaemia (50% vs. 31%, p = 0.016) and increased emergency department utilization (47% vs. 30%, p = 0.03), while iron deficiency, hospitalizations, and transfusion requirements were similar between groups. Health-related quality of life was similarly impaired in both groups (PedsQL fatigue scores of 61.1 vs. 59.6, p = 0.65).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: BDUC is highly prevalent among adolescents with HMB and is associated with a clinical burden comparable to, and in some domains exceeding, that of established bleeding disorders. These findings support BDUC as a clinically meaningful phenotype and highlight the need for improved diagnostic precision and targeted management strategies.

articles.title: Outpatient cerebrospinal fluid tap testing with delayed patient and caregiver assessment in suspected normal pressure hydrocephalus.
articles.journal_full: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Delayed responses after cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) removal and changes observed in daily life may be missed by same-day clinic-based testing. We evaluated an outpatient CSF tap-test pathway combining quantitative testing with a 1-week patient and caregiver assessment in older patients with suspected normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively reviewed all 22 consecutive patients who entered the pathway at two hospitals from January 2024 through December 2025. After removal of 30-50 mL of CSF, Timed Up and Go (TUG) and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) assessments were performed when feasible approximately 1 h later and at 1 week. At the 1-week visit, patients and/or accompanying family members were interviewed face to face about changes in daily activities.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: All patients completed testing without admission. Quantitative improvement occurred in 10 patients, clinician-documented improvement in 13, and patient- or caregiver-reported improvement in 13. The integrated clinical response was positive in 18 patients; 5 had improvement reported only by the patient or caregiver. One transient orthostatic headache occurred. No emergency department visit, unplanned hospitalization, or serious tap-test-related adverse event occurred through 1 week. Twelve patients underwent shunt surgery, and 11 had gait improvement at 3 months.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This outpatient pathway was feasible at the participating hospitals. Delayed patient and caregiver assessment identified changes not captured by clinician documentation in some patients and may complement quantitative testing. Prospective studies should use standardized reported-outcome measures and predefined assessment schedules.

articles.title: Early-Phase Computed Tomography Bowel Diameter and Neurological Outcomes Post-Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: We aimed to conduct an exploratory investigation on the association between bowel diameter on early-phase abdominal computed tomography (CT) and neurological outcomes in patients undergoing extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This observational study included patients who underwent ECPR for OHCA and abdominal CT before intensive care unit admission between January 2015 and December 2021 at a tertiary emergency medical center. Maximum bowel diameter was measured with a picture archiving and communication system by an investigator blinded to outcomes. The primary endpoint was unfavorable neurological outcomes at 1 month, defined as Cerebral Performance Category 3-5. The discriminatory ability of bowel diameter was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Data from 181 patients were analyzed (median age, 57 years; 84.5% male). Bowel diameter demonstrated a weak ability to predict unfavorable neurological outcomes, with an AUC of 0.58 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.47-0.70). However, higher discriminatory performance was observed in subgroups of patients aged ≥ 65 years (AUC, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.69-0.96) and those with initial nonshockable rhythms (AUC, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.47-0.91).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The results of this exploratory investigation suggest that bowel diameter may represent a potential adjunctive marker associated with functional outcomes post-ECPR for OHCA.

articles.title: Wearable Technologies and Artificial Intelligence in Sports Medicine: A Systematic Narrative Review of Injury Prevention and Rehabilitation.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND AIMS
abstract.text: Wearable technologies and artificial intelligence (AI) are shifting sports medicine from episodic, subjective assessment toward continuous, data-driven injury surveillance. This review aimed to map the main wearable sensor modalities used in injury prevention and rehabilitation, evaluate AI architectures applied to biomechanical and physiological data, summarize clinically relevant applications by anatomical region, and identify methodological, ethical, and implementation challenges.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A systematic narrative review was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for studies published from 2016 to 2026, supplemented by manual reference screening. Search terms combined wearable sensors, AI and machine learning, and sports medicine outcomes. After title and abstract screening of 614 records and full-text assessment of 87 articles, 28 studies met the inclusion criteria.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Inertial measurement units, GPS/GNSS, surface electromyography, and photoplethysmography were the most frequently reported sensor modalities. Deep learning, ensemble methods, and multimodal fusion were commonly used to process biomechanical and physiological signals. One hybrid IMU-sEMG study involving 50 athletes reported 92.3% accuracy, 90.5% recall, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.93 for classifying biomechanical injury-risk states. An ankle-monitoring study using data from 87 athletes across 12 sports reported 87.4% overall detection accuracy, a 12.1% false-alarm rate, and 17.2 ms latency. However, substantial heterogeneity in study design, populations, outcomes, and validation methods prevented direct comparison or pooled quantitative interpretation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Wearable-AI systems show promising potential for injury-risk monitoring, rehabilitation, and return-to-play support. Wider clinical adoption will require more diverse populations, longitudinal and field-based validation, improved model interpretability, standardized protocols, and robust ethical, legal, and governance frameworks.

articles.title: Association Between Injury Mechanisms, Hospital Admission, and Length of Stay Among Trauma Patients Aged ≥14 Years in an Adult Emergency Department in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Trauma presentations to emergency departments (EDs) encompass a wide range of injury mechanisms and clinical outcomes. Mechanisms of injury may influence both hospital admission and length of stay (LOS). This study examined the association between injury mechanisms and hospital admission as the primary outcome and evaluated LOS as a secondary and exploratory outcome among trauma patients presenting to the ED in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at King Khalid University Hospital, including patients aged 14 years and older who presented with traumatic injuries between January 2019 and April 2025. Hospital admission following the initial ED evaluation was the primary outcome, while LOS among admitted patients was considered a secondary and exploratory outcome. From a database of 10,722 trauma-related records available for screening, patients were randomly selected and assessed against predefined eligibility criteria, with ineligible records replaced by additional randomly selected records until a final sample of 218 eligible ED encounters was obtained. Data were extracted from electronic medical records and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. A pre-specified multivariable logistic regression model was used to assess factors associated with hospital admission.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 218 patients were included, with a median age of 29.5 years (IQR 22-39); 66.5% were male. Falls were the most frequently documented injury mechanism (49.1%), followed by traffic-related incidents (22.0%). Overall, 32 patients (14.7%) required hospital admission. Among the 30 admitted patients included in the LOS analysis, the median LOS was 5 days (IQR 2-14). Traffic-related injury was associated with higher odds of hospital admission after adjustment for age, sex, and any comorbidity (adjusted OR 3.41, 95% CI 1.49-7.83; p=0.004), whereas age, sex, and the presence of any comorbidity were not significantly associated with admission. Poisoning was associated with longer LOS (median 15 vs 4 days; p=0.042), although this finding was based on only three admitted patients with poisoning.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Falls were the most frequently documented injury mechanism in this single-center ED cohort, whereas traffic-related injuries were independently associated with higher odds of hospital admission. Poisoning was associated with longer LOS, although this finding was based on a small number of cases and should be interpreted cautiously. These findings highlight the distinction between injury mechanisms contributing to ED presentation volume and those associated with greater inpatient utilization.

articles.title: Traumatic brain injury mechanism of injury in adults: analysis by injury severity and sex in the National Trauma Databank.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Traumatic brain injuries (TBIs) are a global health issue, causing significant morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Despite their prevalence, research gaps remain, particularly regarding adults aged 18-64, sex disparities, mechanisms of injury (MOI), and moderate TBI severity.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This cross-sectional study analyzed data from the National Trauma Data Bank (NTDB), comprising 747 trauma-designated hospitals (N = 299,856). The study examined sociodemographic characteristics associated with TBI severity overall and by sex, and tested for effect modification between TBI severity and MOI by sex. Multinomial logistic regression was used to assess associations between MOI and TBI severity, adjusting for covariates.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Significant effect modification was found between TBI severity and MOI by sex. Transportation-related TBIs were the most common MOI across all severities and sexes, emphasizing the need for targeted prevention strategies. Disparities were identified, with fewer severe TBI cases treated at level I trauma centers and larger hospitals, indicating barriers to optimal care. Females exhibited higher TBI severity compared to males.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The study highlights the significant burden of transportation-related TBIs and sex disparities in injury outcomes, particularly the higher severity among females. These findings call for sex-specific prevention strategies and further research into post-injury outcomes and healthcare access for severe TBI cases.

articles.title: Designing a hybrid surgical ICU to avoid intrahospital transport in selected critically Ill patients: the CUHK-SZ institutional concept.
articles.journal_full: World journal of emergency surgery : WJES

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Intrahospital transport for surgery exposes critically ill patients to equipment failure, displacement of tubes and lines, interrupted monitoring, and physiologic instability. Although transport protocols can reduce these hazards, they do not address the underlying physical decoupling of surgical infrastructure from the critical care environment.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This institutional perspective describes the rationale and design of a hybrid surgical ICU planned for the Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen (CUHK-SZ) Medical Center: a dedicated clinical space designed to function as both a critical care unit and a procedural suite, bringing surgery to the patient rather than transporting the patient to the operating room (OR). The model is presented as an illustrative, hypothesis-generating concept rather than a validated clinical pathway.

abstract.label: DESIGN CONCEPT
abstract.text: The design concept, which is a patient-centered approach, should guide healthcare delivery in modern medicine by placing the patient at the forefront of all decisions and mobilizing all available resources to serve them. This approach addresses all three domains: personnel, environment, and equipment. Overlapping anesthesiology and critical care competencies support integrated staffing. Connectable ICU rooms, adequate space and electrical capacity, anterooms, and switchable HEPA-filtered positive-pressure ventilation meet environmental requirements. Total intravenous anesthesia, portable surgical platforms, and minimally invasive or robotic techniques reduce dependence on fixed OR infrastructure. At CUHK-SZ, the concept is planned as a prototype in the trauma building using two adjacent ICU rooms with an openable partition and switchable ventilation. Candidate patient groups, procedural levels, and implementation requirements are presented as provisional, expert-derived proposals, and engineering testing and simulated drills are planned before any clinical use.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The hybrid surgical ICU is a technically plausible option for carefully selected patients at high risk from transport, but its clinical effectiveness, safety, and cost-effectiveness remain unproven. The CUHK-SZ concept is intended to generate hypotheses for prospective evaluation, and its transferability to existing hospitals is likely to depend on incremental adaptation rather than direct replication.

articles.title: Apixaban vs rivaroxaban for venous thromboembolism: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract.text: Direct oral anticoagulants are first-line therapy for venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet comparative evidence between apixaban and rivaroxaban remains limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of apixaban versus rivaroxaban in patients with VTE. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library was conducted from inception through March 2026. Studies directly comparing apixaban and rivaroxaban in adult VTE patients were included. Outcomes, including recurrent VTE, major bleeding, all-cause mortality, and net clinical harm, were pooled using a random-effects model. Thirteen studies comprising more than 220,000 patients were included. Apixaban was associated with a significantly lower risk of recurrent VTE compared to rivaroxaban (RR 0.85; 95% CI 0.74-0.98), with moderate heterogeneity. Apixaban was also associated with a significant 28% reduction in major bleeding risk (RR 0.72; 95% CI 0.65-0.81), with low heterogeneity, indicating consistent findings across studies. When efficacy and safety outcomes were combined, apixaban demonstrated a significantly lower risk of net clinical harm (RR 0.76; 95% CI 0.68-0.86). In contrast, no statistically significant difference was observed in all-cause mortality (RR 0.95; 95% CI 0.80-1.12), with substantial heterogeneity across studies. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these findings, with no single study significantly altering the overall estimates. Overall, apixaban demonstrated a more favorable efficacy and safety profile compared with rivaroxaban in VTE management, with reduced recurrence and bleeding risk, while mortality remained comparable. These findings suggest that apixaban may be associated with a more favorable efficacy and safety profile than rivaroxaban; however, the results should be interpreted cautiously given the predominance of observational evidence.

articles.title: Community-based monitoring of neonatal jaundice using the point-of-care Bilistick® System 2.0.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Neonatal jaundice often peaks after discharge, creating the need for reliable post-discharge monitoring. This study evaluated the feasibility and safety of a hospital-to-community pathway using the Bilistick® System 2.0 within routine Community Health Family Services (CHFS).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective observational study was conducted within a Local Health Authority in northeastern Italy. Newborns eligible for out-of-hospital bilirubin testing according to a Diagnostic-Therapeutic Assistance Pathway (DTAP) were referred either to CHFS or to hospital follow-up based on bilirubin risk profile, clinical factors, and organizational considerations.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 397 eligible newborns meeting inclusion criteria, 244 were included. Of these, 108 (44.3%) were referred to CHFS, 135 (55.3%) to hospital follow-up, and 1 was lost to follow-up. Among newborns referred to CHFS, 97 (89.8%) completed monitoring without hospital referral. Eleven were referred to the hospital, of whom 7 received phototherapy. Among newborns referred directly to the hospital, 6 (4.4%) required phototherapy. No sampling-related adverse events, missed phototherapy, exchange transfusions, or cases of kernicterus were recorded.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Community-based bilirubin monitoring using the Bilistick® System 2.0 appears feasible and safe for selected low-risk newborns within a structured hospital-to-community pathway.

abstract.label: IMPACT
abstract.text: To our knowledge, this is the first real-world evaluation of a structured hospital-to-community pathway integrating point-of-care bilirubin testing into routine community care within UNICEF's Baby-Friendly Initiative framework. Among selected newborns referred to community services, 89.8% completed bilirubin monitoring without hospital referral. Community midwives identified infants requiring escalation of care; no missed phototherapy, exchange transfusion, or kernicterus occurred. The model may reduce unnecessary hospital reassessment and disruption to the mother-infant dyad; local administrative estimates indicate a direct cost difference of €32.30 per bilirubin reassessment.

articles.title: Comparative health outcomes of buprenorphine versus methadone treatment for opioid use disorder: a retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study in the global federated electronic health record network.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To compare the therapeutic profiles of buprenorphine and methadone medication-assisted treatment (MAT) for opioid use disorder (OUD).

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort study with 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) using Cox proportional hazards models.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: Global real-world electronic health record data from the TriNetX federated network.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: Adults (≥18 years) with a diagnosis of OUD and a prescription for either buprenorphine or methadone for OUD between 1 July 2021 and 1 July 2024.

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract.text: The index event was the first exposure to either buprenorphine or methadone.

abstract.label: PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES
abstract.text: Incident metabolic and cardiovascular complications, serious infections, healthcare utilisation and indices of addiction and mental health.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: After PSM, 52 410 individuals remained in each cohort (mean age 46.2 years; 44% female). Most individuals were white (69%), with substantial black and Hispanic representation. Compared with methadone, buprenorphine was associated with lower risks of type 2 diabetes (HR 0.87; 95% CI 0.79 to 0.96), metabolic syndrome (HR 0.64; 95% CI 0.49 to 0.83), ischaemic strokes (HR 0.91; 95% CI 0.84 to 0.99), sepsis (HR 0.74; 95% CI 0.69 to 0.78), hospitalisations or emergency department visits (HR 0.78; 95% CI 0.77 to 0.80), opioid-related overdoses (HR 0.73; 95% CI 0.69 to 0.77), and a higher rate of OUD remission (HR 1.76; 95% CI 1.69 to 1.83). Buprenorphine was associated with higher risks of alcohol use disorder (HR 1.14; 95% CI 1.09 to 1.19), cannabis use disorder (HR 1.26; 95% CI 1.16 to 1.36), major depression (HR 1.06; 95% CI 1.04 to 1.09) and anxiety disorders (HR 1.07; 95% CI 1.05 to 1.10). Fewer patients initially on buprenorphine treatment switched to methadone during the study period (2049 (3.9%) events) than patients initially on methadone switched to buprenorphine (2806 (5.4%) events). No significant differences were observed for obesity, myocardial infarction, hypertension, tobacco use disorder or suicidality.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Buprenorphine and methadone were associated with distinct physical, addiction-related and mental health profiles. These associative rather than causal findings underscore the importance of individualised treatment planning and careful monitoring of patients undergoing MAT with buprenorphine and methadone.

articles.title: Early post-ROSC laboratory phenotypes and clinical outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a 10-year national cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Prior phenotyping in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) relied predominantly on prehospital indicators, which neither describe nor grade the underlying ischemia-reperfusion injury. We aimed to derive laboratory-based phenotypes and describe their clinical characteristics and outcome associations.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adult resuscitated OHCA patients of presumed cardiac etiology between 01/02/2011 and 01/01/2022, linking Singapore's national OHCA and cardiovascular databases. Unsupervised latent class analysis (LCA) was applied to 14 laboratory variables within six hours post-return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). Stability was confirmed through split-sample validation. Logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards model, adjusted for age, sex and initial cardiac rhythm, assessed poor neurological recovery at hospital discharge, 30-day and 3-year mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1514 eligible patients (median age 65.0 years, 73.6% males), LCA identified three distinct phenotypes: multi-organ dysfunction (MOD, N = 286), homeostatic (HOM, N = 967), and immune-dysregulated (IMD, N = 261), independently reproduced in derivation (entropy = 0.817) and replication (entropy = 0.892) subsamples. The most discriminative variables were creatinine, eosinophil and lymphocyte. Compared to MOD, both HOM (aOR: 0.50, 95% CI 0.30-0.78, p = 0.004) and IMD (aOR: 0.46, 95% CI 0.26-0.78, p = 0.005) phenotypes had significantly lower odds of poor neurological recovery. This pattern was consistent for 30-day mortality (HOM aHR: 0.71, 95% CI 0.61-0.83; IMD aHR: 0.78, 95% CI 0.64-0.94) and 3-year mortality (HOM aHR: 0.70, 95% CI 0.60-0.82; IMD aHR: 0.74, 95% CI 0.62-0.90), all p ≤ 0.01.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Early post-ROSC laboratory data identified three prognostically distinct phenotypes among resuscitated OHCA patients. These exploratory findings support external validation and investigation of phenotype-guided therapies.

articles.title: The epidemiology of paediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in Australia and New Zealand: a report from the Australasian resuscitation outcomes Consortium Epistry (Aus-ROC).

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: This first epidemiological study of paediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (pOHCA) across Australia and New Zealand explores the incidence, patient and event characteristics, both overall and by developmental age groups, and examines factors associated with outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: All pOHCAs (aged <18 years) attended by emergency medical services (EMS) in Australia and New Zealand from 2017 to 2023 were included. Crude incidence rates (per 100,000 person-years) were calculated for EMS-attended and EMS-treated cases. Logistic regression models were used to identify associations between patient and arrest characteristics and survival (event and 30-day/hospital discharge).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: EMS attended 4779 cases and treated 3139 (65.7%). Incidence rates for EMS-attended and EMS-treated cases were 10.1 and 6.6, respectively; with a bimodal age distribution peaking in infants (65.4) and adolescents (11.4). Most EMS-attended cases were unwitnessed (66.9%), of medical origin (60.1%), had initial non-shockable rhythms (91.1%), occurred in private residences (74.3%), and received bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (62.7%). Few (1.6%) received bystander defibrillation. Arrest characteristics varied widely between age groups. Survival to 30-days/hospital discharge in EMS-treated cases was 10.0% (highest in late childhood [15.4%] and lowest in infants [7.9%]). Multivariable analysis identified that increasing age was positively associated with event survival, whilst bystander-witnessed arrest, initial shockable rhythm, arrest aetiology, and EMS response time were significant predictors of short and long-term survival.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The incidence, patient characteristics, and survival outcomes of pOHCA in our region differ significantly by age groups. Age- and context-specific prevention and resuscitation strategies are essential for reducing the burden and improving survival outcomes.

articles.title: Opioid-associated vs undifferentiated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: examining differences in outcomes and the relationship with Utstein variables.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The pathophysiology of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) due to opioid toxicity is different from other OHCAs. Our aims were to determine: (1) whether opioid-toxicity is associated with OHCA outcomes; and, (2) whether the relationship between Utstein variables and outcomes differ between those with opioid-associated (OA) and other OHCA.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analysed adult emergency medical services (EMS)-treated OHCAs from the British Columbia Cardiac Arrest Registry. Using post-mortem toxicological investigations, death certificates, and hospital-based diagnoses, we classified as OA-OHCA or "undifferentiated OHCA". We fit a multivariable logistic regression model to assess the association between OA-OHCA (versus undifferentiated OHCA) and favourable neurological outcome at hospital discharge. We then added pre-specified interaction terms to individual models for: sex, initial cardiac rhythm, bystander CPR, witnessed arrest, and location type.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 10,786 OHCAs: 1349 (13%) were OA-OHCA, of whom 331 (25%) were female, and the median age was 40 years (IQR 31-50); 9437 (87%) were undifferentiated, of whom 2910 (31%) were female, and the median age was 70 years (IQR 58-81). We did not detect an association between OA-OHCA (OR 1.02, 95% CI 0.77, 1.35) and survival with favourable neurological outcomes. Models adding interaction terms demonstrated statistically significant interactions for: sex (p = 0.032), initial cardiac rhythm (p = 0.024), and bystander-witnessed status (p ≤ 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Overall, we did not detect an association between opioid toxicity and outcomes. In models with interaction terms, the relationship between Utstein and outcomes differed between opioid-associated and other OHCAs, highlighting the impact opioid-associated cases may have in observational OHCA analyses.

articles.title: Cytochrome P450 1A protects against hyperbaric oxygen-induced lung injury by regulating neutrophil extracellular trap formation.
