abstract.text: Although hyperbaric oxygen (HBO) therapy is a clinically established intervention for various pathological conditions, excessive oxygen exposure can induce acute lung injury (ALI), the underlying mechanisms of which remain elusive. In this study, we demonstrate that neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) contribute to the pathogenesis of HBO-induced ALI. HBO exposure upregulates pulmonary expression of CYP1A1 and CYP1A2, two isoforms of the cytochrome P450 (CYP) 1A subfamily. Genetic deletion of both CYP1A1 and CYP1A2 exacerbates, whereas the CYP1A inducer attenuates NET formation and ALI in HBO-exposed mice. Mechanistically, HBO-induced upregulation of CYP1A protects against lung injury by suppressing oxidative stress-driven NET formation via an NRF2(nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2)-dependent pathway. Notably, the inhibitory effect of the CYP1A/NRF2 signaling axis on NET formation is mediated indirectly through its antioxidant actions in alveolar epithelial cells, rather than via direct modulation of neutrophils, thereby establishing an antioxidative microenvironment that limits NET formation. Our findings reveal a novel protective mechanism whereby activation of the CYP1A/NRF2 pathway mitigates HBO-induced lung injury through regulation of intercellular crosstalk between alveolar epithelial cells and neutrophils within the oxidative milieu.

articles.title: Screening for suspected child physical abuse in a Colombian pediatric emergency department: Clinical characteristics and performance of SPUTOVAMO-R.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Physical abuse causes morbidity and mortality in young children, yet Latin American emergency data are scarce.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To describe characteristics associated with a multidisciplinary child-protection panel's classification and estimate SPUTOVAMO-R sensitivity relative to ICD-10 coding and panel classification.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING
abstract.text: Children aged 1 month-18 years with emergency department records at a pediatric referral hospital in Bogotá, Colombia (2015-2017), coded with physical-abuse ICD-10 diagnoses.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective cross-sectional study. High- and low-probability classifications were compared using Fisher's exact test and odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 322 coded children, 59 (18.3%) were classified as high probability. An internally inconsistent account (OR 34.7, 95% CI 12.0-124.0), history inconsistent with injury (OR 18.0, 8.3-40.7), and disclosure by the child (OR 56.1, 12.7-516.7) were strongly associated with high-probability classification. Absence of an adult witness was not associated among children aged 0-4 years and was associated with low-probability classification in older children (OR 0.08, 0.00-0.58). All four high-probability children with high-specificity fractures, and none of three low-probability children, had a history inconsistent with injury. SPUTOVAMO-R sensitivity was 34.2% (110/322; 95% CI 29.0-39.6) relative to ICD-10 coding and 91.5% (54/59; 81.3-97.2) relative to the panel.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: ICD-10 abuse coding corresponded poorly with panel classification. Panel classification was most strongly associated with history coherence. SPUTOVAMO-R was negative in two-thirds of coded children and should be evaluated in unselected populations.

articles.title: Ultrasound-based multimodal diagnosis and endovascular therapy for phlegmasia cerulea dolens secondary to May-Thurner syndrome in a middle-aged male patient: A case report.

abstract.label: RATIONALE
abstract.text: This study explores the value of ultrasound in the diagnosis of patients with phlegmasia cerulea dolens (PCD). The enrolled patient suffered from PCD secondary to iliac vein compression syndrome (IVCS) and complicated by extensive lower-limb deep vein thrombosis (DVT). We analyzed an atypical case in a middle-aged male. We summarized the advantages and limitations of ultrasound. We aimed to provide practical references for multimodal diagnosis and emergency management of critical DVT patients.

abstract.label: PATIENT CONCERNS
abstract.text: A 54-year-old male patient was diagnosed with IVCS. The condition was complicated by extensive left lower-limb DVT and subsequent PCD. We retrospectively collected his clinical data, imaging findings, and interventional records. We summarized the typical ultrasound features. We combined computed tomography angiography (CTA) and venography results. We further clarified the clinical role of ultrasound in such life-threatening vascular emergencies.

abstract.label: DIAGNOSES
abstract.text: Based on clinical manifestations and multimodal imaging examinations, the final diagnoses were phlegmasia cerulea dolens (PCD) secondary to iliac vein compression syndrome (IVCS), complicated by extensive left lower-limb deep vein thrombosis.

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract.text: The patient received emergency endovascular interventional therapy, including thrombus aspiration, catheter-directed thrombolysis, and iliac vein stent implantation. Anticoagulant therapy was administered perioperatively. Serial ultrasound examinations were performed before and after intervention to dynamically evaluate venous hemodynamics.

abstract.label: OUTCOMES
abstract.text: Ultrasound rapidly detected extensive thrombosis in the left femoral vein, popliteal vein, and calf intermuscular veins. It clearly displayed thrombus location, scope, and echogenic features. It provided critical imaging evidence for emergency intervention. However, ultrasound could not directly visualize iliac vein stenosis. Pelvic anatomical depth and intraluminal thrombus obstruction mainly accounted for this limitation. CTA and venography successfully confirmed the underlying IVCS etiology. Postoperative ultrasound hemodynamic parameters objectively evaluated vascular recanalization efficacy. Combined interventional treatment effectively restored limb blood flow. Lower-limb edema and pain were significantly relieved after treatment.

abstract.label: LESSONS
abstract.text: Ultrasound serves as the first‑line screening tool for PCD. It allows rapid and real‑time evaluation of thrombus burden in the emergency department. Routine postoperative hemodynamic ultrasound can objectively assess vascular recanalization for therapeutic monitoring. However, ultrasound carries a high risk of missed diagnosis of primary iliac vein stenosis. For highly suspected IVCS cases, CTA and venography are essential for etiological confirmation. A multimodal collaborative diagnosis and treatment strategy is strongly recommended for critical PCD patients.

articles.title: ST elevation in lead aVR - a marker of critical left main coronary artery stenosis: A series of case reports and literature review.

abstract.label: RATIONALE
abstract.text: Lead augmented vector right (aVR) has historically been overlooked in acute coronary syndromes. ST-segment elevation (STE) in lead aVR with diffuse ST depression in multiple leads has emerged as a critical marker for left main coronary artery (LMCA) stenosis and triple-vessel disease (3VD). Recognition of this high-risk electrocardiogram (ECG) pattern is essential for timely diagnosis and improved outcomes.

abstract.label: PATIENT CONCERNS
abstract.text: In this retrospective case series, 5 consecutive patients presented to the emergency department between January 2023 and June 2024 with acute chest pain or cardiac arrest.

abstract.label: DIAGNOSES
abstract.text: All 5 patients exhibited ECG findings of STE in aVR (≥1 mm) with diffuse ST depressions (≥1 mm) in ≥6 leads. All underwent coronary angiography within 24 hours, which confirmed LMCA stenosis (70%-99%; mean STE in aVR: 3.0 mm). A narrative literature review was performed using PubMed/MEDLINE databases (2000-2024) with search terms including "lead aVR," "ST-segment elevation," "left main coronary artery," and "acute coronary syndrome." Literature review shows that STE ≥0.5 mm in aVR with diffuse ST depression has been reported to have a sensitivity of 78% and specificity of 86% for LMCA/triple-vessel disease in prior studies. However, it is important to recognize that this ECG pattern can occur in other conditions, including severe anemia, shock states, and aortic dissection. STE ≥1 mm increases diagnostic yield. Patients with this pattern have higher in-hospital mortality (8.6%-19.4% vs 1.3%) and increased heart failure and reinfarction.

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract.text: A total of 2 patients underwent coronary artery bypass grafting, 2 underwent percutaneous coronary intervention, and 1 was managed medically.

abstract.label: OUTCOMES
abstract.text: No in-hospital deaths occurred.

abstract.label: LESSONS
abstract.text: STE in aVR with diffuse ST depression represents a high-risk ECG pattern that should prompt urgent invasive evaluation. Recognition of this high-risk ECG pattern is essential for timely diagnosis of critical LMCA stenosis and improved outcomes. However, findings from this small case series require validation in larger prospective cohorts.

articles.title: Analysis of the spectrum of critical illnesses in the emergency department of Hebei Children's Hospital: A single-center study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To analyze the distribution and epidemiological characteristics of critical illnesses in the emergency department of Hebei Children's Hospital.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: Through retrospective medical record review, patients triaged as level Ⅰ or Ⅱ (aged 0-18 years) who visited the emergency department of the hospital from January 2023 to December 2024 were included. The distribution of diseases, age, gender, season and other indicators were statistically analyzed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1,450 critically ill patients with triage levels Ⅰ and Ⅱ were included. The median (IQR) age of all patients was 4.00 (1.00, 9.00) years, and the male-to-female ratio was 1.2:1. Among each age group, the 1 to <3 years group had a proportion of 27.9%, and the 0 to <1 year group had a proportion of 9.5%, representing the highest and lowest values, respectively. The distribution of critical illnesses in the emergency department of this hospital was led by the nervous system (n = 548, 37.8%), trauma and accidental injuries (n = 286, 19.7%), and the respiratory system (n = 214, 14.8%), which ranked as the top three categories. The top five primary diagnosed diseases were seizure (n = 352, 24.3%), drug poisoning (n = 242, 16.7%), severe pneumonia (n = 137, 9.5%), status epileptics (n = 137, 9.5%), and arrhythmia (n = 102, 7.0%). Among them, the proportion of severe pneumonia was the highest in the 0 to <1 year group; the proportion of seizure was the highest in the 1 to <3 years group, 3 to <6 years group and 6 to <12 years group, while the proportion of drug poisoning was the highest in the 12 to <18 years group. The distribution of the top five disease differed significantly across age groups (p < 0.001) and seasons (p = 0.004). Cardiopulmonary arrest (CPA) is one of the most critical conditions in an emergency department. However, the distribution of diseases causing CPA did not show significant differences by age or season. The top three diseases causing CPA are severe pneumonia, asphyxia, and multiple body region injuries (Road traffic accident).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The spectrum of critical illnesses varied significantly by age and seasonal distribution in the emergency department of Hebei Children's Hospital. Therefore, age and season-tailored approaches are recommended for managing common critical illnesses, whereas CPA requires a standardized, universally applied emergency response. It is necessary to further strengthen training and optimize resource allocation.

articles.title: Enhancing Culturally Sensitive Care for Critically Ill Native American Patients and Families: An Educational Initiative and Resource Guide for Nursing and Medical Teams.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of hospice & palliative care

abstract.text: BackgroundNative American (NA) patients experience persistent inequities in advance care planning (ACP) and often present to tertiary centers with critical illness; culturally respectful serious-illness communication is therefore essential in emergency and intensive care settings.InterventionWe developed and implemented a nursing-led, multidisciplinary educational initiative at a large academic medical center serving patients from >50 tribal nations. Informed by a literature review, local practice needs, and expert input from a Native American Patient Experience Ambassador, we created (1) an "Honoring Your Choices" (HYC) communication card with culturally sensitive prompts for serious illness conversations and (2) a quick reference guide (QRG) outlining key cultural considerations and unit-specific resources. Tools were disseminated to seven intensive care units and the emergency department through nurse leader engagement, unit rounding, and staff education, and the initiative was presented at departmental Grand Rounds/didactics with pre/post surveys to assess impact.ResultsTwenty-seven pre-session and twenty-four post-session surveys were collected from clinicians and trainees. Prior to the session, >80% of respondents reported being not or only slightly confident discussing end-of-life issues with NA patients/families; post-session surveys demonstrated increased self-reported confidence in recognizing when cultural beliefs may influence care and in conducting end-of-life discussions.ConclusionsThis initiative demonstrates how culturally congruent approaches to serious illness conversations may support more meaningful engagement with NA patients and families. Our experience suggests that developing and evaluating a brief, point-of-care communication tool like Honoring Your Choices may be accomplished with existing interdisciplinary partnerships, offering a practical model that other institutions can readily mirror.

articles.title: Gut Microbiota and Its Metabolites in the Prognosis of Coronary Heart Disease: A Systematic Review and Mechanistic Insights.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Emerging evidence links gut microbiota dysbiosis and its metabolites to atherosclerosis. This systematic review aims to synthesize prospective evidence on the association of gut microbiota and its metabolites with prognosis in coronary heart disease (CHD) patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library was conducted from inception to January 21, 2026. Prospective cohort studies, nested case-control studies, or prospective case-control studies reporting associations between gut microbiota features or metabolite levels and major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE, including all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, unstable angina, heart failure, and all-cause unplanned hospitalization/emergency department visits) in CHD patients were included.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eighteen studies were included. Higher Lactobacillus abundance was associated with favorable prognosis, whereas a 10-species microbial risk score (MRS) predicted increased MACCE risk. For microbial metabolites, elevated trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) showed a consistent concentration-response association with increased MACCE risk. Phenylacetylglutamine (PAGln) and imidazole propionate (ImP) independently predicted poor outcomes in STEMI patients. Indole-3-propionic acid (IPA) was associated with reduced mortality, whereas deoxycholic acid (DCA) was associated with increased risk, while indoxyl sulfate (IS), acylcarnitines, and choline predicted worse outcomes. Mechanistically, these metabolites modulate inflammation, lipid metabolism, endothelial function, and platelet activation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Gut microbial features, particularly Lactobacillus abundance, are associated with favorable prognosis, whereas specific microbial risk patterns predict increased risk. Metabolites TMAO, PAGln, and ImP are linked to poor outcomes, while IPA may confer protection and DCA is associated with increased risk. These findings not only provide new insights into the pathogenesis of coronary heart disease but also identify potential therapeutic targets for microbiota-based interventions.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance and timeliness of ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy for peripheral lymphadenopathy in Internal Medicine: a multicenter real-world study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy (CNB) is increasingly used for evaluating peripheral lymphadenopathy, but evidence regarding its implementation in Internal Medicine remains limited. We assessed its diagnostic performance, safety, and diagnostic timeliness in routine clinical practice.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective multicenter study included consecutive patients undergoing ultrasound-guided CNB of peripheral lymphadenopathy in five Internal Medicine departments between February 2021 and March 2026. The primary outcome was diagnostic performance. Secondary outcomes included safety, diagnostic timeliness, performance in lymphoma patients, and factors associated with obtaining a definitive diagnosis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 413 patients were included (median age 62 years; 41.3% women). Lymphoma and carcinoma accounted for 44.1% and 23.7% of final diagnoses, respectively. The first CNB provided a definitive diagnosis in 85.7% of patients and a suggestive diagnosis in 8.0%, yielding an overall diagnostic yield of 93.7%. No major complications occurred. Median time from biopsy request to procedure was 1 day (IQR 0-2), and median time to definitive diagnosis was 10 days (IQR 6-16). Surgical biopsy was required in 9.4% of patients and was associated with longer diagnostic delays (42 vs 9 days; p < 0.001). Among 182 patients with lymphoma, overall diagnostic yield was 93.4%. Lower operator experience and hospital size < 500 beds were independently associated with a lower likelihood of obtaining a definitive diagnosis.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Ultrasound-guided CNB of peripheral lymphadenopathy performed by internists demonstrated high diagnostic yield, excellent safety, and short diagnostic timelines in a large multicenter real-world cohort. Operator experience and institutional context may influence diagnostic performance.

articles.title: Immunonutritional status and survival after cardiac arrest: prognostic value of the prognostic nutritional index, the cholesterol-modified prognostic nutritional index, and the controlling nutritional status score in post-cardiopulmonary resuscitation intensive care patients.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Patients achieving return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) after cardiac arrest experience marked systemic inflammation, metabolic stress, and nutritional impairment, all of which contribute to high mortality. Practical prognostic indices reflecting immunonutritional status may facilitate early risk stratification in this population.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To evaluate the prognostic value of immunonutritional indices for predicting mortality in patients with ROSC after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center, retrospective cohort study included adult patients admitted to the intensive care unit after ROSC following out-of-hospital cardiac arrest between January 2015 and January 2025. Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI), cholesterol-modified Prognostic Nutritional Index (CPNI), and Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) scores were calculated from laboratory parameters obtained within the first 24 h of ICU admission. Patients were classified as survivors or non-survivors based on ICU outcome. Associations with mortality were evaluated using univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses, and discriminatory performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 444 post-ROSC patients, non-survivors had lower PNI (43.66 ± 15.47 vs. 55.06 ± 17.21) and higher CPNI (81.10 ± 13.70 vs. 66.90 ± 18.25) and CONUT scores (4.27 ± 3.04 vs. 2.43 ± 2.43; all p < 0.001). In separate stepwise multivariable models, PNI (aOR 0.64 per 10-point increase), CPNI (aOR 1.25 per 10-point increase), and CONUT (aOR 1.24 per 1-point increase) remained independently associated with mortality. AUCs were 0.689, 0.631, and 0.681, respectively; PNI showed the highest sensitivity (86.3%) at a cut-off of ≤ 59.90.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: PNI, CPNI, and CONUT were significantly associated with ICU mortality after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. These indices may reflect systemic inflammation, immune dysfunction, metabolic stress, and nutritional reserve rather than nutritional status alone. Their availability from routine laboratory parameters may support early risk stratification. Further prospective studies are needed to confirm their prognostic value and clinical applicability.

articles.title: Comparison of HACOR score and ROX index for predicting noninvasive ventilation failure in acute hypoxemic respiratory failure: a prospective study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF) is commonly managed with noninvasive ventilation (NIV) in the emergency department (ED), but delayed identification of NIV failure worsens outcomes. We compared the HACOR (Heart rate, Acidosis, Consciousness, Oxygenation, and Respiratory rate) score and the ROX (Respiratory rate-OXygenation) index for predicting NIV failure in ED patients with AHRF.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective observational study enrolled adult patients with AHRF receiving NIV in the ED between December 2024 and December 2025. HACOR and ROX were calculated at baseline and 1 h post-NIV; score changes (ΔHACOR, ΔROX) were also assessed. The primary outcome was NIV failure requiring intubation within 24 h. Predictive performance was evaluated via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and DeLong comparisons.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 127 patients, 66 (52.0%) failed NIV. Non-survivors/failures had significantly worse scores at both timepoints. The 1-hour HACOR showed the highest discriminative ability (AUC 0.878, 95% CI 0.808-0.930), outperforming baseline HACOR, all ROX parameters, and ΔROX (all p ≤ 0.05). A cut-off > 5 yielded 96.7% sensitivity and a negative likelihood ratio of 0.05.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In ED patients with AHRF treated with NIV, the 1-hour HACOR score was superior to all ROX-based metrics for predicting NIV failure. Early HACOR reassessment may enable timely escalation of respiratory support and improve clinical decision-making.

articles.title: The mental health sequelae of mass shootings on affected children, adolescents and young adults - a scoping review.

abstract.text: While the incidence of school shootings is highest in the US worldwide, these events also occur in Europe, such as the recent fatal school shooting in Graz in Austria, highlighting the importance of evidence-based care for the survivors. This study aims to synthesize existing evidence on the short- and long-term effects of mass shootings on the mental health of children, adolescents, and young adults, and to identify risk factors that predispose individuals to psychological sequelae to inform appropriate aftercare recommendations. After conducting a literature search in PubMed, Medline, Scopus and the Cochrane Library, 483 references were identified, which were screened by two independent raters according to inclusion criteria, resulting in 15 eligible studies. Most shootings examined took place in the US, with some focusing on shootings in Finland. All studies examined either adolescents or young adults. No studies examining the effects on children were found. The results showed that directly after such an event, a large proportion of the affected show posttraumatic stress symptomatology (PTSS); in the long-term most recuperate without intervention, however a small percentage remain symptomatic and later develop PTSD. Key risk factors include female sex, younger age, previous traumatic experiences, an avoidant attachment style and a higher grade of exposure. Social support is an important protective factor. Based on the findings, a multitiered approach tailored to the needs of affected individuals is recommended, supported by a coordinated screening process to identify those with relevant risk factors.

articles.title: Renal trauma in a pediatric Level 1 trauma center: morbidity, mortality, and the role of renal scintigraphy.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Pediatric renal trauma is uncommon but potentially serious, and is often managed conservatively. Complications may occur, and the clinical value of renal scintigraphy during follow-up remains unclear. This study aimed to assess morbidity and mortality after pediatric renal trauma and to assess the clinical value of renal scintigraphy during follow-up.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective single-center cohort study included pediatric trauma patients (< 18 years) with renal injuries admitted to a Level 1 trauma center in the Netherlands between January 1, 2001, and December 31, 2024. Mortality and in-hospital complications were assessed, and associations between renal scintigraphy abnormalities and complications during follow-up were evaluated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 72 patients were included, of whom all injuries resulted from blunt trauma. Conservative management was applied in 88% of cases; embolization and nephrectomy were performed in 8% and 3% of patients, respectively. In-hospital mortality was 11% and was attributed exclusively to concomitant traumatic brain injury. Complications occurred in 25% of patients, primarily infections (19%), followed by hypertension during follow up (4%). Renal scintigraphy was performed in 53% of patients, predominantly in those with high-grade injuries; abnormalities were frequently observed (77%) but did not correlate with the occurrence of hypertension, proteinuria, or renal insufficiency during follow-up.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Pediatric renal trauma, including high-grade injuries, can often be managed conservatively, and most complications can be treated using medical therapy or minimally invasive interventions. Renal scintigraphy showed no clear association with long-term morbidity and had limited additional value in routine follow-up. Given the potential for late-onset hypertension, structured long-term clinical surveillance with periodic monitoring of blood pressure, proteinuria, and renal function is warranted, particularly after high-grade injuries.

articles.title: Measurement properties of pulmonary function measurement and patient-reported outcome measures in patients with multiple rib fracture without flail segment; validation study alongside the multicenter FixCon trial.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The reliability and validity of pulmonary function, pain and health related quality of life (HR-QoL) as outcome measures for patients with rib fractures, remain uncertain. Our objective was to evaluate measurement properties in patients with multiple rib fractures by comparing them with generic HR-QoL instruments (EuroQoL-5D-5L [EQ-5D-5L], Short Form-12 [SF-12]).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A multicenter RCT in adults (n = 180) was performed. Spirometry was performed at 30 days, 3, 6, and 12 months after trauma. Patients completed five questions on pain, EQ-5D-5L, SF-12, and two anchor questions on improvement in pulmonary function and thoracic complaints since previous measurement. Reliability, construct validity, responsiveness and floor and ceiling effects were evaluated for all follow-up time-points.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: EQ-5D and SF-12 (sub)scales showed adequate internal consistency. Construct and longitudinal validity were adequate for all (sub)scales, except for construct validity of the SF-12 Physical Component Summary. Ceiling effects were present for all pain questions from 30 days onwards, for EQ-5D-5L utility score (US) from 3 months onwards. Responsiveness analysis indicated that spirometry values showed trivial (tidal volume), small (inspiratory capacity, FEV1), or moderate (FVC) degree of change from 30 days to 12 months. All five pain levels, EQ-5D-5L and SF-12 (sub)scales showed moderate to large degree of change form 30 days to 12 months.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Spirometry and pain are valid instruments for monitoring functional recovery in patients after sustaining multiple rib fractures. Responsiveness was confirmed for pain and spirometry (FVC). EQ-5D-5L and SF-12 are valid, reliable, and responsive. Pain and HRQoL are therefore suitable instruments for measuring treatment effects over time.

articles.title: Prehospital severity and in-hospital mortality in trauma patients managed by the Friuli-Venezia Giulia helicopter emergency medical service: a 6-year retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Data on in-hospital mortality among trauma patients managed by Helicopter Emergency Medical Services (HEMS) in Italy remain limited. We aimed to describe the epidemiology and in-hospital mortality of trauma patients transported after management by the Friuli-Venezia Giulia HEMS and to assess prehospital factors associated with death.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study including trauma patients managed by HEMS FVG and transported to hospital, either directly by HEMS or after continuation of transport by ground emergency medical services, between 2018 and 2023. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Jeffreys-prior penalized logistic regression was used to reduce sparse-data bias and instability from separation. The RTS-based model was designated as the primary model and the NACA-based model as a secondary sensitivity analysis. Model performance was assessed internally, and the functional forms of both age and RTS were examined using restricted cubic splines.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 3,357 trauma records in the source cohort, 205 prehospital deaths were excluded from the in-hospital mortality analysis, leaving 3,152 transported patients. Outcome data were available for 3,143 patients, of whom 107 died in hospital (3.4%). In the primary RTS-based model, older age, lower RTS, tracheal intubation, and prehospital CPR were associated with mortality. Compared with RTS ≥ 7, adjusted ORs were 2.36 (95% CI 1.11-5.50) for RTS 4-<7 and 5.19 (95% CI 1.64-17.04) for RTS < 4. Age was associated with mortality (OR 1.03 per year, 95% CI 1.01-1.04). Continuous RTS analysis was concordant (OR 0.68 per one-point increase, 95% CI 0.54-0.86; p = 0.0013).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among trauma patients transported to hospital after HEMS management, older age, higher prehospital injury severity, tracheal intubation, and prehospital CPR were associated with in-hospital mortality. Intubation and CPR should be interpreted primarily as markers of severe physiological compromise rather than causal determinants of death.

articles.title: Survival benefit of prehospital TXA in fibrinolytic shutdown: Insights from two prospective trauma trials.
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Fibrinolytic phenotypes have been implicated in postinjury pathophysiology and outcomes. While prehospital tranexamic acid (TXA) administration has demonstrated survival benefits, the interaction between TXA administration and distinct fibrinolytic profiles remains poorly defined.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed data from a harmonized dataset combining 2 prospective trials evaluating prehospital TXA use in trauma (Prehospital Tranexamic Acid Use for Traumatic Brain Injury and the Study of Tranexamic Acid During Air and Ground Medical Prehospital Transport Trial). Patients were stratified by initial thromboelastographic (TEG) LY30 into fibrinolytic shutdown (<0.9%), hyperfibrinolysis (>3%), and physiological fibrinolysis (0.9-3%). The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included 24-hour mortality and adverse events. Multivariable regression adjusted for TXA administration, fibrinolysis phenotypes, age, mechanism of injury, injury severity score, and shock index on presentation to the hospital.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1,249 patients, 30-day mortality was 14.5% in the fibrinolytic shutdown group, 6.7% in the hyperfibrinolysis group, and 6.5% in the physiological fibrinolysis group. After multivariable regression, hyperfibrinolysis was associated with increased risk of death (HR 2.87; 95% CI: 1.10-7.53; p 0.03). Patients with fibrinolytic shutdown who were randomized to TXA had decreased risk of death (HR 0.32; 95% CI: 0.11-0.91; p =0.03).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This multitrial analysis revealed greater statistically significant differences between fibrinolytic phenotypes than analysis of each trial alone. Fibrinolytic phenotypes were independently associated with mortality. Fibrinolytic shutdown in patients randomized to receive TXA was associated with lower risk of death. These findings support the relevance of fibrinolysis profiling during early trauma care and underscore the need for larger studies to further elucidate the prognostic and therapeutic implications in trauma.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Prognostic and Epidemiological; Level III.

articles.title: Decompressive craniectomy: The potential association with long-term functional outcomes in children with traumatic brain injury.
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is the leading cause of death and disability in pediatric patients. However, TBI management widely varies due to a lack of high-quality evidence in pediatric population. We aimed to determine the association of decompressive craniectomy (DC) on long-term functional independence in pediatric TBI. We hypothesize that the use of DC would not be associated with improved functional independence after discharge.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This is a retrospective cohort study using the Federal Interagency Traumatic Brain Injury Research (FITBIR) Informatics System, a national database of TBI studies. The Approaches and Decisions in Acute Pediatric TBI (ADAPT) Trial was selected for its international patient population from 2014 to 2017. Patients (age ≤18 y) with TBI, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) ≤8, and insertion of an intracranial pressure monitor were categorized into the DC and no-DC groups. The primary outcome was Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended Pediatric Version (GOS-E Peds) at a follow-up visit ≥6 months postdischarge. A secondary analysis included all patients admitted for the management of TBI to examine the association between DC and in-hospital mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We included 686 TBI patients followed up ≥6 months postdischarge or recorded mortality. Of those, 213 (31.0%) patients received DC. The median GCS on presentation was 5. The median GOS-E at follow-up was 5. In a multivariate regression model, the use of DC was not associated with good functional recovery defined as GOS-E Peds <5 (odds ratio [OR]: 0.64, 95% CI: 0.39-1.05, p=0.077). In a secondary analysis, DC was not associated with in-hospital mortality (OR: 1.02, 95% CI: 0.60-1.74, p=0.95).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The results of this study suggest that DC is not significantly associated with favorable functional outcomes >6 months postdischarge or decreased in-hospital mortality. Future research is warranted to further delineate the indication for DC in the pediatric TBI population.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Prognostic/epidemiological study; Level IV.

articles.title: Does Surgeon Experience Affect Outcomes in Robotic Cholecystectomy for Emergency Biliary Disease? A Statewide Analysis.
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The use of robotic surgery (RS) as an operative technique in emergency general surgery (EGS) is rapidly growing, with a >3-fold increase in RS-EGS operations since 2011. Prior work has utilized payer claims to evaluate outcomes of RS-cholecystectomy in the EGS setting. However, these studies fail to evaluate how outcomes are affected by surgeon experience or whether there is a learning curve for RS in the EGS setting. We hypothesized that surgeons on the learning curve may have higher rates of complications.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: EGS collaborative data from 12 hospitals were used to compare the postoperative outcomes of patients undergoing RS-cholecystectomy to those undergoing laparoscopic (LS) cholecystectomy. Unadjusted and adjusted outcomes were compared between the control (LS) and the exposure (RS) groups, using entropy balancing and multivariable analysis. Learning curves were plotted for postoperative outcomes, operative time, and hospital length of stay, using linear spline curve modeling (single knot at case 70) to represent how outcomes change with increasing surgeon experience.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We evaluated 8,221 minimally invasive total cholecystectomy cases, of which 2,141 were performed with RS. RS-cholecystectomy was associated with a lower rate of technical complications, independent of surgeon experience (adjusted odds ratio: 0.38, 95% CI: 0.21-0.69, p=0.002). Operative time was longer, and nontechnical complications were higher for RS-cholecystectomy (+13.1min, 95% CI: 7.3-18.8, p<0.001 and adjusted odds ratio: 1.18, 95% CI: 1.01-1.39, P=0.043, respectively). Adjusted operative time decreased by 14.1 minutes over the first 70 cases (95% CI: -21.8 to -6.4, p<0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: RS-cholecystectomy is not associated with more technical complications, and surgeons with less RS experience did not have a higher likelihood of technical complications for cholecystectomy when compared with LS in an EGS setting. Operative times for RS-cholecystectomy are longer than LS and significantly decrease with increasing surgeon experience.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Therapeutic/Care Management; Level III.

abstract.label: STUDY TYPE
abstract.text: Prognostic/epidemiological.

articles.title: Ventricular Fibrillation in PRKAG2 Cardiomyopathy: A Genetic Arrhythmia Substrate Beyond Wolff-Parkinson-White.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: PRKAG2 syndrome is a rare autosomal dominant glycogen storage cardiomyopathy characterized by left ventricular hypertrophy, ventricular pre-excitation, and progressive conduction system disease.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: We report the case of a 25-year-old woman with genetically confirmed PRKAG2 syndrome who presented with an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Echocardiography revealed preserved left ventricular systolic function with mild concentric hypertrophy and marked apical thickening. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed anterolateral trabecular hypertrophy without evidence of myocardial fibrosis. Electrophysiological study excluded Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome and instead identified a fasciculoventricular accessory pathway. Given the occurrence of ventricular fibrillation and the associated arrhythmic risk, a transvenous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was implanted for secondary prevention.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This case illustrates the atypical presentation of arrhythmias that deviate from classical patterns, such as those seen in Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGE
abstract.text: Individualized risk assessment, close electrophysiological monitoring, and consideration of early implantable cardioverter-defibrillator implantation are important in PRKAG2-related cardiomyopathy.

articles.title: A Simple Platelet-Centered Coagulation-Inflammation Combined Score for Predicting In-Hospital Mortality in Sepsis.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Accurate mortality prediction in sepsis requires assessing coagulation and inflammatory disturbances, yet existing scores are complex or incompletely capture these interconnected processes. We developed and internally validated a simple score combining inflammatory and platelet-related indicators with clinical parameters to predict in-hospital mortality in sepsis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study included 6175 adults with sepsis from the MIMIC-IV database. Patients were randomly divided into training (n=4322) and validation (n=1853) cohorts. Candidate predictors were screened by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, and final variables entered multivariable logistic regression to construct the Coagulation-Inflammation Combined Score (CICS). Performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration, internal bootstrap validation, and decision curve analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 6175 patients, 807 (13.1%) died during hospitalization. The final CICS incorporated five routinely available variables: lactate, Glasgow Coma Scale score, age, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and platelet count. Discrimination was good, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.768 (95% CI, 0.747-0.788) in training and 0.806 (95% CI, 0.776-0.835) in validation cohorts, comparable to SOFA (DeLong P=0.526 and P=0.180). Calibration was acceptable (Brier scores 0.102 and 0.091). Bootstrap validation indicated minimal optimism, and decision curve analysis showed exploratory findings across clinically relevant thresholds.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The CICS is a parsimonious prognostic score using five routinely available variables from the first 24 hours after ICU admission. It showed discrimination comparable to SOFA, acceptable calibration, and favorable decision-curve performance. CICS should be interpreted as a separate prognostic score for early ICU stratification once first-24-hour data are available, rather than for emergency department triage or ICU admission decisions.

articles.title: Interviews With Physicians and Nurses Revealed Inconsistencies in Paediatric Basic Life Support Training for Families of Children With Heart Disease in Sweden.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: Paediatric basic life support (PBLS) training is strongly recommended for the families of children with elevated risks of cardiac arrest, as their initial survival could rely heavily on bystanders. We explored the perspectives of physicians and nurses on PBLS training and identified perceived barriers and facilitators to implementing family training.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: An exploratory descriptive design was used, based on semi-structured interviews with 15 physicians and 16 registered nurses working in paediatric cardiology clinics in university and regional hospitals across Sweden.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Healthcare professionals were concerned that introducing PBLS training might heighten parental anxiety and were reluctant to raise the subject. Consequently, PBLS training was infrequently discussed or offered. Furthermore, there was uncertainty regarding which families should be prioritised. The absence of structured routines and national guidelines was perceived as frustrating and ethically burdensome. The lack of formal policies emerged as the primary barrier to implementation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This study revealed inconsistencies in PBLS training practices for families of children with heart disease. There is a clear need for consensus on which families should be prioritised for PBLS training and for national guidelines to support healthcare professionals in identifying eligible families.

articles.title: Ectopic pregnancy-related severe maternal morbidity in Shenzhen: a sentinel indicator for gaps in early pregnancy care systems.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Despite China's progress in reducing maternal mortality, severe maternal morbidity in early pregnancy, particularly ectopic pregnancy, remains a critical challenge in urban settings like Shenzhen. This study examines the clinical presentation scenarios, types, and sociodemographic compositions of ectopic pregnancy -related severe maternal morbidity to map potential structural vulnerabilities within the maternal healthcare continuum and propose interventions aligned with China's 'Healthy Motherhood 2030' agenda.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective analysis used 2023 data from Shenzhen's Maternal and Child Health Care Management Information System, covering 66 maternity hospitals. A total of 245 ectopic pregnancy-related severe maternal morbidity cases were identified using standard WHO near-miss criteria. Statistical analyses evaluated the descriptive distributions and baseline profiles of clinical outcomes across different initial resuscitation settings.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 154,000 live births, 1,075 severe maternal morbidity cases (0.70%) included 257 (23.9%) ectopic pregnancy-related emergencies. After exclusions, we analysed 245 cases: 67.35% multiparous women, 31.84% had a junior high education or lower and 95% without prenatal care. Ectopic pregnancy-severe maternal morbidity occurred mostly at home (46.12%), followed by outpatient/emergency (30.20%) and inpatient (23.67%) settings. Among home/emergency presentations, 83.3% of women had lower education and 80.4% were employed. Tubal isthmus pregnancies (42.45%) dominated home-based emergencies, while atypical sites were frequent in clinical settings. Advanced severe complications occurred in only seven cases, limiting meaningful statistical comparisons across settings.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In a high-resource, low-MMR urban environment, ectopic pregnancy-related emergencies account for nearly one-quarter of the total SMM burden, with acute crises often concentrated in pre-hospital or frontline care settings. These descriptive patterns suggest that maternal safety strategies should consider shifting focus toward enhancing community health literacy and rapid-response integration at the primary care level. Forward-looking interventions - such as mobile health platforms, clinical simulation training, and formalised early pregnancy emergency networks - warrant prospective evaluation as potential operational pathways to bridge the identified gaps.

articles.title: General Anesthesia vs Monitored Anesthesia Care With Local Anesthetic Infiltration (MAC-VL) for Ankle Fracture Open Reduction and Internal Fixation: Impact on Recovery Metrics and Safety.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Monitored anesthesia care (MAC) combined with regional anesthetic techniques is commonly used for open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) of unstable ankle fractures. When compared to general anesthesia (GA), MAC with regional anesthesia has been associated with reduced systemic adverse effects and shorter recovery times, although regional anesthesia carries additional costs and potential complications of its own. A new technique involving the infiltration of high-volume, low-concentration (VL) local anesthetic was therefore developed. When used in conjunction with MAC, we refer to this technique as MAC-VL. This study evaluates outcomes and recovery metrics following outpatient ankle ORIF performed under GA vs MAC-VL without regional anesthesia.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: An IRB-approved retrospective cohort study was conducted including 159 adults who underwent outpatient ankle ORIF between February 1, 2023, and January 31, 2026. Patients were identified using standardized diagnostic and procedural codes and grouped according to anesthesia type. All patients received a standardized injection of local anesthetic around the proposed operative sites before the procedure; anesthesia type was MAC (n = 48) or GA (n = 111). The primary outcome was time to discharge, defined as the interval from incision closed to hospital discharge. Secondary outcomes were considered exploratory and included tourniquet, operative, anesthesia time, time in room, Post Anesthesia Care Unit length of stay, conversion from MAC to GA, reported postoperative nausea and vomiting, admissions, and postoperative emergency department visits.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 160 procedures for which no significant difference in case mix could be detected with the numbers available, MAC-VL was associated with a significantly shorter time to discharge-reducing discharge time by 55.2 minutes (P < .001) following adjustment for demographic, clinical, and operative covariates-and shortened total anesthesia and operating room time compared with GA. With the numbers available, no significant difference was detected for the remaining secondary outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The MAC-VL protocol was associated with shorter operating room and recovery times and may improve health care resource use.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level III, retrospective cohort study.

articles.title: The Evaluation and Management of Patients With Suicidal Ideation or Behavior by Emergency Medical Services.

abstract.text: Emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians, such as paramedics and emergency medical technicians, frequently respond to 911 calls involving patients with suicidal ideation or behavior (SIB); however, guidance for these complex prehospital encounters remains limited. This article describes the Los Angeles County EMS Agency's (LAC-EMSA) initiative to develop a comprehensive policy for evaluating and managing patients with SIB. A quality improvement (QI) committee approach was used to assess current practices, identify targets for improvement, design countermeasures, and implement policy changes. Key activities included reviewing national model guidelines and California's EMS agencies' policies; conducting interdisciplinary case reviews of EMS encounters with patients with SIB; surveying emergency departments on suicide screening practices; collecting EMS clinicians' perspectives on challenges and potential interventions; and evaluating commonly used suicide risk screening instruments. Findings were synthesized through committee discussions, identifying five critical domains for improvement: (1) standardized terminology; (2) evidence-based guidance for evaluating suicide risk; (3) enhanced decision support for patient disposition; (4) protocols for safety planning; and (5) strategies for collaboration with law enforcement and conflict resolution. The committee recommended a new comprehensive policy addressing these domains which was subsequently developed and implemented. Limitations include the initiative's focus on a single county EMS system, the absence of validated prehospital suicide risk screening tools, and the need for evaluation of the policy's effectiveness. This initiative demonstrates that EMS agencies can leverage QI methodologies to create evidence-informed policies that advance prehospital care for SIB and reduce variability in practice.

articles.title: Reverse sinus barotrauma with periorbital emphysema as an occupational hazard - a case report.

abstract.text: Sinus barotrauma is the second most common diving injury among divers. It results from an imbalance between the pressure within the sinuses and the ambient pressure. It may occur not only as "barotrauma of descent" but also as "barotrauma of ascent/reverse barotrauma," which is less common. Here, we describe a professional diver who had worked at a fish farm for nearly 3 years, diving with SCUBA equipment, and developed reverse sinus barotrauma with periorbital emphysema. This diving injury is preventable. To help prevent it, divers must have adequate education and knowledge of diving physics, physiology, and injuries. They should also be aware of their health status and whether they are fit to dive on a given day. If in doubt, they should cancel the dive. If they are unable to equalize the pressure difference and/or experience sinus pain, they should stop descending, abort the dive, and seek medical evaluation and treatment.

articles.title: A Simulation-based Mastery Learning Curriculum to Address Cardiac Point-of-care Ultrasound Requirements of Anesthesiology Board Certification.
articles.journal_full: The journal of education in perioperative medicine : JEPM

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Focused cardiac ultrasound (FoCUS) is increasingly recognized as an essential competency for anesthesiologists and appears in the American Board of Anesthesiology (ABA) APPLIED exam. Standardized training approaches remain limited. This study evaluated a simulation-based mastery learning (SBML) curriculum for achieving FoCUS image acquisition competency among anesthesiology fellows and attending anesthesiologists.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this single-center, pretest/posttest study (August 2022-February 2024), 12 fellows and 6 attending anesthesiologists participated in a curriculum consisting of 2 3-hour sessions combining transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) simulation and standardized patient scanning. Performance was assessed using a 20-item checklist derived from the ABA objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) content outline. A minimum passing standard (MPS) of 85% was set using the Mastery Angoff method. Posttests were administered ≥1 month after training. The primary outcome was improvement in FoCUS image acquisition skills, defined by achievement of the MPS on posttest assessment. Secondary outcomes included FoCUS knowledge on a written exam, confidence, course satisfaction, and OSCE success.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eighteen participants completed the curriculum. At baseline, 0/18 (0%) participants achieved the MPS. Among participants who completed both scheduled training sessions (15/18), 12 (80%) achieved mastery on their first posttest attempt, including all fellows who completed both sessions (9/9). The remaining participants required additional deliberate practice before achieving the MPS on a subsequent posttest. Performance improved significantly across all TTE views (p < .01).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This SBML curriculum enabled rapid mastery of FoCUS image acquisition across learners with varying experience levels and achieved competency aligned with expectations for FoCUS image acquisition on the ABA APPLIED examination. SBML can be utilized to create effective curricula addressing evolving certification requirements and clinical needs.

articles.title: Interstate EMS medication restocking after hospital closure: A pharmacy-led regulatory response.
articles.journal_full: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To describe a multi-state regulatory and operational response that preserved EMS controlled substance access following the closure of a rural community hospital.

abstract.label: SUMMARY
abstract.text: Hospital closures can disrupt established emergency medical services (EMS) medical control relationships and medication restocking pathways, including access to controlled substances. Limited literature describes the role of hospital pharmacy departments in maintaining EMS medication continuity during system-level disruptions. Following the closure of Nashoba Valley Medical Center in Massachusetts, local EMS agencies experienced increased transport times and operational strain related to medication restocking requirements. To mitigate service disruption, the Massachusetts Department of Public Health Drug Control Program and Office of Emergency Medical Services issued a time-limited waiver permitting interstate restocking at designated New Hampshire hospitals. Hospital pharmacy leadership collaborated with EMS agencies and regulators to establish controlled substance custody safeguards, documentation workflows, and reconciliation procedures consistent with state and federal requirements. This case highlights structural differences between Massachusetts and New Hampshire EMS medication governance models and demonstrates the role of hospital pharmacy in aligning cross-jurisdictional compliance frameworks.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Hospital pharmacists may serve as critical regulatory integrators during regional healthcare disruptions. Formal agreements, clearly defined custody models, and interagency coordination are essential to maintaining EMS controlled substance access while ensuring compliance with applicable laws and regulations.

articles.title: Flood Response in Rural Indonesia Implementing the World Health Organization Emergency Medical Team Minimum Data Set - Disaster Report.

abstract.text: Indonesia experiences recurrent natural disasters that impose substantial strain on its health system, with annual flooding affecting rural communities such as Sitiarjo Sumbermanjing Wetan. Despite these recurring events, Indonesia has not systematically adopted the World Health Organization (WHO) Emergency Medical Team (EMT) Minimum Data Set (MDS) for standardized disaster medical reporting, thereby limiting data integration and evidence-based policy development. This disaster report describes the operational patterns, clinical demographics, and syndromic distribution captured by the WHO EMT MDS framework across three distinct flood responses in 2017, 2022, and 2023. The Universitas Brawijaya Emergency Medical Team (UB-EMT) prospectively collected daily surveillance data using the WHO EMT MDS reporting system. A total of 363 consultations were analyzed and stratified according to age, sex, and reporting period. Consultation volume peaked on Day 1 and declined on subsequent days. Females accounted for 62% of the cases and adults (18-64 years old) represented the majority of patients (68.87%). The most frequently reported conditions were skin diseases (33.46%), musculoskeletal problems (24.39%), and acute respiratory infections (16.64%), respectively. Age-specific patterns were evident: preschoolers and school-aged children presented with acute respiratory infections, whereas adults and older people more commonly experienced skin diseases and musculoskeletal problems. The absence of systematic implementation of the WHO EMT MDS constrains standardized surveillance and inter-team coordination in disaster settings. Therefore, the institutional adoption of the WHO EMT MDS is essential to strengthen real-time monitoring, optimize resource allocation, and enhance post-disaster evaluation in Indonesia.

articles.title: Two divers submerged in the Mediterranean Sea for 30 years: persistence of adipocere and implications for postmortem submersion interval estimation.

abstract.text: Estimation of the postmortem submersion interval (PMSI) remains challenging in bodies recovered from aquatic environments, particularly after prolonged submersion and in the presence of adipocere. We report the cases of two divers who disappeared during the same accident in the Mediterranean Sea in December 1993 and were recovered 30 years later at depths of 103 and 113 m, 13 m apart. Both bodies underwent whole-body postmortem computed tomography, external examination, autopsy, toxicological analyses, and genetic identification. Both showed advanced skeletonization predominantly affecting the upper body, associated with persistence of adipocere-like tissues in the pelvic regions and lower limbs. However, the quality of soft-tissue preservation differed markedly: in X1, residual tissues were largely disorganized and consisted of yellowish-to-brown aggregates, whereas X2 showed more extensive preservation of the skin, hair, and discernible muscle masses in the lower limbs. X1 wore a two-piece semi-dry wetsuit, whereas X2 wore a full dry suit; these differences in preservation are discussed in relation to the characteristics of the diving equipment and local microenvironmental conditions. Pelvic tissues compatible with adipocere showed attenuation values ranging from - 100 to - 40 Hounsfield units. Genetic identification was achieved from muscle in X1 and from femoral bone in X2; toxicological analyses were negative. These observations illustrate regional and interindividual variability in preservation after the same 30-year marine PMSI and highlight the limitations of estimating PMSI solely on the basis of the macroscopic appearance of the bodies.

articles.title: Impact of antithrombotic therapy on management and prognosis of patients hospitalized for upper gastrointestinal bleeding: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Antithrombotic agents are frequently implicated in upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB), yet their impact on prognosis and management remains unclear. The aim of this study was to assess the impact of pre-existing antithrombotic therapy on the management and prognosis of patients hospitalized for UGIB.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This study used data from a retrospective, multicenter cohort of adult patients hospitalized for UGIB between January 2019 and December 2020 in Greater Paris University Hospitals. Patients were categorized into four groups according to their pre-existing antithrombotic treatment: antiplatelet therapy, anticoagulant therapy, both, or none. The primary outcome was thirty-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included endoscopy, endoscopic hemostasis, and blood transfusion within 7 days, and intensive care unit admission. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression and reported as adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (95%CIs).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 928 patients, 226 (24%) were on antiplatelet therapy alone, 154 (17%) on anticoagulant therapy alone, 61 (7%) on combined therapy, and 487 (52%) received no antithrombotic treatment. Thirty-day mortality was 6.9%: 8.4% in the no-antithrombotic group, 6.2% in the antiplatelet group, 4.5% in the anticoagulant group, and 3.3% in the combined therapy group. Compared with the no-antithrombotic group, anticoagulant therapy alone was associated with lower mortality (aOR=0.28, 95% CI 0.10-0.83), while antiplatelet therapy alone or combined therapy were not significantly associated (aOR=0.47, 95% CI 0.19-1.14 and aOR=0.12, 95% CI 0.01-1.11, respectively). Neither anticoagulant nor antiplatelet therapy was associated with secondary outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Antithrombotic therapy had no negative impact on the management or prognosis of patients hospitalized for UGIB.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of shock index, revised trauma score, and injury severity score for mortality prediction in trauma: A hierarchical meta-analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Shock Index (SI) and Revised Trauma Score (RTS) are physiological tools available at the point of trauma triage. Injury Severity Score (ISS) is an anatomical score that requires completed injury characterization and is typically available only after initial resuscitation. Their comparative value for predicting mortality and whether ISS meaningfully adds to the acute tools remains unclear.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: The aim of this systematic review and hierarchical meta-analysis is to pool the diagnostic accuracy of SI and RTS as acute mortality-prediction tools in adult trauma patients; to benchmark these against ISS; and to formally test, in studies reporting both, whether RTS and ISS differ in diagnostic accuracy.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Electronic databases were searched from inception to May 2026. In-hospital mortality was prespecified as the primary endpoint. Pooled sensitivity, specificity and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) analyses were performed with a bivariate random-effects model for each tool separately. For studies reporting both RTS and ISS in the same cohort, a paired comparison was performed using a bivariate model with test type as a covariate and a pooled within-study difference analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twelve studies (234,129 patients) were included. Pooled sensitivity/specificity were 0.679/0.763 for SI (5 studies, AUC 0.747), 0.788/0.801 for RTS (6 studies, AUC 0.852), and 0.788/0.796 for ISS (9 studies, AUC 0.855). In the six studies reporting both RTS and ISS, a paired bivariate comparison found no significant difference in diagnostic accuracy (likelihood-ratio test, p = 0.91; within-study sensitivity OR 1.59, 95% CI 0.82-3.07; specificity OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.55-1.45).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: RTS and ISS did not differ significantly in a formal paired comparison, and neither tool, alone, reliably rules in or out death at realistic trauma prevalence. SI, RTS and ISS should be understood as serving different, complementary roles across the trauma timeline - SI and RTS at the point of acute triage, ISS as a later anatomical benchmark - rather than as competing predictors to be ranked against one another.

articles.title: Epidemiological patterns and surgical outcomes of pediatric supracondylar humerus fractures: a focus on domestic safety and seasonal variations.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Supracondylar humerus fractures (SHFs) are prevalent pediatric elbow injuries. This study investigates the epidemiology, clinical characteristics, and treatment outcomes of pediatric SHFs to identify preventive strategies.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study included 298 pediatric patients (aged ≤14 years) treated for SHFs between December 2018 and June 2024. Demographic data, injury mechanisms, seasonal variations, and surgical details were analyzed. Radiological reduction was assessed via the Baumann angle and anterior humeral line. Functional outcomes were evaluated using Flynn's criteria.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The study cohort (mean age 6.1 years; 58.7% male) predominantly sustained extension-type fractures (96.3%), with the severely displaced Gartland Type III being the most frequent (49.3%). The incidence of injuries peaked during the summer months and school holidays, with the majority occurring at home (64.1%) due to simple falls (93%). Surgical intervention, consisting of closed reduction and percutaneous pinning, was necessitated in 75.8% of cases, with a mean time-to-surgery of 4.6 h. Satisfactory (excellent and good) functional outcomes were achieved in 97.9% of the patients. Overall complication rates were minimal, and transient nerve injuries (2%) fully resolved spontaneously during follow-up.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Pediatric SHFs frequently occur in domestic settings during the summer months, strongly highlighting the need for "safe home" modifications and parental education. Despite a high prevalence of severely displaced fractures, prompt surgical intervention and meticulous anatomical reduction yield excellent long-term functional outcomes and minimize complications.

articles.title: The peri-operative burden of e-bike and e-scooter injuries in Greater London: a prospective cohort study.

abstract.text: The contribution of e-bike and e-scooter injuries to peri-operative activity across a trauma network is poorly characterised. We conducted a prospective cohort study across 24 London hospitals from 30/03/2026 to 12/04/2026 to measure the proportion of urgent and emergency operations associated with these injuries and describe the peri-operative resource use. Thirty-one patients underwent one operation each, accounting for 31/3327 (0.9%) urgent and emergency operations. E-bikes were involved in 26/31 (84%) injuries. Median operative duration was 153 (110-221 [19-405]) min; 7/31 (23%) operations occurred out of hours and 3/31 (10%) required immediate life- or limb-saving surgery. Orthopaedics accounted for 26/31 (84%) cases. Six of 31 patients (19%) required postoperative critical care and 7/31 (23%) spent at least 1 week in hospital. Most patients (22/31; 71%) presented to trauma units. Exploratory estimates for the included ambulance, emergency department, theatre, hospital stay and major haemorrhage components were £224,658-£373,820 under low- and high-cost assumptions, respectively. Theatre time was the largest component. These injuries accounted for a small proportion of operations, but some patients required immediate surgery, out-of-hours operating or critical care. Their occurrence across trauma units and major trauma centres supports including both settings and peri-operative outcomes in future surveillance. Longer, seasonally representative surveillance and more complete follow-up are needed to estimate annual operative workload and costs.

articles.title: Effect of Intrathecal Bupivacaine Temperature Variation on Prophylaxis of Shivering in Urologic Patients Undergoing Spinal Anesthesia.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Postspinal shivering is a frequent complication of spinal anesthesia (SA) and is particularly relevant in urological procedures, where perioperative heat loss can be exacerbated by irrigation fluids. Modifying the temperature of the intrathecal local anesthetic may affect thermoregulatory responses and the properties of the blockade.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective, randomized, double-blind, controlled trial was conducted in 96 patients (ASA I-II, aged 18-60 years) undergoing elective urological procedures under SA. Participants received intrathecal hyperbaric bupivacaine 0.5% (15 mg) combined with fentanyl 25 μg at one of three temperatures: 4°C (cold; n = 32), 24°C (room; n = 32), or 37°C (warm; n = 32). Shivering was graded using the validated Crossley and Mahajan scale. The primary endpoint was the incidence of clinically significant shivering (Grade ≥ 3) throughout the observation period, evaluated at 10-min intervals.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Cold bupivacaine demonstrated a significantly higher incidence of clinically significant shivering (Grade ≥ 3) (81.3%) compared with the room-temperature (34.4%) and warm (25%) groups (p < 0.001). The post hoc analysis showed that the difference between the room-temperature and warm groups was not significant. Pharmacological intervention requirements were substantially elevated in the cold group (43.8%, 15.6%, 15.6%; p = 0.01). Warm bupivacaine accelerated sensory and motor block onset (p = 0.001) while reducing residual motor blockade.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Warmed intrathecal bupivacaine significantly reduces PSS incidence and severity while optimizing block characteristics without compromising safety in urological patients. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT07081516.

articles.title: Prevalence and psychosocial factors of PTSD among disaster-affected populations in India: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) is a widespread condition affecting individuals globally in the aftermath of disasters. For this review, the disaster-affected population refers to individuals or populations who have experienced a potentially traumatic event with psychosocial consequences. The current review aims to assess the prevalence and psychosocial factors of PTSD among disaster-affected populations in India.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in the present study. Relevant keywords were identified and used to search databases, including Scopus, PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Cochrane, as well as websites and reference lists, to identify eligible studies. The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) flow chart was used for the final included studies to reveal the results. The current review conducted a critical appraisal of the included studies by using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) quality evaluation. Meta-analysis using Jeffreys's Amazing Statistics Program (JASP) software and manual analysis was done to assess the psychosocial factors and conceptual framework.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1370 documents were identified from the databases, and 151 documents were duplicates. Following title/abstract screening, 1178 studies were excluded, 21 full text not retrieved, and 20 studies were included for the final results. The critical appraisal results found that more than half of the studies demonstrated good methodological quality. The results revealed that the pooled prevalence of PTSD was 38%, with young populations disproportionately affected, although no significant associations were found with age group, disaster type, or region. Nineteen psychosocial risk factors were identified, prominently including loss of family members or pets and property damage. The conceptual framework highlights the interplay between traumatic events and psychosocial factors in PTSD outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The findings underscore the need for multidisciplinary collaboration among mental health professionals, long-term intervention strategies, and evidence-based practices to address India's mental health challenges.

articles.title: Perfusion imaging predicts therapeutic cooling response and tracks cis-p-tau pathology in porcine brain injuries.
articles.journal_full: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics

abstract.text: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) and ischemic stroke cause substantial morbidity and mortality, yet effective neuroprotective therapies remain elusive. Although therapeutic hypothermia shows strong neuroprotection in lissencephalic rodent models, adult clinical trials have repeatedly failed, largely due to poor preclinical translatability and uniform cooling protocols that overlook patient heterogeneity. Using a large cohort of gyrencephalic porcine models (n = 89) of TBI and stroke, subjects were allocated to sham, injury, or therapeutic cooling groups administered via a custom-designed, non-invasive intranasal selective brain cooling device for pre-hospital and hospital settings. We combined clinical CT perfusion and neuropathology to identify biomarkers that predict cooling efficacy. Brain cooling significantly reduced mortality in TBI and stroke compared to untreated controls. We showed that concurrent hyperemia (elevated cerebral blood flow) and blood-brain barrier (BBB) leakage during cooling predicted intracranial hypertension, which may facilitate identification of high-risk subjects that require intervention. Sustained hyperemia was pathological. Neuropathological assessment revealed that cis-phosphorylated-tau (cis-p-tau), a major early driver of both TBI and stroke, is correlated with injury severity, treatment response, and BBB permeability. In TBI, mild selective brain cooling (∼1.3 °C reduction) was associated with reduced secondary brain damage, whereas deeper cooling (≥3 °C) offered no added benefit in this cohort. These findings suggest that integrating perfusion imaging and the early molecular driver cis P-tau can guide personalized hypothermia, advancing the field toward precision medicine in acute brain injury neuroprotection.

articles.title: Can hyperbaric oxygen therapy revolutionise the management of central retinal artery occlusion? A systematic review and meta-analysis of its efficacy and safety.
Is paediatric conscious sedation as effective as general anaesthesia for removing aural and nasal foreign bodies?
Impact of prehospital olanzapine for methamphetamine intoxication on patient and system-level outcomes: a population-based retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Acute methamphetamine intoxication is a common presentation in emergency departments (EDs). Empowering paramedics to treat methamphetamine intoxication in the prehospital setting could help to improve patient and system outcomes. This study evaluated the impact of a 2018 policy allowing paramedics to administer olanzapine for methamphetamine intoxication in the prehospital setting on patient and system outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective pre-post analysis of population-based health administrative data and qualitative paramedic reports. Individuals with a methamphetamine-related health system contact between 2016–2020 in Winnipeg, Canada, who were eligible for pre-hospital olanzapine were included. The exposure was the administration of olanzapine in the pre-hospital setting by paramedics. Individuals who received prehospital olanzapine were compared with those who did not, prior to (2016–2018) and after (2018–2020) the policy change. Primary outcomes included physical or chemical restraint prior to ED, transport to ED and leaving from the ED prior to being seen or against medical advice. Outcomes were modelled using logistic (binary outcomes) and Cox proportional hazard (temporal outcomes) models adjusted for covariates using inverse probability of treatment weighting.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The cohort included 1041 individuals, of which 222 received the intervention. Among individuals receiving olanzapine, the median age was 31 years, 58.1% were male, 56.8% were in the lowest income quintile and a high prevalence of mental health disorders and legal system involvement were observed. After adjusting for covariates, individuals receiving olanzapine in the prehospital setting were more likely to be transported to ED by paramedics (adjusted OR (aOR): 11.83, 95% CI 3.19 to 43.80) and less likely to leave the ED without being seen by a doctor (aOR: 0.56, 95% CI 0.32 to 0.97) compared with individuals who did not.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Prehospital administration of olanzapine among individuals experiencing methamphetamine intoxication was associated with a higher likelihood of transport to the ED and being seen by a physician.

articles.title: Digital Health-Enabled Prehospital Notification for Acute Stroke Using the Brain Saver Mobile App in Emergency Medical Transport in South Korea: Pilot Quasi-Experimental Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Timely access to stroke care is critical for patient prognosis.
