abstract.text: Portable ophthalmic devices expand access to eye care beyond standard clinics and accommodate patients underserved by traditional equipment. Addressing technical and usability challenges and enhancing training opportunities will strengthen their integration into routine and outreach care.

articles.title: Role of Telemedicine in Congenital Heart Disease Care Models in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American Heart Association
authors: American Heart Association Council on Lifelong Congenital Heart Disease and Heart Health in the Young, Rheumatic Fever, Endocarditis, and Kawasaki Disease Committee; Council on Clinical Cardiology; and the Council on Cardiovascular and Stroke Nursing

abstract.text: Telemedicine is increasingly recognized as a transformative strategy to address critical challenges in low- and middle-income countries, which comprise 63% of all nations, 84% of the global population, and 90% of children <15 years of age. These regions experience multiple barriers, including geographic remoteness, economic constraints, limited healthcare infrastructure, and a shortage of trained healthcare professionals. Congenital heart disease, a highly specialized field often centralized in urban centers, is particularly affected, leaving many children without timely or equitable access to life-saving care. In this context, telecardiology has emerged as a valuable tool across the congenital heart disease care continuum, supporting prehospital assessment, inpatient management, postdischarge follow-up, and multidisciplinary collaboration. Beyond video consultations, telemedicine enables secure transmission of electrocardiograms, echocardiograms, advanced imaging, and digital auscultation data. Artificial intelligence-based tools further enhance education, diagnostic support, and quality assurance in image acquisition. Together, these capabilities reduce unnecessary travel, expedite specialist input, strengthen local decision-making, and contribute to improved outcomes. Telemedicine also facilitates collaboration among pediatric cardiologists, neonatologists, intensivists, imaging specialists, and nurses, fostering more integrated and resilient care networks that link peripheral facilities with tertiary centers. By optimizing limited resources and expanding specialist reach, telemedicine holds significant promise for improving access, equity, and outcomes in congenital heart disease care across low- and middle-income countries. Continued investment, strategic planning, and collaborative capacity-building will be essential to ensure its sustainable and effective implementation worldwide.

articles.title: Pediatric Patients-Are Sometimes Just Small Adults.

abstract.text: The phrase "children are not small adults" has appropriately emphasized the distinct physiological, developmental, pharmacologic, and psychosocial needs of pediatric patients. Yet when educators and health systems convey this message without placing equal emphasis on Pediatric Readiness, they may unintentionally imply that pediatric emergency care is primarily the domain of pediatric specialists. This implication conflicts with the reality that more than 80% of children receive emergency care outside specialized children's hospitals, often in settings where pediatric specialists are not physically present. This Special Feature calls for Pediatric Readiness to be understood as essential infrastructure for every emergency department that cares for children. Rather than diminishing pediatric specialization, we reframe pediatric expertise as a system-level resource that can be extended through education, protocols, simulation, teleconsultation, transfer collaboration, and advocacy. The next imperative in pediatric emergency care is to preserve what is distinct about children while ensuring that every emergency setting can care for them safely, competently, and collaboratively.

articles.title: Missing the Deadline: Predictors of Surgical Delay Beyond 18 Hours in Pediatric Supracondylar Humerus Fractures.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: A common national pediatric hospital ranking program utilizes treatment of supracondylar humerus fractures (SCHFx) within 18 hours of presentation as a quality metric when evaluating institutions. However, prior investigations have demonstrated that an arbitrary cutoff of <18 hours has no impact on patient outcomes. The present study aimed to identify clinical and systemic predictors of surgical delay beyond 18 hours following presentation to the emergency department (ED). We hypothesized that evening presentation to the ED and increased injury severity would delay patient care.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We identified 450 patients who underwent surgical treatment for SCHFx between 2013 and 2024. The primary outcome of this study was defined as time to the operating room (OR) following presentation to the ED. Descriptive statistics were obtained for demographic variables and injury specifics. Variables that were normally distributed were compared utilizing Student t tests, while non-normally distributed variables were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test. All categorical variables were compared using χ2 or Fisher exact test. A multivariate logistic regression model was utilized to identify predictors of treatment delays.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The average age of patients was 6.0±2.4 years, and 51.8% (n=233) were male. Most patients were injured following a fall (n=319, 70.9%), had no vascular injury (n=437, 97.1%), no neurological injury (n=390, 86.7%), and no open injury (n=444, 98.7%). Most patients were referred to our institution (n=311, 69.1%) and arrived at the ED via private transportation (n=324, 72.0%), most commonly in the evening (n=256, 56.9%). Only 72 patients (16.0%) experienced surgical delay beyond 18 hours, while the average time to the OR was 12.2±5 hours. On multivariate analysis, evening ED arrival (OR=3.44, 95% CI: 1.87-6.34, P<0.001) and high Gartland severity (OR=2.39, 95% CI: 1.21-4.74, P=0.013) were independent predictors of surgical delay.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: The present study showed that surgical delays for SCHFx repair are driven by predictable system issues and clinical findings. High Gartland severity and evening ED arrival were predictors of delay. Higher-severity cases were more likely to exceed the proposed time to treatment threshold, likely secondary to interfacility transfers and the need for postoperative admission. National quality metrics for pediatric supracondylar humerus fractures should be grounded in clinical outcomes, which are more reflective of the quality of care delivered.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level III.

articles.title: Respiratory morbidity at age 4 across COVID-19 and pre-pandemic birth cohorts: the role of atopic risk.

abstract.label: UNLABELLED
abstract.text: The COVID-19 pandemic dramatically reduced early-life respiratory viral exposures, yet the long-term respiratory consequences for pandemic-born children remain unclear. We aimed to compare respiratory morbidity at age 4 between children born during versus before the pandemic and assess whether atopic risk modifies this association. This single-center birth cohort follow-up study included children born in February-March 2020 (COVID-19 cohort) and pre-pandemic controls born during the same period in 2019. Respiratory outcomes at age 4 were assessed using a structured telephone questionnaire (The International Study of Wheezing in Infants). The primary outcome was composite respiratory morbidity (CRM), defined as use of a short-acting bronchodilator (SABA), inhaled and/or oral corticosteroids, and/or emergency room visits for respiratory symptoms. Of 588 eligible children, 329 (55.9%) completed follow-up (139 COVID-19, 190 controls); baseline characteristics, including atopy prevalence, were comparable between cohorts. CRM during the fourth year of life was significantly more common in the COVID-19 cohort (39.6% vs. 27.4%, p = 0.02). In stratified analyses, CRM was markedly higher among atopic-risk pandemic-born children (atopic subgroup: n = 47 COVID-19, n = 68 controls) (66% vs. 27.9%, p < 0.001), but not among non-atopic children (26.1% vs. 27%). Multivariable logistic regression confirmed a significant COVID-19 cohort × atopy interaction for CRM (OR 5.04, 95% CI 1.83-13.89, p = 0.002), while neither factor alone was independently associated with the outcome.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Birth during the COVID-19 pandemic was associated with increased preschool respiratory morbidity, particularly among children with atopic risk. These findings suggest that altered early-life microbial exposures may modify respiratory morbidity trajectories according to host atopic susceptibility.

abstract.label: WHAT IS KNOWN
abstract.text: • Children born during the COVID-19 pandemic had fewer respiratory infections and wheezing episodes in infancy due to reduced viral circulation. • Atopic predisposition is among the strongest risk factors for recurrent wheezing and persistent asthma in preschool children.

abstract.label: WHAT IS NEW
abstract.text: • Pandemic-born children show significantly higher composite respiratory morbidity at age 4, but exclusively among those with atopic risk (OR 5.04). • Neither pandemic birth nor atopy alone predicts excess morbidity-only their combination does, suggesting host susceptibility shapes long-term respiratory trajectories.

articles.title: Radiographic assessment of metacarpal shortening after nonoperative and operative treatment of spiral and oblique metacarpal shaft fractures.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE
abstract.text: Spiral or oblique metacarpal shaft fractures (MSFs) can be treated nonoperatively with unrestricted mobilisation; however, this approach leads to bone shortening upon healing. While an association between bone shortening and impaired hand function is suspected, empirical clinical evidence is lacking, and differing measurement methods make comparisons between studies difficult.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This study is based on a midterm follow-up (mean 4.5 years) of 33 patients with a single spiral or oblique MSF from our previous randomised controlled trial. The original study and the present study were registered at clinicaltrials.gov (NCT03067454, NCT05869331). The main outcome in the present study was the amount of shortening following nonoperative compared with operative treatment. Bilateral radiographs were obtained, and shortening was determined by comparing the fractured metacarpal to its contralateral counterpart using the Shortening Absolute (SH-Abs) measurement method. Intra- and interrater reliability for SH-Abs were presented with intraclass correlation coefficients. Additional outcomes included extension deficit, cosmesis, and overall satisfaction.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 17 patients had been treated nonoperatively with unrestricted mobilisation and 16 operatively. Mean shortening was 3.9 mm (95% confidence interval [CI], 4.8-3.0 mm) and 0.9 mm (95% CI, 2.0 to -0.3 mm), respectively, with a mean difference of 3 mm (95% CI, 4.3-1.6 mm) (p < 0.001). The SH-Abs showed substantial to excellent reliability. Extension deficit, cosmesis, and overall satisfaction were similar in both groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Metacarpal shortening is to be expected after nonoperative treatment of displaced spiral or oblique MSFs. SH-Abs provides a reproducible measurement and could be used to facilitate comparisons between studies.

articles.title: Association of loneliness and substance use among emergency department patients.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Loneliness is associated with numerous adverse health outcomes. However, little is known about its relationship with substance use among emergency department (ED) patients, a population at elevated risk for substance use and related harms. We examined associations between loneliness and past 90-day substance use among ED patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A convenience sample of patients aged 18-75 years was recruited from an urban academic ED between March 2025 and January 2026 (N = 300). Loneliness was assessed using the UCLA Loneliness Scale (UCLA-20; range = 20 to 80). The Tobacco, Alcohol, Prescription Medication, and Other Substance Use (TAPS) tool assessed binge alcohol use, cannabis use, and illicit drug use, including crack/cocaine, sedatives/hypnotics, opioids, and polydrug use. Multivariable logistic regression models examined associations between loneliness and substance use outcomes, adjusting for demographic characteristics, cigarette use and anxiety and depression symptoms.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Each one-point increase in loneliness was associated with greater odds of illicit drug use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.07, 95% confidence interval [CI]:1.03-1.11), including use of opioids (aOR = 1.10, 95% CI:1.03-1.19), crack/cocaine (aOR = 1.06, 95% CI:1.01-1.13), and polydrug use (aOR = 1.04, 95% CI:1.01-1.08).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Loneliness was independently associated with recent illicit drug use. These findings suggest that loneliness may be an important and underrecognized correlate of high-risk substance use in ED populations. Incorporating loneliness assessment into ED screening workflows may help identify patients at elevated risk for substance-related harms and inform interventions aimed at improving engagement with substance use treatment and supportive services.

articles.title: Importance of early recognition and intervention in Ludwig's angina by emergency medicine physicians to prevent life-threatening complications.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Ludwig's angina is a life-threatening cellulitis that can easily progress to airway compromise. Significant infection, often from periodontal abscesses of the molar teeth, may cause superior and posterior displacement of the tongue compromising patient's airways if not identified and treated promptly. Early recognition and clinical diagnosis, with or without imaging and blood cultures, and antibiotic treatment can help prevent rapid airway compromise, systemic infection and Le Mierre's disease (a rare life-threatening complication). Given that emergency departments are often the first point of contact, maintaining a high index of suspicion and acting decisively can significantly improve patient outcomes.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: We report a case of a 79-year-old male presenting with a swollen neck progressing over the course of 24 h. This gentleman presented to our emergency department with a superior and inferior swelling to the mandible, a change in voice, and displacement of his tongue. Clinical examination showed a trismus of 1.5 cm, a superiorly and posteriorly displaced tongue, and a tender dental abscess of the lower molars. From examination a clinical diagnosis of Ludwig's angina was made, later confirmed on CT head and neck. A suspicious incidental finding of an internal jugular embolus on the background of dental infection was also suspicious for an early presentation of Le Mierre's disease. Intravenous antibiotics were promptly started. Intensive care team was contacted to support the patient's airway and facilitate transfer to our intensive care unit (ICU). Maxillofacial team was also notified and following antibiotics and tooth/abscess removal the patient made a full recovery and has no repeat presentation since.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This case highlighted and emphasised the importance of early recognition of neck swelling by emergency physicians to prevent progression of airway compromise and Le Mierre`s disease. Assessing emergency doctors must be able to identify, diagnose, treat and escalate Ludwig's angina secondary to periodontal abscesses prior airway compromise or systemic infection.

articles.title: Proximal humerus fractures: A review of current management evidence and guidance on contemporary surgical strategies.

abstract.text: Proximal humerus fractures (PHFs) most commonly affect elderly, osteoporotic women, although younger patients sustain them through high-energy trauma. Both incidence and the associated healthcare burden continue to rise with demographic ageing. Non-operative management is preferred for undisplaced fractures and for many elderly patients, whereas a range of internal fixation methods and arthroplasty options are available for more complex injuries. Patient age, comorbidities, functional demands and fracture pattern are the primary determinants of treatment selection, implant choice and expected outcome. Absolute indications for surgery include acute fracture-dislocations, open fractures and injuries with vascular or neurological compromise. Relative indications are based on the degree of displacement and the predicted failure of non-operative treatment, and include head-splitting fractures, severe varus, valgus or posterior tilt of the humeral head, anatomical neck fractures, calcar comminution, complete displacement of the humeral head from the shaft, significant displacement of the lesser or greater tuberosity, displaced three- and four-part fractures, and large impaction defects of the humeral head, particularly when associated with instability. It is important to recognise that the displacement thresholds in routine use are pragmatic and consensus-derived rather than validated, and that expert panels do not agree on a maximum acceptable deviation. Surgery is technically demanding, requiring anatomical reduction, calcar restoration, avoidance of varus, secure fixation of the tuberosities and correct patient and implant selection. Locked plating has been the most common operation, but is associated with high complication rates and has failed to show superiority over non-operative treatment in several large randomised controlled trials. Augmentation of fixation and intramedullary nailing may address calcar comminution, metaphyseal voids and varus collapse. Arthroplasty is increasingly used in elderly patients, with reverse shoulder arthroplasty now dominating over hemiarthroplasty. Results appear better than hemiarthroplasty and plate fixation in the single trial that has compared them directly, but the evidence remains limited. To support this narrative review a systematic search was undertaken to identify every randomised controlled trial of PHF management. This review synthesises and compares current evidence on the management options for PHFs and provides practical guidance on contemporary surgical strategies.

articles.title: Patient centered outcomes after surgical stabilization of rib fractures: A prospective cohort study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Rib fractures are associated with pain, impaired physical function, and reduced quality of life. Surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF) is established for flail chest and ventilator-dependent patients, but its impact on longer-term patient-reported outcomes in broader injury patterns remains unclear. We evaluated whether SSRF is associated with improved physical functioning and pain outcomes compared to nonoperative management.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a prospective observational cohort study of trauma ICU patients with rib fractures admitted between June 2023 and August 2024 at a single Level I trauma center. Patients met institutional criteria for SSRF, including flail chest, ≥ 3 contiguous rib fractures, or ventilator failure. Outcomes were assessed using the SF-36 and SF-MPQ-2 at discharge, 2 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months. Multivariable linear regression adjusted for RibScore, flail chest, ISS, age, obesity, hospital length of stay, and associated injuries. Primary outcomes were SF-36 physical functioning and SF-MPQ-2 present pain intensity (PPI).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 121 patients, 39 (32%) underwent SSRF. The SSRF group had greater chest injury severity, including higher RibScores and more pneumothorax and hemothorax, while overall injury severity and demographics were similar. There were no differences in ICU length of stay, hospital length of stay, ventilator days, or mortality. After adjustment, SSRF was associated with improved physical functioning at discharge (β 13.29, 95% CI 6.53-20.05; p < 0.001) and at 6 months (β 23.40, 95% CI 7.52-39.28; p = 0.005). SSRF was associated with lower pain at discharge, but not at 6 months.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: SSRF was associated with improved short-term and six-month physical functioning without differences in inpatient outcomes or sustained differences in pain. These findings suggest SSRF may primarily accelerate functional recovery rather than provide durable pain reduction.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: II Study type: Prospective Cohort.

articles.title: Timing matters: Prehospital whole blood improves unexpected survivorship in pediatric trauma.
Thoracic irrigation for traumatic hemothorax: a cost-effective analysis.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Recent studies have shown thoracic irrigation after tube thoracostomy drainage of traumatic hemothorax (HTX) reduces the rate of retained HTX and need for secondary interventions such as video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) but the cost-effectiveness of thoracic irrigation is not well-studied. We hypothesized that thoracic irrigation after thoracostomy tube drainage of traumatic HTX would be more cost-effective compared to standard tube thoracostomy drainage.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A decision-analytic model was created to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of thoracic irrigation after thoracostomy tube placement for traumatic HTX. Our base case was a 38-year-old hemodynamically stable patient presenting with a traumatic HTX requiring thoracostomy tube placement on presentation. Cost, probabilities, and utilities were obtained from the published literature, with cost represented in 2025 US dollars. Utilities were represented in Quality-Adjusted Life Years (QALY's). One-way sensitivity analysis was performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The decision-analytic model identified that thoracic irrigation after thoracostomy tube placement for traumatic HTX was the dominant strategy with lower cost at $17,818 with QALY 0.69 compared to no irrigation at $34,527 with QALY 0.67. The strategy of thoracic irrigation demonstrated an increased net monetary benefit compared to no irrigation ($51,086 vs $32,581) with increased QALY. Using one-way sensitivity analysis, thoracic irrigation was cost-effective when its net monetary benefit surpasses $33,581.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In hemodynamically stable patients, adoption of routine thoracic irrigation for traumatic HTX is cost-effective providing additional benefit at less cost. Adoption of this management strategy should be strongly considered as it may reduce cost and improve quality of life, in addition to previously demonstrated improvement in clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Clinical equipoise as inclusion criterion to control for confounding in observational studies.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: This study investigates whether higher levels of expert disagreement, as a proxy for clinical equipoise, are associated with improved baseline comparability between treatment groups in patients with proximal humerus fractures. Additionally, it aimed to assess how progressively stricter inclusion criteria-based on this disagreement-affect the distribution of baseline characteristics between the treatment groups.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We used data from the LADON Humerus study, a multicentre, prospective cohort including patients treated operatively or non-operatively in five hospitals in the Netherlands and Switzerland. An international expert panel of trauma surgeons assessed anonymized cases, blinded to the actual treatment, and each expert gave a treatment recommendation. Disagreement between the treatment given and the expert recommendations was categorized into four levels (A: complete disagreement, B: partial disagreement, C: partial agreement, D: complete agreement). Standardized differences (StDiff) for age, sex, ASA score, and AO classification were used to assess comparability between treatment groups across disagreement levels.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 351 patients were included in the analysis. Comparability between treatment groups improved as the level of disagreement increased. At complete disagreement (Level A), the groups were well balanced with respect to age, sex, and ASA score (StDiff ≤ 0.1). For AO classification, group comparability improved but remained insufficiently balanced at the highest level of disagreement. Stricter inclusion criteria resulted in improved balance at the cost of reduced sample size.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Using expert panel disagreement as inclusion criterion can enhance group comparability in observational research. This approach may reduce the potential for confounding when RCTs are not possible.

articles.title: A Case of Hemorrhagic Shock Due to Abdominal Hemorrhage in Hemophilia A: The Role of Laboratory Medicine in Multidisciplinary Team.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Spontaneous abdominal hemorrhage due to hemophilia A is one of the most lethal complications, progressing rapidly and potentially leading to hemorrhagic shock or death.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We report a case of a 38-year-old male patient with hemophilia A who presented with massive spontaneous abdominal hemorrhage, leading to a large hematoma and severe hemorrhagic shock. Upon admission, the patient showed unstable vital signs and a significant decline in hemoglobin levels, indicating an extremely perilous condition that required immediate multidisciplinary collaborative intervention.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A multidisciplinary team was assembled, including specialists from emergency medicine, intensive care, hematology, cardiothoracic surgery, laboratory medicine, and radiology. The team quickly diagnosed active abdominal hemorrhage and performed successful catheter-directed arterial embolization. Despite ongoing hemoglobin decline after the procedure, the multidisciplinary team employed targeted laboratory monitoring and assessments to identify underlying causes and adjust coagulation factor replacement and transfusion strategies, effectively stabilizing hemoglobin levels. During recovery, the patient developed progressive jaundice, which was determined to be due to the absorption of the large hematoma, thus preventing unnecessary invasive procedures.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This case underscores the importance of a multidisciplinary approach in managing complex critical conditions and highlights the vital role of laboratory medicine in accurate diagnosis, decision-making, and management of complications.

articles.title: Emergency use of monoplace hyperbaric chamber to treat two patients simultaneously.

abstract.text: Objective: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) chambers are classified as monoplace chambers accommodating one patient and multiplace chambers capable of treating multiple patients simultaneously. Patient and Methods: A 68-year-old woman and her 42-year-old daughter began baking bread in an oven at a bakery. One hour later, they developed headaches and dizziness but continued baking and subsequently experienced difficulty moving. They were discovered later by family members and transported to our hospital by ambulance. Upon arrival, the mother's and daughter's carboxyhemoglobin (CO-Hb) levels were 22.6% and 15.6%, respectively. Transfer to the multiplace hyperbaric chamber facility would have taken approximately 90 minutes by emergency vehicle; therefore, both were treated simultaneously in the monoplace hyperbaric chamber in our facility. Results: After HBOT, both women's symptoms resolved and CO-Hb levels decreased to 1.4%. The mother, who experienced more severe symptoms, was admitted to the hospital and discharged the following day. Conclusions: This case involved simultaneously performing HBOT in two patients with acute carbon monoxide poisoning using the monoplace hyperbaric chamber as an emergency measure; the treatment was completed without issue. When treating two patients using a monoplace hyperbaric chamber, close physical contact is necessary, and realistically, treatment would be difficult unless the patients are relatives.

articles.title: End-of-life care for older adults receiving home medical care in Japan: a pilot retrospective cohort study.

abstract.text: Objective: Home medical care plays an important role in supporting aging and dying in one's preferred place. However, little is known regarding end-of-life (EOL) care among older adults receiving home medical care. This study aimed to describe the EOL characteristics in this population and identify factors associated with dying at home. Patient/Materials and Methods: In this retrospective cohort study, we used clinical data derived from a single home medical clinic in Tokyo, Japan. The study participants were adults aged ≥65 years who had received home medical care and died between April 2016 and October 2022. Demographic characteristics, clinical conditions, long-term care needs, family caregiving arrangements, advance care planning (ACP), hospitalizations, emergency department visits, and place of death were extracted from medical records. Logistic regression analysis was performed to examine factors associated with home death. Results: Of the 85 patients included in this study (mean age, 91.8 ± 7.3 years; 69.4% female), almost half had received home medical care for ≥5 years, and most required a high level of long-term care. Dementia was identified as the most common underlying condition. ACP was conducted for 75.3% of participants, whereas only 31.8% had living will documents. Home was the most frequent place of death (42.4%), followed by hospitals (32.9%) and residential facilities (24.7%). Multivariable logistic regression analysis revealed a significant association between conducting ACP and a higher likelihood of dying at home (odds ratio, 5.48; 95% confidence interval, 1.29-23.3). In contrast, no significant associations were detected between a home death and possession of a living will document, hospitalization, or emergency department visits. Conclusion: The findings of this study highlight the importance of ACP discussions involving patients, families, and healthcare professionals in supporting end-of-life care, which is consistent with the preferences of older adults.

articles.title: Assessing the effectiveness of surfactants on the treatment of gas embolism in microfluidic networks mimicking microvasculature.
articles.journal_full: Journal of colloid and interface science

abstract.label: HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: Gas embolism -reported as rare, but often lethal or with devastating neurological outcomes- occurs when gas bubbles obstruct blood flow and oxygen delivery to vital organs. Immediately after its genesis, a resilient membrane comprising surface-adsorbed biomolecules present in blood slows gas dissolution back in the liquid phase. Consequently, therapeutic and prevention strategies could focus on microscale interfacial processes instead of, or in addition to the present, macroscale hyperbaric oxygen therapy. Surfactants can modulate the evolution and dynamics of gas bubbles by preventing bubble coalescence, decreasing bubble volume, and facilitating intravascular displacement.

abstract.label: EXPERIMENTS
abstract.text: Conventional in vivo testing of pharmacological agents is challenging due to ethical, logistical, and reproducibility constraints, motivating the search for alternative strategies. Here we report the design, fabrication, and operation of a lab-on-a-chip platform mimicking human microvasculature, which enables in situ investigation of gas embolism-like events by monitoring the impact of Pluronic F-127, a surfactant approved for in vivo medical use, on gas bubble parameters, i.e., average volume and velocity, spatial distribution across vascular bifurcations, temporal accumulation, extent of coalescence, and hematocrit distributions, modulated by varying blood pressure, hematocrit concentration, and blood vessel geometry.

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: The results demonstrated that Pluronic F-127 significantly reduced gas bubble size and the risk of vessel occlusion, and its effects could be directly compared with those of other pharmacological agents. The analysis using Weber, Capillary, and Euler dimensionless numbers indicates that the addition of surfactant significantly decreases the likelihood of bubble entrapment, supporting the case of surfactants being further explored as viable alternative or adjunct strategies for the prevention and therapy of gas embolism.

articles.title: Exploratory evaluation of a medical vision-language model for electrocardiographic detection of acute coronary occlusion.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.text: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly explored for clinical interpretation tasks. Electrocardiographic (ECG) identification of acute coronary occlusion (ACO) is a high-risk application requiring accurate pattern recognition, and medical VLM performance on this task remains poorly characterised outside benchmark datasets.,Methods: A medical-domain VLM (MedGemma 1.5) was tested between 30 January and 22 February 2026 using 15 de-identified 12‑lead ECGs: 14 source-labelled ACO or high-risk occlusion phenotypes and one normal control. Each ECG was submitted with a standardised prompt requesting a structured interpretation and overall concern level (low, intermediate, or high), without iterative prompting. The same ECGs were submitted to a general-purpose VLM comparator (Gemini 3.1 Pro).,Results: MedGemma 1.5 assigned low concern in 8/15 cases (53%) and intermediate concern in 7 (47%); no case reached high concern, including among the 14 high-risk ECGs. It under-recognised ST-segment elevation, failed to integrate reciprocal and territorial patterns, and missed hyperacute T-wave morphology. Conduction abnormalities and quantitative parameters were assessed inconsistently. The comparator assigned high concern to all 14 high-risk cases but also to the normal control, citing an incorrect ECG pattern.,Conclusion: A medical VLM showed clinically important interpretation failures and did not escalate concern in any high-risk ECG. A general-purpose comparator was more consistent across high-risk cases but misclassified the normal control, suggesting some failure modes may not be modelspecific. These findings support task-specific validation and governance before multimodal AI is deployed in time-critical cardiovascular settings.

articles.title: Trauma governance and system maturity: A cross-national analysis of authority, funding, enforcement, and surveillance in 37 countries.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Organized trauma systems reduce mortality, yet most countries lack such systems and among those that exist, maturity varies widely. While the World Health Organization (WHO) emphasizes governance components including authority, funding, enforcement, and surveillance, empirical evidence linking these elements to measurable system outcomes is absent. We hypothesized that trauma governance entities (TGE) would demonstrate a dose-dependent association with WHO's Trauma System Maturity Index (TSMI) scores after adjusting for macro-economic resources.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: WHO reports, peer-reviewed literature, and national trauma registry publications spanning 2017-2024 were used to perform a cross-sectional analysis of 37 countries representing all World Bank regions and three income tiers (lower-middle, upper-middle, high). TSMI scores were assigned to four TSMI domains: prehospital care, facility-based care, education/training, quality assurance. For each nation, a composite mean TSMI score was calculated. A novel TGE score (0-4) was created to assess four domains: authority, funding, enforcement, surveillance (AFES). Spearman correlation and multivariable ordinary least-squares regression adjusting for income level, injury mortality rate (IMR), and system type were employed to assess associations between AFES and system maturity. The primary effect estimate was the contrast between countries with any governance component present (AFES≥1) and countries with none (AFES=0).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 37 nations, 15 (41%) nations had a TGE. Nations with a TGE demonstrated lower median IMR per 1000 persons (6.9 [IQR 5.2-8.1] vs 22.2 [IQR 8.7-34.9], p = 0.002) and higher composite TSMI scores (3.50 [IQR 3.25-4.00] vs 3.00 [IQR 1.81-3.44], p = 0.003). TSMI did not increase monotonically across AFES categories (median 2.25, 3.25, 3.88, 2.50 and 3.50 for AFES=0 through AFES=4). In an adjusted OLS model, countries with any governance components present (AFES≥1) had TSMI scores 0.66 points higher than countries with no governance components (β=0.66, 95% CI [0.13, 1.18], p = 0.016).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Trauma governance, operationalized through establishment of AFES domains, is strongly associated with trauma system maturity with the difference concentrated between countries that have no formal governance and those that have any. Establishing any formal governance structure may be a particularly high-yield, scalable target to improve trauma system outcomes, especially in high-burdened, lower-middle income nations.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Prognostic and Epidemiological; Level III.

articles.title: A tourniquet is a good thing for continued arterial bleeding in a severely traumatized lower limb.
Predictors of prolonged emergency department length of stay in severely injured pediatric patients.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Prolonged emergency department length of stay (ED-LOS) in severely injured pediatric patients has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes. The determinants of the prolonged length of stay in severely injured pediatric patients remain incompletely understood.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study aims to identify patient-, injury-, and system-level predictors of prolonged ED-LOS among severely injured pediatric trauma patients. Data for this analysis were obtained from a multicenter trauma registry.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively analyzed prospectively collected data from the Abu Dhabi Trauma Registry over a 10-year period (2014-2023). Patients included were under 18 years old with an Injury Severity Score (ISS) over 12. We defined prolonged ED-LOS as more than 4 h. We analyzed demographic, clinical, institutional, and temporal variables. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of prolonged ED-LOS.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We included 874 pediatric patients, with a median ED-LOS of 227.5 min. Prolonged ED-LOS was independently associated with treatment in teaching hospitals (OR 2.25, 95% CI 1.43-3.55), absence of trauma team activation (OR 2.08, 95% CI 1.35-3.22), and non-local nationality (OR 1.66, 95% CI 1.12-2.45). Prolonged ED-LOS was also linked to specific injury mechanisms: road traffic collisions (OR 13.89, 95% CI 1.75-110.00) and low-height falls (OR 13.87, 95% CI 1.68-114.73). Higher injury severity was associated with a decreased likelihood of prolonged ED-LOS (OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.92-0.96). The model showed acceptable discrimination (AUC 0.733).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Prolonged ED-LOS in severely injured pediatric patients was primarily associated with system-level factors, specifically trauma team activation and hospital characteristics. Additionally, injury mechanisms and demographic factors contributed to prolonged ED-LOS. Optimizing trauma activation protocols and workflow processes, particularly in teaching hospitals, may reduce ED-LOS and improve the efficiency of pediatric trauma care.

articles.title: Human Trafficking and Exploitation in Pediatric Acute Care: Recognition, Communication, and Response.

abstract.text: Human trafficking and exploitation of children are recognized pediatric public health concerns. Children and adolescents who experience trafficking may present to pediatric acute care settings with injuries, sexually transmitted infections, pregnancy concerns, malnutrition, substance use, chronic pain, behavioral health crises, delayed care, or non-specific somatic symptoms. Disclosure is uncommon, and clinical recognition depends on awareness of risk factors, careful observation, trauma-informed communication, and clear response pathways. Pediatric clinicians should avoid relying on stereotypes or expecting patients to self-identify as trafficked. Instead, clinicians can use developmentally appropriate and nonjudgmental questions, ensure privacy when safe, use professional interpreters, and involve multidisciplinary partners. This article provides a practical approach for pediatric clinicians in emergency department, urgent care, hospital, inpatient settings, and outpatient clinics to recognize possible trafficking, communicate safely, avoid common pitfalls, and connect children with appropriate protection and support.

articles.title: Patient Perspectives on Offers of Buprenorphine in the Emergency Department.

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Buprenorphine reduces mortality in opioid use disorder (OUD), and emergency department-initiated buprenorphine (EDIB) doubles 30-day treatment retention, yet many patients decline EDIB when offered. Patient-driven factors limiting uptake are not well characterized.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To identify factors associated with patients accepting or declining EDIB.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: Convergent parallel mixed-methods qualitative study conducted from May 1 to December 31, 2023, with data analyses performed from March 2025 to April 2026, at 4 emergency departments within the National Drug Abuse Treatment Clinical Trials Network (CTN) in South Carolina, Michigan, and Ohio. Adult patients (aged ≥18 years) with OUD who were offered buprenorphine by clinical staff were eligible; prisoners and patients concurrently enrolled in other CTN trials of OUD treatment or overdose prevention were excluded.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: The main outcomes were acceptance or declination of EDIB; validated measures of treatment readiness (Stages of Change Readiness and Treatment Engagement Scale [SOCRATES]), cultural mistrust, perceived discrimination, and social needs; and qualitative interview themes regarding reasons for accepting or declining buprenorphine.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eighty-two participants completed the study (median [IQR] age, 38 [31-53.5] years; 52 male [64%]). Overall, 19 participants (23%) declined buprenorphine. Among 54 participants who described reasons for accepting EDIB, motivators for accepting EDIB included assistance with opioid withdrawal (37 [69%]), desire to be substance free (21 [39%]), wanting to return to a "normal life" (15 [28%]), fear of overdose or death (13 [24%]), and caring for children (7 [13%]). Among 22 participants who described reasons for declining EDIB, barriers included concern about precipitated withdrawal or adverse effects (11 [50%]), not wanting to be physically dependent on buprenorphine (7 [32%]), and housing and logistical barriers (5 [23%]). SOCRATES treatment readiness (1-5 scale) was similar in patients who accepted (mean [SD] score, 4.11 [0.55]) and declined (mean [SD] score, 4.05 [0.50]) EDIB.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: In this mixed-methods qualitative study of adult ED patients with OUD who were offered buprenorphine, declination was driven less by low treatment readiness than by specific, addressable concerns: precipitated withdrawal, physical dependence, and housing and logistical barriers. Targeted interventions addressing these concerns may increase uptake of this life-saving treatment.

articles.title: Pediatric perineal trauma: a prospective observational study of mechanisms, surgical management, and outcomes.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Paediatric perineal trauma is uncommon but may involve the genital, urinary, anorectal, and pelvic-floor structures. Accurate assessment and individualized reconstruction are essential to preserve function and achieve satisfactory anatomical and cosmetic outcomes. This study evaluated the mechanisms, injury patterns, surgical management, and outcomes of surgically managed paediatric perineal trauma.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective observational study included consecutive children with perineal trauma requiring surgical management at the Children's Hospital and University of Child Health Sciences, Lahore, between October 2020 and October 2021. All patients underwent examination under general anaesthesia, with vaginoscopy, cystoscopy, or proctoscopy performed according to the suspected anatomical involvement. Injuries were categorized using the Genital Injury Score. Functional and cosmetic outcomes were assessed during follow-up.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-eight children were included; the median age was 6 years (range, 1-11), and 21 (75.0%) were female. Falls onto objects accounted for 15 injuries (53.6%), road traffic accidents for nine (32.1%), and child sexual abuse for four (14.3%). Seven patients had GIS Grade I injuries, three Grade II, five Grade III, five Grade IV, and eight Grade V. All road traffic accident-related injuries were GIS Grade III-V. Vaginoscopy, cystoscopy, and proctoscopy were performed in 21, 11, and 16 patients, respectively. Primary repair was undertaken in 22 patients (78.6%), while six (21.4%) required delayed reconstruction. Eleven patients underwent anal sphincter repair. Three adverse outcomes occurred. Anal sphincter function was good in 23 patients (82.1%), weak in four (14.3%), and absent in one (3.6%). No vaginal stenosis was identified during follow-up.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Examination under general anaesthesia with selective endoscopic evaluation enables accurate assessment of surgically managed paediatric perineal trauma. Primary anatomical repair is feasible in most patients, while delayed reconstruction and selective diversion may be required for infected or complex injuries. Structured multidisciplinary management can achieve favourable functional and cosmetic outcomes.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence Echocardiographic Interpretation in the Emergency Department: Agreement, Interpretation Yield and Reporting Scope.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To assess the agreement between artificial intelligence (AI) interpretation and expert emergency physician sonologist review of echocardiograms performed in the Emergency Department (ED).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective multicentre agreement study in four Australian EDs. A total of 195 echocardiograms (2016-2023) underwent three-stage adjudicated human expert review. Human reports were compared with us2.ai reports. Agreement across 10 validated parameters was reported as percentage exact match with 95% confidence intervals and kappa under two pre-specified tiers: Guideline Compliant (GC; ASE/EACVI multi-view criteria) and Pragmatic (PR; any available measurement). Reference standard reliability was quantified.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Pooled agreement was 76% at both tiers (GC n = 875; PR n = 1323); AI returned an interpretation in 46% of evaluations at GC and 70% at PR. Four structural parameters reached 78%-87%: right atrial size 87% (κ = 0.62), right ventricular (RV) contractility 83% (κ = 0.42), left ventricular (LV) size 83% (κ = 0.52) and RV size 78% (κ = 0.37). Binary LV systolic agreement was 79% GC and 83% PR. Expert reviewers agreed on 85% of interpretations. Pericardial effusion, aortic regurgitation and mitral stenosis, present in 7%-20% of patients, are not reported in the current us2.ai algorithm.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: AI agreed with expert review in about three-quarters of evaluations but provided a guideline-compliant interpretation in less than half; a pragmatic approach raised yield to 70% at the same agreement. The AI withheld classifications that experts could reach; its validated scope covers only part of what ED echocardiography must address, and reports did not mark unassessed parameters. This study reports agreement, not accuracy. For now, human expert review of AI reports is required.

articles.title: Predictors of 48-h Pain-Related Re-Presentation Following Emergency Department Discharge: A Multicentre Retrospective Case-Control Study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aimed to identify patient and clinical factors associated with 48-h pain-related re-presentation following ED discharge across four metropolitan emergency departments.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective matched case-control study across four public EDs in Western Sydney Local Health District between September and December 2024. Adult patients presenting with a primary complaint of pain were eligible. Cases were patients who re-presented within 48 h with a pain-related complaint, matched to up to four controls on hospital site, pain location and age. Binomial and conditional logistic regression were performed to identify independent predictors of re-presentation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 876 participants were included (179 cases, 697 controls). Findings were consistent across both models. Pain score documentation was most strongly associated with re-presentation (binomial aOR 7.90, 95% CI 5.35-11.66; conditional aOR 25.50, 95% CI 12.90-50.43). Mental health comorbidity was independently associated with increased odds of re-presentation (binomial aOR 2.48, 95% CI 1.40-4.38; conditional aOR 2.43, 95% CI 1.23-4.81). Discharge opioid prescribing was inversely associated with re-presentation after adjustment (binomial aOR 0.53, 95% CI 0.34-0.83; conditional aOR 0.47, 95% CI 0.26-0.83).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Pain score documentation and mental health comorbidity were most strongly associated with re-presentation, though the binary nature of the pain score variable renders this finding hypothesis-generating. Pain location and triage category were not independently associated with re-presentation. The crude opioid association may partly reflect confounding by indication; the inverse adjusted association warrants cautious interpretation and prospective investigation.

articles.title: Reengineering the Concept of Emergency Care.
articles.journal_full: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine

abstract.text: Emergency departments (EDs) absorb most acute unscheduled care (AUC) in the United States. Routing all of this care through one high-intensity system serves no one well: crowding delays care for time-critical patients; visits that turn on evaluation and coordination, and routine and chronic care defined by longitudinal needs, are delivered episodically and at high cost in a setting built for resuscitation and stabilization; and clinicians trained for emergencies spend much of their time on work the category does not fit. I argue that this is not only a capacity or workflow problem but a conceptual one. In practice, "emergency care" is defined by arrival: crossing the ED threshold, not clinical risk, triggers the legal duties, insurance protections, and workflows attached to the label. This was no one's mistake; routing everything through the one door always open was a rational adaptation to a fragmented system. But the adaptation no longer merely persists; it forecloses alternatives. Using conceptual engineering, I trace how history, regulation, payment, public scripts, and lexical entrenchment stabilize this system, and situate it against the social drivers that make ED-as-default ethically necessary and operationally costly. I then propose an ameliorated concept of emergency care: a risk- and time-sensitive, expert-mediated, priority-conferring subset of AUC, determined by structured triage wherever it occurs. Because a definition changes nothing by itself, I outline a phased implementation pathway, show how it applies across delivery settings, including rural and safety-net systems where the ED should remain the local acute care hub, and describe the workforce implications for emergency medicine. The choice posed to the specialty is whether to keep treating crowding, mismatched care, and clinician dissonance as operational problems to optimize within the ED, or to recognize them as properties of what we mean by emergency care and of the system that enacts it.

articles.title: Open Posterolateral Elbow Dislocation in an Adult after Low-Energy Trauma: A Case Report Highlighting Diagnostic and Operative Considerations.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Open elbow dislocations are rare injuries in adults, accounting for <2% of cases, and may occur even after low-energy mechanisms. Their presentation can be subtle, particularly when periarticular wounds appear benign, leading to delayed recognition of joint violation. Early identification of intra-articular air and associated soft-tissue injury is essential to guide timely operative management. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges and surgical considerations associated with an uncommon open posterolateral elbow dislocation following a low-energy fall.

abstract.label: CASE REPORT
abstract.text: A middle-aged man presented after slipping and landing on an outstretched right arm, resulting in a posterolateral elbow dislocation with an associated medial elbow laceration. The joint was reduced in the emergency department, and the wound was irrigated and repaired. Subsequent computed tomography (CT) imaging revealed intra-articular air concerning for an open dislocation. The patient underwent operative irrigation and debridement, during which complete avulsion of the flexor pronator mass from the medial epicondyle was identified and repaired. The elbow remained stable intraoperatively and was immobilized in a long arm splint.

abstract.label: RESULT
abstract.text: The patient received 24 h of intravenous antibiotics and was discharged the following day. At 2 weeks' follow-up, he began a range of motion exercises, and by 4 weeks demonstrated excellent motion and a stable elbow joint. He continued non-surgical management with favorable early recovery.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Open elbow dislocations in adults may occur after low-energy trauma and require a high index of suspicion, particularly when periarticular wounds are present. CT evaluation for intra-articular air is critical for identifying joint violation, and early operative washout with soft-tissue repair is essential to prevent infection and instability. This case underscores the importance of timely recognition and management to achieve optimal functional outcomes.

articles.title: The Safety and Interventions for Redirecting Non-Urgent Patients From Emergency Departments to Primary Care Services: A Scoping Review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency departments (EDs) experience overcrowding, resulting in delayed care for life-threatening conditions, increased healthcare costs, and prolonged waiting times. Non-urgent patients contribute to ED overcrowding, and redirecting these patients to primary care (PC) is a strategy to reduce pressure on emergency services. However, the safety and procedural components of redirection have not been comprehensively described due to limited evidence. This scoping review aimed to identify the safety outcomes and intervention components associated with redirecting non-urgent patients from EDs to PC.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Five electronic databases were searched. Eligible studies included non-urgent patients presenting to EDs who were redirected to PC, reported safety outcomes, and described redirection procedures. Two reviewers independently conducted title and abstract screening and full-text screening using Rayyan.ai and assessed study quality. Safety outcomes included return visits, hospitalisation, death, and adverse events, which were compared across studies. Redirection procedures were identified using the Innovation domain of the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR).

abstract.label: MAIN RESULTS
abstract.text: Nine studies met the inclusion criteria, including eight observational studies and one randomised controlled trial. The highest reported safety outcomes were a 9.7% return rate, a 1.7% hospitalisation rate, and a 0.07% mortality rate. Most reported components across all studies included documentation of chief complaints, patient registration, measurement of vital signs, and triage. Studies reporting zero hospitalisations and deaths included multiple constructs within the CFIR Innovation domain.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Redirecting non-urgent patients from EDs to PC appears safe and acceptable when clear criteria are implemented; however, evidence remains limited.

articles.title: A Retrospective Descriptive Analysis of Consultations Provided by the National Poisons Centre Relating to Medicines on the Aotearoa New Zealand Antidote Stocking Guideline, 2020-2025.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Many antidotes are relatively rare-use, indication-specific medicines with a variable evidence base. In Aotearoa New Zealand, there are no national statistics available on their use. This study aimed to characterize the numbers of cases and advice provided by the Aotearoa New Zealand National Poisons Centre (NZNPC) on the use of true antidotes and antidote-adjacent medicines to treat poisonings from 2020 to 2025.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The numbers of NZNPC medical/clinical toxicologist consultations advising on the use of antidotes and antidote-adjacent medicines were determined and data categorized by health region, the caller type of healthcare provider and the numbers of cases advising for and against the use of specific medicines.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Consultations occurred in 2952 exposure incidents with hospital-based clinicians comprising 2800 (95%); covered all regions; and consisted of advising on use of individual antidotes/adjacent medicines 3408 times. N-acetylcysteine (1371; 40%) and charcoal (775; 23%) were most frequently discussed. Of relatively high-cost antidotes, NZNPC advised against use of fomepizole in 22/58 (38%) and digoxin-binding antibody in 36/74 (49%) cases. Of labour-intensive interventions, NZNPC advised against use of high-dose insulin euglycemic therapy in 52/89 (58%) and whole bowel irrigation in 68/135 (50%) cases.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: There was use of the NZNPC consultation service across all regions, and the recommendations provided for each antidote ranged from mostly in favour of use to mostly against use based on the patient presentation. Utilizing a specialist medical/clinical toxicologist consultation service may assist in rationalizing care and optimizing use of healthcare resources.

articles.title: PROMOTED-EM: Shifting Focus From Cataloging Barriers to Identifying Hidden Determinants of Advancement for Women in Academic Emergency Medicine.
articles.journal_full: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine

abstract.text: Gender disparities in academic promotion persist despite decades of research documenting their scope. Women remain underrepresented at senior academic ranks in Emergency Medicine, with only 19% of full professors identifying as women. Existing literature has largely cataloged the barriers driving this gap-disproportionate clinical workloads, non-promotable labor burden, sponsorship deficits, and caregiving responsibilities-but has devoted comparatively little attention to the strategies women use to successfully navigate these barriers. This commentary proposes a shift in research focus: From documenting the problem to systematically studying the hidden determinants of advancement among women who have achieved promotion. We introduce PROMOTED-EM, a qualitative research framework organized across 14 domains of academic career life, designed to elicit the tactical, behavioral, and relational strategies that enabled promotion. By centering the experiences of successfully promoted women in Emergency Medicine while explicitly attending to intersectionality and the limitations of survivor bias, this agenda aims to generate actionable, evidence-based guidance for women faculty, department leaders, and institutions committed to closing the promotion gap.

articles.title: SECURE: A Cognitive Scaffold for Post-Intubation Sedation and Analgesia in the Emergency Department.
articles.journal_full: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine

articles.title: Characteristics, Practice Patterns, and Outcomes of Emergency Department Intubation for Sepsis: An ANZEDAR Registry Study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Sepsis is a leading cause of critical illness in Australia and New Zealand, with over 75% of admissions occurring through emergency departments. This study aimed to characterise the demographics, process of care, pharmacology, and peri-intubation adverse events of sepsis intubations using a prospective Australasian registry.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from the Australian and New Zealand Emergency Department Airway Registry (ANZEDAR) was performed across 79 hospitals between January 2010 and March 2026. Intubations performed for a primary indication of sepsis were identified. A paediatric subgroup analysis was performed stratified by age band. Statistical comparisons used Mann-Whitney U tests for continuous variables and chi-square or Fisher's exact tests for categorical variables.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 11,289 registry intubations, 280 (2.5%) were performed for sepsis. Paediatric patients with confirmed age under 16 years comprised 30 of 280 sepsis intubations (10.7%). Adults were older, more haemodynamically compromised, and had longer triage to intubation times than non-sepsis patients across all age groups. Laryngoscopic views and first-pass success were comparable between sepsis and non-sepsis groups. Haemodynamic complications occurred in 27.9% of sepsis intubations and peri-intubation cardiac arrest in 4.6%. Waveform capnography was used less frequently in sepsis versus non-sepsis groups (87.5% vs. 94.1%; p < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Emergency department sepsis intubation is associated with high rates of haemodynamic complications despite similar laryngoscopic views and first-pass success rates. Low waveform capnography use in infant sepsis represents a potential patient safety concern. These findings support targeted interventions.

articles.title: A Systematic Review of Interventions to Support Health, Wellbeing, and Job Satisfaction for Emergency Call Handlers in the Ambulance, Police, and Fire Services.
articles.journal_full: Stress and health : journal of the International Society for the Investigation of Stress

abstract.text: Emergency call handlers (ECH) in ambulance, police, and fire services experience high levels of occupational stress which can have adverse health consequences. To systematically review interventions to support the health, wellbeing and employment of ECH working in the emergency services. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, academic databases and grey literature were searched [Last search: 06/02/25]. Studies of any design assessing physical or mental health or employment outcomes were eligible. Screening and quality appraisal were conducted independently, with data extraction completed and cross checked by two reviewers. The JBI family of tools was used to assess quality and risk of bias. Twelve studies met the inclusion criteria and were narratively synthesised into four categories: psychoeducation and resilience training, residential recovery programme, organisational wellbeing initiatives, and multicomponent interventions. Sample sizes ranged from n = 9 to n = 4020. The majority of interventions identified aimed to improve mental health, while physical health and employment outcomes were less frequently assessed. There was significant heterogeneity in study design which limited comparability between the studies. Most studies included a mixed sample of ECH and first responders and the methodological quality of included studies was variable. Some studies employed rigorous designs (e.g., RCTs), whilst others relied on observational methods. The included studies also demonstrated organisational barriers to the delivery of interventions in these settings. There was limited evidence for the effectiveness of interventions for supporting health and wellbeing or reducing stress amongst ECH. There is a need for role-specific interventions for ECH. SYSTEMATIC REGISTRATION: This systematic review was registered on PROSPERO: CRD42025639271.

articles.title: Risk Stratification of Acute Pulmonary Embolism: Outcomes in Patients With Intermediate sPESI Scores and Negative Cardiac Biomarkers.
articles.journal_full: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Current pulmonary embolism (PE) guidelines support outpatient management for selected low-risk patients, typically identified using the simplified Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index (sPESI). The prognostic value of individual sPESI scores in the direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) era, particularly when combined with cardiac biomarker assessment, remains uncertain.

abstract.label: RESEARCH QUESTION
abstract.text: To evaluate 7-day and 30-day all-cause mortality among patients with acute PE, sPESI scores of 2 or 3, and negative cardiac biomarkers treated with a DOAC.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort study of US adults diagnosed with acute PE in a VA emergency department and prescribed a DOAC within 24 h of diagnosis at any U.S. Veterans Affairs (VA) Health System from 2015 to 2024.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
abstract.text: Seven-day and 30-day all-cause mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 6427 eligible patients, 1365 had an sPESI score of 2 and 455 had an sPESI score of 3 with negative cardiac biomarkers. In the sPESI 2 cohort, 7-day and 30-day mortality were 0.44% and 1.39%, respectively. In the sPESI 3 cohort, rates were 0.22% and 2.20%. Approximately 71% of sPESI 2 patients and 75% of sPESI 3 patients were hospitalized. Hospitalization was not associated with lower 7-day or 30-day mortality in either cohort.

abstract.label: INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Patients with acute PE, sPESI scores of 2 or 3, and negative cardiac biomarkers had low short-term mortality in this large, contemporary DOAC-treated cohort. These findings support prospective studies evaluating outpatient management in carefully selected patients.

articles.title: Pre-hospital fluid resuscitation and return of spontaneous circulation in earthquake victims with cardiac arrest during the first 24 hours after the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes: Implications for disaster risk management.
articles.journal_full: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Earthquakes can cause crush injuries and post-extrication deaths. Hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis, hypovolemia, and circulatory failure are key mechanisms of cardiac arrest in victims at risk of crush syndrome. Although intravenous fluid resuscitation is recommended in disaster care, evidence on resuscitation outcomes remains limited. This study evaluated earthquake victims with cardiac arrest during the first 24 h after the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes and examined the association between pre-hospital fluid resuscitation, admission metabolic parameters, and return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center retrospective study was conducted in the emergency department of a tertiary hospital in Mersin, Türkiye. Adult earthquake victims admitted within the first 24 h who developed cardiac arrest before or after emergency department arrival were included. Patients with fatal head, thoracic, or abdominal injuries or missing data were excluded. Initial admission blood gas values were analyzed. The primary outcome was ROSC.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty-seven patients were included. The mean age was 49.30±18.63 years, and 20 patients (54.1%) were female. Pre-hospital fluid resuscitation was administered to 25 patients (67.6%), with a mean volume of 1540±611 mL. Patients receiving fluids had higher pH and lower lactate, potassium, and base excess values. ROSC occurred in 10 patients (27.0%), all of whom had received fluids (p=0.010).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Pre-hospital fluid resuscitation was associated with a more favorable metabolic profile and higher ROSC rates in earthquake-related cardiac arrest. These findings support field-based fluid resuscitation and hyperkalemia management in disaster response planning; however, causality cannot be inferred.

articles.title: Simulation-based evaluation of emergency medicine residents' preparedness for toxic terrorism.
articles.journal_full: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Toxic terrorism is a rare but potentially catastrophic threat that can result in mass casualties and overwhelm healthcare systems. Effective management of such incidents requires specialized clinical competencies and preparedness that may be underemphasized in standard emergency medicine training. This study aimed to assess emergency medicine residents' competencies in toxic terrorism preparedness and emergency medical management using a structured simulation-based examination.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Emergency medicine residents working in the emergency departments of two tertiary university hospitals in Trabzon participated in a simulation-based clinical assessment. The examination comprised five realistic, fully immersive objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) stations designed to evaluate diagnostic decision-making and treatment planning in toxic terrorism scenarios. Each station was scored using standardized checklists developed by medical toxicologists. Factors associated with improved performance were also examined.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Although 33.3% of participants successfully passed the botulism scenario (Station 3), no participant successfully completed all five stations. The radiation exposure scenario (Station 2) was the most challenging. Higher performance was significantly associated with having more than 24 months of residency training, prior chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) training, and previous exposure to simulation-based education.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: These findings suggest that current training may not adequately prepare emergency medicine residents to manage toxic terrorism incidents. Incorporating standardized simulation-based assessments, such as OSCEs, into residency curricula may help identify training gaps and improve preparedness for low-frequency, high-impact events.

articles.title: Ocular trauma presentations to a tertiary emergency department: Demographic characteristics, injury mechanisms, and clinical outcomes.
articles.journal_full: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: This study aimed to evaluate the demographic characteristics, etiological factors, associated injuries, and clinical outcomes of patients presenting to a tertiary emergency department with ocular trauma.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective observational study included 6,557 patients who presented to the Emergency Department of Süleyman Yalçın City Hospital with ocular trauma between 2022 and 2025. Demographic data, trauma mechanisms, physical examination findings, associated injuries, need for surgical intervention, and clinical outcomes were evaluated. Categorical variables were analyzed using the chi-square test, while Student's t-test and the Mann-Whitney U-test were used for continuous variables.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of the patients, 85.4% (n=5,598) were male, and 52.9% were aged between 20 and 39 years. The most common reason for presentation was ocular foreign body injury (88.9%), and the most frequent physical examination finding was corneal abrasion (30.9%). Computed tomography (CT) was performed in 8.6% of cases. In 95.9% of patients, ocular trauma occurred without associated injuries, and 1.5% required surgical intervention. Overall, 97.9% of patients were discharged from the emergency department. Ocular foreign body injury (p<0.001), falls (p<0.001), traffic accidents (p=0.004), penetrating or sharp object injuries (p<0.001), and chemical injuries (p=0.002) were more frequent in males. Female sex (p<0.001), age over 60 years (p<0.001), Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score below 13 (p<0.001), and the presence of associated injuries (p<0.001) were associated with increased surgical intervention. Female sex (p<0.001), age under 9 years (p<0.001) and over 60 years (p<0.001), GCS score ≤13, presentation due to falls (p<0.001) or traffic accidents (p<0.001), and the presence of orbital or extraocular bone fractures (p<0.001) were associated with higher hospitalization rates.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Ocular trauma predominantly affected young males and was most commonly caused by foreign bodies. Corneal abrasion was the most frequent finding. Most cases involved isolated ocular trauma, did not require CT, and were discharged from the emergency department. Female sex, pediatric and geriatric age groups, low GCS scores, and trauma related to falls or traffic accidents were associated with increased surgical intervention and hospitalization.

articles.title: Spontaneous splenic rupture in a patient with congenital factor XIII deficiency: A case report and literature review.
articles.journal_full: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES

abstract.text: Spontaneous (atraumatic) splenic rupture is a rare but potentially life-threatening clinical condition. Most reported cases of spontaneous splenic rupture are associated with splenomegaly due to infectious, neoplastic, or inflammatory diseases. Spontaneous rupture in the absence of these conditions is extremely rare. There is often an underlying trauma history. Factor XIII deficiency, a rare autosomal recessive bleeding disorder, is associated with abnormal fibrin stabilization despite normal routine coagulation parameters. Therefore, it can also lead to defects in wound healing. For the same reason, spontaneous splenic rupture has rarely been reported in patients with Factor XIII deficiency. We report a 32-year-old male with congenital Factor XIII deficiency who presented to the emergency room with hypovolemic shock following sudden-onset abdominal pain. The case was complicated by spontaneous splenic rupture and severe intra-abdominal bleeding. Contrast-enhanced abdominal computed tomography revealed a large perisplenic hematoma. Despite intensive blood transfusion and replacement therapy with fresh frozen plasma and cryoprecipitate, the patient required surgical intervention, and a splenectomy was performed. Histopathological examination revealed no underlying splenic pathology. Spontaneous splenic rupture is extremely rare in patients with factor XIII deficiency, but it should be considered in the differential diagnosis in this patient group presenting with an acute abdomen. Suspicion, early recognition, and supportive care with appropriate blood products and factors, along with prompt surgical intervention, are crucial to prevent mortality.

articles.title: Trauma-related simultaneous asymmetric bilateral hip dislocation: A case report.
articles.journal_full: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES

abstract.text: Trauma-related simultaneous asymmetric bilateral hip dislocations (SABHDs) are extremely rare cases. High-energy trauma plays a role in their etiology. Traumatic hip dislocations account for 2-5% of all dislocations. Of all hip dislocations, 90% are posterior and 10% anterior. Bilateral traumatic hip dislocation is exceedingly rare. Asymmetric dislocations are even rarer, accounting for approximately 0.01-0.02% of all joint dislocations. This study aimed to evaluate a patient with trauma-related SABHD through a case presentation and discuss therapeutic options. A 27-year-old male patient was diagnosed with dislocation of both hips (left hip anterior and right hip posterior) following high-energy trauma. The patient was prepared for general anesthesia under emergency conditions and was taken to the operating room 2 h after admission to the emergency department without waiting for the fasting period. Under general anesthesia, left anterior and right posterior hip dislocations were reduced using the Allis and Boehler maneuvers. Direct radiography, computed tomography, and spiral tomography performed after the procedure demonstrated a successful reduction in both hips. While no bony pathology was observed in the right hip, a small fracture of the anterior acetabular wall and a non-displaced fissure line in the subcapital region of the femoral head were detected in the left hip; however, surgical intervention was not considered for either pathology. Since SABHD is caused by high-energy trauma, patients should be managed with a multidisciplinary approach. To prevent or minimize potential complications, the dislocations must be reduced as soon as possible.

articles.title: Prognostic Significance and Factors Associated With Worsening LV Dilatation in Heart Failure.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Left-ventricular end-systolic dimension (LVESD) and end-diastolic dimension (LVEDD) are associated with adverse outcomes in heart failure (HF). The prognostic significance of a change in LVESD or LVEDD is uncertain.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study included patients experiencing ≥ 1 HF hospitalization or emergency department (ED) visit between April 2008 and March 2016 and underwent ≥ 2 echocardiograms, separated by ≥ 6 months.
