The primary outcome was the composite all-cause mortality, HF hospitalization, and ED visits for HF. We performed cut-point analysis to determine the threshold increase in LVESD or LVEDD associated with all-cause mortality. We evaluated characteristics associated with an increase in LVESD and LVEDD above threshold using multivariable logistic regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We included 8790 patients, 56.1% were male, with a mean (SD) age of 70.9 (14.5). The thresholds for change in LVESD and LVEDD associated with all-cause mortality were -3.13% and 1.33%, respectively. Patients with ischemic cardiomyopathy and lower LVEF were at increased risk of a change in LV size above the threshold. There was a significant association between an increase in LVESD or LVEDD above threshold and the composite outcome (HR 1.13; 95% CI 1.06, 1.20; HR 1.07; 95% CI 1.01, 1.13, respectively). An increase in LVESD or LVEDD above threshold was associated with increased risk of HF hospitalization (HR 1.27; 95% CI 1.15, 1.39; HR 1.24; 95% CI 1.12, 1.36) and an increased risk of ED visits for HF (HR 1.25; 95% CI 1.15, 1.37; HR 1.16; 95% CI 1.06, 1.26).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Small adverse changes in linear dimensions of LVESD and LVEDD are clinically significant in patients with HF.

articles.title: Escalating Concerns in Paediatric Hospital Care: A Qualitative Study of Involvement, Support and Empowerment of Families From Culturally and Linguistically Diverse Backgrounds.
articles.journal_full: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Families frequently recognise early signs of deterioration in their children. In English-centric environments, families from culturally and linguistically diverse (CALD) backgrounds face challenges in escalating concerns in hospital because of language barriers, limited health literacy, uncertainty about escalation pathways, and variable staff responsiveness. Although digital approaches may support communication, it remains unclear whether they address the wider organisational conditions required for equitable escalation of care.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study explored hospital experiences of CALD families and investigated their views on a potential digital tool to escalate acute clinical concerns during their child's hospitalisation.

abstract.label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
abstract.text: This qualitative study was guided by a multicultural consumer advisory group. Families from CALD backgrounds participated in semi-structured focus groups and one-to-one interviews, conducted in English or with interpreters. Audio-recordings were transcribed, de-identified and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty-four parents/carers representing 34 distinct families and 15 CALD backgrounds participated in 11 focus groups and two individual interviews. Three themes were identified: (i) communicating is not easy; (ii) shaping health system satisfaction; (iii) communicating using digital tools. Families described both supportive and challenging interactions with health staff and the system. Positive experiences were associated with plain language, clear explanations, and inclusive communication. Negative experiences included not feeling heard when raising concerns, inconsistent access to interpreters, unclear information about how to escalate concerns, and distress associated with waiting and uncertainty in emergency care. Although some families saw the value in digital tools, particularly for translation, rapid communication, and access to information, they consistently prioritised broader service changes. These included routine offers of interpreter support, clearer explanations of hospital processes, more detailed information about their child's condition and treatment, and a more welcoming environment for asking questions and raising concerns.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Families viewed digital tools as potentially useful, but not sufficient on their own. Inequities in escalation of care were shaped not only by language discordance, but also by wider organisational conditions, including inconsistent interpreter access, unclear escalation pathways, variable staff responsiveness, and limited opportunities for families to feel heard. System change is therefore essential if digital approaches are to support equitable escalation of care in hospital settings for these families.

abstract.label: LIVED EXPERIENCE OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION
abstract.text: A consumer and community involvement was integral to the study. A Multi-Cultural Consumer Advisory Group (MCAG), comprising six members from CALD backgrounds (China, Egypt, India, Russia, Sierra Leone, and Vietnam), contributed to study design, recruitment planning, interpretation of findings, and refinement of the developing intervention. MCAG members also supported recruitment by sharing study information with their communities.

articles.title: Heliox versus trimix in closed-circuit rebreather diving: A comparative study of pulmonary and decompression stress in male divers.

abstract.text: Closed-circuit rebreather (CCR) and helium-based breathing mixtures are widely used in technical diving. This study compared the effects of Heliox and Trimix on pulmonary function and decompression stress during CCR dives. Nineteen divers performed a standardized dive (50 ± 3 msw, 147 ± 10 min) using Heliox (16% O2/84% He; n = 9) or Trimix (16% O2/32% He/52% N2; n = 10). Pre- and post-dive venous gas emboli (VGE), pulmonary function, lung ultrasound, heart rate variability, and inflammatory parameters were assessed. VGE were detected in all Heliox divers but in only 50% of Trimix divers. Heliox exhibited higher VGE counts 45 min post-dive than Trimix (12 [IQR 3-32] vs. 0 [IQR 0-6], p = 0.03); this difference disappeared by 90 min. No clinically significant pulmonary function changes were observed. Lung diffusion capacity decreased moderately regardless of breathing gas (-6% ± 7%). Lung ultrasound revealed minor transient B-line changes. Dive induced mild inflammatory responses, including neutrophilia and increased MRP8/14 in both groups. Heliox divers also showed transient complement activation alongside increased circulating platelets. CCR dives induced limited pulmonary stress, without gas-dependent differences. Although Heliox may promote a higher post-dive VGE burden and inflammatory responses, the relationship between these physiological effects and decompression sickness risk remains uncertain.

articles.title: Global Research Highlights.
[Planning for the Possible in Healthcare: From PEIMAF to the Management of the Unknown.].

abstract.text: This paper examines the evolution of healthcare planning in light of the increasing complexity of contemporary emergencies, which are characterized by high levels of uncertainty and the frequent absence of established interpretative models. Starting from the historical role of Hospital Emergency Plans for Mass Casualty Incidents (PEIMAF), the article highlights the limitations of approaches based solely on known scenarios and proposes a conceptual shift toward managing the unknown. It outlines the need to broaden the operational meaning of PEIMAF, extending it to all types of patients and transforming the concept of a "plan" into a dynamic process of developing decision-making capacity. Within this framework, a model structured on two integrated levels is proposed: an operational level, grounded in continuous training and practical exercises, and a decision-making level, focused on adaptability, experimentation, and the development of new solutions in uncertain contexts. Particular attention is given to strengthening decision-making skills through training pathways based on complex, multidisciplinary, and highly variable simulations, aimed at fostering proactive and adaptive capabilities. The paper ultimately emphasizes that the resilience of healthcare systems lies in the quality of decisions made under uncertainty, highlighting the need for a cultural and organizational evolution that integrates planning, training, and decision-making capacity to ensure effective responses to future crises.

articles.title: Beyond the oscillometric cuff: the utility of point-of-care ultrasound-derived blood pressure in shock.
Human-artificial intelligence collaboration in emergency medical services: from diagnostic algorithms to shared decision support.
Utility of nano-impregnated surface coating to achieve continuous active disinfection in ICU of a tertiary trauma center.
articles.journal_full: Journal of infection in developing countries

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Implementing continuous active disinfection presents challenges as conventional cleaning methods may not fully mitigate risks. Hence, evaluating innovative technologies becomes imperative. This study assessed a nanoparticle-based surface coating containing titanium dioxide engineered into nano-molecules that is activated by normal light and provides ongoing disinfection.

abstract.label: METHODOLOGY
abstract.text: The research took place in two intensive care units (ICUs): ICU A (coated) and ICU B (control). Data on healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) and environmental factors were collected pre- and post-coating application to gauge its impact. The change in percentage of positive swabs/HAI cases in ICU A was compared to ICU B and statistically analyzed using a 2-sample test for equality of proportions.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: ICU A witnessed a 26.5% decrease in positive environment swabs post-coating, while ICU B saw a 160.9% increase. This disparity was statistically significant (p = 0.000). Both ICUs experienced decreased ventilator associated pneumonia (VAP) cases, though central line associated-blood steam infection (CLA-BSI) and catheter associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI) cases increased in ICU A post application. Following coating, positive environmental swabs and VAP decreased by 71.8%, and 72.5%, while CLA-BSI and CAUTI increased by 198% and 43.5%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The evaluation showed that the coating may serve to supplement traditional cleaning and disinfection methods. Further research into the efficacy and cost-effectiveness of such antimicrobial coating is needed for overall improvement in patient care.

articles.title: Trend analysis in hand hygiene from the early COVID pandemic to the post-COVID periods at a Tunisian University Hospital.
articles.journal_full: Journal of infection in developing countries

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The COVID-19 pandemic has further underscored the importance of Hand Hygiene (HH) adherence as an effective measure for infection prevention and control. This study aims to evaluate trends in HH practices from 2020 to 2023 and assess the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic at the University Hospital of Mahdia (Tunisia).

abstract.label: METHODOLOGY
abstract.text: From June 2020 to October 2023, annual direct observations of HH were performed among health care workers (HCWs) at Mahdia hospital based on the ''HygMain Hygiene audit'' validated by the Practice Assessment Group of Hospital Hygiene in France. Data were collected through structured observations by trained doctors and hygienists. Compliance and relevance rates were analyzed for each observation period.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 993 HH opportunities were observed across five periods from 2020 to 2023, involving 731 HCWs, predominantly paramedical staff (54.4%). Among them, 478 (65%) were female. The overall HH compliance was 22.1%, with a higher compliance rate after patient contact (28.4% vs 39%, p = 0.08). Overall, HH compliance increased significantly during the COVID-19 pandemic, peaking at 33.1% in 2022 before declining to 14.7% in 2023. Similarly, the overall HH relevance rates rose from 6.5% in 2020 to 30% in 2022, but fell to 19.4% in 2023. Compliance was higher in high-risk departments and during invasive procedures.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The study highlights the positive impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on HH, though the post-pandemic adherence rate has declined. Continuous monitoring and institutional support are essential to enhance and maintain compliance levels, ensuring long-term improvements in infection control practices.

articles.title: Intelligent Cloud Resource Usage Potentially to Improve Task Scheduling by the use of Artificial Intelligence.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The high variability of workloads makes it very difficult for cloud datacenters to efficiently schedule their tasks and resource allocation. The correct forecasting of future resource utilization allows us to proactively scale and implement more sophisticated scheduling policies, which eventually results in has potential to improve resource utilization and fewer failures.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Leveraging only data that is exposed to the scheduler at task dispatch times, this research assesses four supervised learning approaches for estimation of CPU consumption on the Google Cluster Data v3 trace: Linear Regression, Support Vector Regression, Random Forest, and a Neural Network.

abstract.label: RESULT
abstract.text: The randomized forest version gave the optimum regression performances on a held-out test set (MAE ≈ 0.00233, RMSE ≈ 0.00589, R 2 ≈ 0.895), while an ordinary hybrid composition of the two best systems performed similarly. Estimating if a task's real CPU consumption surpasses a train-set-derived high utilization threshold which was achieved up to 0.921 accuracy and ≈ 0.844 best F1, chosen via a detailed threshold sweeping as opposed to an individual set cutoff.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This approach are evaluated using RMSE, MAE, and R 2 for held-out on test set, while the 2nd threshold-based analysis is utilized to appraise the recognition of high-CPU tasks. These results underscore the potential of data driven approach definitely machine and deep learning-based CPU demand predictions as valuable tools for cloud schedulers, improving resource management, and reducing operational costs. Also discuss the feasibility of deploying the proposed solution on distributed platforms such as Spark and Google Cloud and outline future research directions to integrate predictive models with real-time cloud resource management.

articles.title: Associations of system noise with lumbar puncture and hospitalization for young febrile infants: a cross-sectional study.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Clinical decisions vary widely for young, febrile infants at risk for invasive bacterial infections. System noise characteristics (i.e., extraneous factors that influence clinical decisions) represents under-studied factors that may systematically affect clinical decisions for febrile infants.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To investigate associations between system noise characteristics and clinical decisions for febrile infants.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We used New York State's all-payer database to identify febrile infants aged 8-90 days brought to emergency departments between 2016 and 2023. Clinical decision outcomes were lumbar puncture and hospitalization. We used multivariable regression to estimate adjusted odds for each clinical decision outcome in the overall cohort and for infants aged 8-28 days, 29-60 days, and 61-90 days. System noise exposures were encounter times relative to day-of-week (i.e., weekday vs. weekend), time-of-day, and changes-of-shift.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 53,625 eligible infants, 9015 (16.8%) received lumbar puncture and 17,104 (31.9%) were hospitalized. For the overall cohort, we observed greater adjusted odds of lumbar puncture on weekdays (adjusted Odds Ratio (aOR) =1.07, 95% CI [1.02,1.13]), during the day (aOR =1.1, 95% CI [1.04,1.16]), and during change-of-shift (aOR =1.06, 95% CI [1.01,1.12]). We also observed greater adjusted odds of hospitalization on weekdays (aOR = 1.09, 95% CI [1.05, 1.14]) during the day (aOR = 1.06, 95% CI [1.01, 1.11]), and during change-of-shift (aOR = 1.34, 95% CI [1.28, 1.40]).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: System noise factors are significantly associated with clinical decisions for febrile infants. Future studies should investigate mechanisms through which observed differences arise and develop interventions to mitigate effects of system noise on clinical decisions for febrile infants.

articles.title: The impact of the Integrated Oncological Decision-Making Model (IODM) on healthcare costs and health outcomes in older patients with lower gastrointestinal tumors.
articles.journal_full: European journal of surgical oncology : the journal of the European Society of Surgical Oncology and the British Association of Surgical Oncology

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The need to transition towards Value-based Healthcare (VBHC) is becoming more apparent in the Dutch healthcare system. The Integrated Oncological Decision-making Model (IODM) extracts more value from oncological treatment and has shown to alter treatment recommendations towards less invasive treatment modalities without compromising one-year all-cause mortality. However, the impact of IODM on costs remains unclear.

abstract.label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study involved patients with lower gastrointestinal tumors treated at the University Medical Centre Groningen (2014-2016). Treatment decisions were supported by the IODM. Patients were stratified into two groups: a modified cohort (N = 24) in which the IODM led to an altered and an unmodified treatment advice (N = 44). Outcomes were in-hospital costs within 1-year post-decision making, one- and five-year all-cause mortality and hospital days. Cost data were available for 65 patients and analyzed using nonparametric bootstrap followed by an independent t-test. All-cause mortality was compared between cohorts using a Log-Rank test, while hospital days were analyzed using an independent t-test.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The mean healthcare costs in the first year after clinical decision-making were €13,901 per patient versus €25,213 in the unmodified cohort (observed difference, €11,312; 44.9% lower; p = 0.011). The estimated counterfactual cost difference for the combined cohort was €260,176 (15.9% lower, 95% CI 65,780; 456,780). Costs were significantly lower in the modified cohort for Surgery (p = 0.029); In-patient clinic (p = 0.024); Intensive Care Unit (ICU) (p = 0.012); paramedical (p = 0.015); and laboratorial (p = 0.032). There was no significant difference in one-year and five-year all-cause mortality. However, the modified cohort spent 10 days less in hospital (p = 0.027).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Modified treatment advice through the IODM was associated with €260,176 lower estimated total healthcare costs in the combined cohort (15.9% lower), a shorter length of hospital stay, and no difference in survival between the two groups.

articles.title: Evaluation of the wound healing effects of a hydrogel containing hydroalcoholic extract of Chelidonium majus in a rat model.

abstract.text: This study aimed to develop an innovative wound dressing by loading Chelidonium majus L. extract into an alginate hydrogel matrix and to assess its efficacy in wound healing. The extract of C. majus, famous for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant features, was obtained from plant material collected in Mazandaran Province, Iran, and incorporated into sodium alginate hydrogels at concentrations of 2% and 5% w/w. The hydrogel formulations were characterized in terms of their morphological, thermal, and swelling properties, demonstrating interconnected porous structures, altered thermal behavior indicating increased amorphous content, and high moisture absorption capacity. To evaluate biological activity, the antioxidant and flavonoid content of the extract were measured, showing notable free radical scavenging ability and high levels of flavonoids. An in vivo wound healing model using adult male Wistar rats compared the effectiveness of control, bare hydrogel, C. majus-loaded hydrogels (2% and 5%), and diltiazem treatments. Wounds treated with the 5% C. majus hydrogel showed accelerated closure rates and improved tissue regeneration, as confirmed by histological examination and enhanced expression of proliferative and regenerative genes (TGF-β) alongside decreased inflammatory markers (TNF-α and IL-1β), in comparison with the control group. These results indicate that C. majus-loaded alginate hydrogel, especially at a 5% concentration, promotes wound healing through offering a wet environment, supporting cell proliferation, and modulating inflammation. This hydrogel may represent a promising topical therapeutic option for treating skin wounds.

articles.title: Occlusion Myocardial Infarction Missed by ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI) Criteria: An Angiographic Emergency Department Cohort.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)/non-STEMI (NSTEMI) paradigm uses ST-elevation as a surrogate for acute coronary occlusion, but ST-elevation criteria miss many occlusions. The occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) vs. non-occlusion (NOMI) paradigm classifies patients by the presence of an acute occlusion.

abstract.label: STUDY OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To compare the 2 paradigms in an angiography-selected emergency department (ED) cohort of acute myocardial infarction.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective single-center cohort of consecutive adults given an ED diagnosis of STEMI or NSTEMI who underwent coronary angiography between December 2021 and October 2023. OMI was defined as an acute culprit lesion with thrombolysis in myocardial infarction (TIMI) 0 to 2 flow, or culprit stenosis above 70% with a peak emergency department high-sensitivity troponin I above 10,000 ng/L.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 1052 patients, 458 (43.5%) were STEMI and 594 (56.5%) NSTEMI; 837 (79.6%) met the study OMI definition. The OMI definition was met by 430 of 594 NSTEMI patients (72.4%), and 430 of 837 OMI patients (51.4%) were STEMI-negative; 51 of 458 STEMI patients (11.1%) had no occlusion. Median peak ED troponin was 155 ng/L in STEMI(+)OMI and 639 ng/L in STEMI(-)OMI (p < 0.001); median ejection fraction was 50% in both (p = 0.004). Angiography within 2 h was performed in 85.7% of STEMI(+)OMI and 15.6% of STEMI(-)OMI patients (p < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this angiography-selected cohort, more than half of the patients who met the study OMI definition were STEMI-negative, and these patients reached angiography far later than STEMI-positive patients with occlusion. Whether such patients can be recognized before angiography requires prospective validation of prespecified electrocardiogram (ECG) criteria.

articles.title: Factors associated with patient satisfaction in a Vietnamese university hospital emergency department: A cross-sectional study.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Patient satisfaction is an important indicator of emergency department (ED) quality, but evidence from low- and middle-income countries remains limited. This study evaluated patient satisfaction and associated factors in a university hospital ED in Vietnam.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A cross-sectional study was conducted at Can Tho University of Medicine and Pharmacy Hospital between June and September 2025. A total of 250 respondents (197 patients and 53 caregiver proxies) completed a structured questionnaire. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multivariable linear regression, with sensitivity analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Overall satisfaction was high, with 94.0% of respondents reporting satisfaction. The highest ratings were observed for nursing adherence to procedures (97.2%), safety and trust (96.8%), physician explanations (96.0%), and staff attitude and communication (95.2%). Lower ratings were reported for waiting time for tests/imaging (89.6%) and cost explanation clarity (91.2%). In the primary analysis, waiting time before physician assessment was the strongest predictor of overall satisfaction (β = 0.238), followed by treatment procedures (β = 0.188), hygiene and environment (β = 0.188), payment convenience (β = 0.172), and nursing adherence to procedures (β = 0.144). In the patient-only sensitivity analysis, nursing adherence to procedures showed the strongest association (β = 0.365), while the other key predictors remained broadly consistent.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Patient satisfaction was high in this university hospital ED. Waiting time before physician assessment, nursing adherence to procedures, treatment procedures, hygiene and environment, and payment convenience were associated with satisfaction; however, these relationships should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects.

articles.title: When the clock strikes eight: Nighttime admissions and worse outcomes of patients admitted with emergency general surgery conditions.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Evidence on the impact of nighttime admission for emergency general surgery (EGS) in low- and middle-income countries is limited. We evaluated the association between admission timing and inpatient outcomes at a tertiary care center.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed 32,278 adult EGS admissions from 2010 to 2019, categorized as daytime (8:00 a.m.-7:59 p.m.) or nighttime (8:00 p.m.-7:59 a.m.). Inpatient mortality was the primary outcome. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess adjusted associations.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Nighttime admissions accounted for 42.4% of cases and were more likely to originate from the emergency department. After adjustment, daytime admission was associated with lower inpatient mortality (odds ratio [OR] 0.79, 95% CI 0.68-0.92) and overall complications (OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.74-0.83). Nighttime admissions also had higher rates of sepsis, acute renal failure, pulmonary failure, and septic shock.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Nighttime admission is independently associated with worse EGS outcomes, supporting the need for targeted system-level interventions to improve off-hours surgical care.

articles.title: Abrupt versus gradual HFNC discontinuation in children: Shorter HFNC duration without increased weaning failure.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: High-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) therapy is widely used in pediatric acute respiratory distress, but evidence-based weaning protocols remain limited, and prolonged use may increase resource utilization. This study compared gradual versus abrupt HFNC weaning strategies and evaluate their clinical outcomes in children.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective observational study was conducted between September 2025 and February 2026 in an academic pediatric emergency department. Patients receiving HFNC who met predefined clinical improvement criteria [FiO2 ≤ 30%, S/F ratio > 270, and Pediatric Early Warning Score < 3] were enrolled. HFNC discontinuation strategy was determined by treating physicians according to routine clinical practice. Patients underwent either abrupt discontinuation or gradual flow reduction. The primary outcome was weaning success, defined as no HFNC re-initiation within 48 h. Secondary outcomes included HFNC duration and length of hospital stay (LOS).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eighty-seven patients were included (63.2% male), with a median age of 10 months (range 4-32). The leading diagnoses were bronchopneumonia (60.9%) and lower airway obstruction (29.9%). HFNC was discontinued abruptly in 43 patients and gradually in 44 patients. Baseline characteristics were similar between groups. Weaning failure occurred in two patients in each group. Among successfully weaned patients, HFNC duration was significantly shorter with abrupt discontinuation [59 h (IQR 44-92) vs. 87 h (IQR 61-110), p = 0.012], whereas LOS did not differ significantly (p = 0.065).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Abrupt HFNC discontinuation was associated with shorter HFNC duration by approximately 32% without increasing weaning failure. This simplified approach may improve device availability and patient flow in high-demand emergency settings.

articles.title: Experiences of emergency care practitioners on pre-hospital rapid sequence intubation in South Africa.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pre-hospital Rapid Sequence Intubation (RSI) is a complex, high-stakes and time-sensitive procedure performed in unpredictable resource-constrained environments. Successful execution of pre-hospital RSI demands coordinated teamwork, thorough preparation and clear communication.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: This qualitative study explored the experiences of Emergency Care Practitioners (ECPs) during pre-hospital RSI.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: The study was conducted across three South African provinces: Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal and the Western Cape.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The study adopted a descriptive qualitative design, using focus group discussions (FGDs) to understand ECPs' experiences during prehospital RSI. Six FGDs were conducted online via Microsoft Teams. All discussions were audio-recorded, transcribed and analysed using qualitative data analysis software, NVivo 13 (2020 R1).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 39 ECPs voluntarily participated in six FGDs, representing both public and private sectors. The following themes emerged; system-driven administrative demands and procedural complexity, resource and workforce constraints affecting RSI performance and communication-related challenges and information gaps affecting clinical decision-making.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The ECPs voice concerns about challenges that require Emergency Medical Services (EMS) management to implement supportive measures, including improved access to resources and equipment during pre-hospital RSI. Additionally, they argue that practitioner proficiency promotes the effective execution of pre-hospital RSI.

abstract.label: CONTRIBUTION
abstract.text: The findings of this study and the insights gained can guide EMS leadership and policymakers in formulating targeted strategies that will ensure the availability of essential resources and strengthen operational support to enhance the safety and quality of care delivered to critically ill or injured patients requiring RSI.

articles.title: Risk factors and interventions for patient aggression and violence towards healthcare workers: An umbrella review of emergency and psychiatric settings.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Violence against healthcare workers (HCWs) is a global concern, particularly in emergency departments (EDs) and psychiatric departments (PDs) settings. We synthesised evidence on the risk factors of patient violence towards HCWs and interventions aimed to reduce such violence and aggression.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We searched Medline, EMBASE, PsychINFO and the Cochrane of Systematic Reviews from inception to May 2025. Eligible studies included reviews examining risk factors for violence and systematic reviews of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating interventions in EDs and PD settings. Risk factor reviews were assessed using AMSTAR 2, while individual RCTs were assessed using the PEDro scale. Two researchers independently conducted screening, data extraction, and quality assessment. We summarised and conducted meta-analyses where data allowed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Our study included 18 reviews of risk factors and 23 reviews examining interventions (47 RCTs). Violence was linked to patient demographics (e.g., male sex), clinical (e.g., psychiatric symptoms severity), staff (e.g., experience), organisational (e.g., overcrowding), and other factors (e.g., day of the week). Multicomponent organisational and behavioural interventions (e.g., Safewards, screening, staff training, de-escalations, environmental improvement) were most effective to reduce violence against HCWs. Pharmacological interventions were effective for acute agitation response, olanzapine demonstrated clinically meaningful short-term reductions in aggression compared to placebo and clozapine showed the strongest evidence for sustained effect.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Violence towards HCWs in EDs and PDs is a function of patient, staff, and organisational factors. Evidence supports trauma-informed multicomponent prevention strategies, while evidence-based clinical acute cases management can be effective to improve safety for HCWs.

articles.title: Risk of mortality after emergency department presentation for self-harm among children and adolescents in Wales: a population-based cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Self-harm in childhood and adolescence is associated with substantial morbidity and premature mortality, particularly from suicide. We aimed to quantify the risk of cause-specific and all-cause mortality following emergency department (ED) presentations for self-harm.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this retrospective population-based cohort study, we used anonymised, linked electronic health records from the Secure Anonymised Information Linkage (SAIL) Databank. We included children and adolescents aged 5-18 years who presented to EDs in Wales between 2008 and 2023. Individuals with at least one ED presentation for self-harm were assigned to the exposed group, and those with no recorded self-harm presentations formed the comparison group. Follow-up began at the index ED presentation and continued until death, possible emigration, or end of data availability. The primary outcome was suicide; secondary outcomes included accidental death, other causes of death, and all-cause mortality. Associations between self-harm and cause-specific mortality were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age and sex. Kaplan-Meier failure curves (1 - survival) were estimated separately for each cause of death.

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: Between 2008 and 2023, we identified 611,336 young people who presented to EDs, of whom 14,007 (2.3%) had at least one self-harm presentation. During follow-up, 1451 deaths were recorded. Mortality was higher among those presenting with self-harm compared with controls without self-harm presentations (114 [0.8%] vs 1337 [0.2%], adjusted hazards ratio [aHR] 3.1, 95% CI 2.6-3.8). Suicide risk was markedly elevated in the first year after presentation (aHR 13.4, 95% CI 4.7-38.0) and remained increased during follow-up (aHR 4.9, 95% CI 3.4-6.9). There was a similarly increased risk of accidental death within one year (aHR 13.9, 95% CI 6.2-31.1) and after one year (aHR 5.5, 95% CI 3.9-7.7). No clear association between self-harm and other causes of death was observed.

abstract.label: INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: ED presentation for self-harm identifies young people at elevated risk of premature mortality. Preventive interventions should extend beyond suicide alone to address accidental deaths, particularly in the period immediately following presentation.

abstract.label: FUNDING
abstract.text: McGill Global Health Programs Fellowship; John Fell Fund; NIHROxford Health Biomedical Research Centre; Academy of Medical Sciences; UK Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy.

articles.title: Optimizing massive transfusion protocol activation: A new decision tool based on a Dutch trauma cohort.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Most trauma centres have implemented a massive transfusion protocol (MTP) to facilitate the rapid transfusion of blood products. However, identifying patients who require transfusion remains challenging, which often results in overactivation. The primary objective of this study was to identify patient-related factors that could be used to accurately predict justified MTP activation, defined by the administration of at least 1 transfusion product after MTP activation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this retrospective cohort study trauma patients for whom the MTP was activated in the Erasmus Medical Centre, Rotterdam, The Netherlands, from January 2018 until November 2024 were eligible for inclusion. Exclusion criteria were children, interhospital transfers and inaccessible patient files. Variables with the highest discriminative ability to accurately predict justified MTP activation were used to create a new decision tool. This new decision tool was compared with existing decision tools.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 463 patients were included, 198 justified and 265 unjustified MTP activations. The variables and their cut-off points used for the new decision tool were pH ≤ 7.25, lactate ≥4.6 mmol/L, SBP ≤ 105 mmHg, DBP ≤ 60 mmHg, PP ≤ 45 mmHg, HR ≥ 110 beats per minute, temperature ≤ 35.8 °C, and a positive eFAST. This resulted in 92.1% sensitivity, 55.8% specificity, 60.4% positive predictive value and 90.6% negative predictive value.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Patient-related factors to predict justified MTP activation were identified. With these variables, a new decision tool was developed that accurately predicted the need for MTP activation and could potentially diminish overactivation.

articles.title: Safety net primary care for emergency physicians: Diagnosis and treatment of non-critical hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.text: Hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism are common in the emergency department, both as established diagnoses and newly identified conditions. Thyroid function tests are also frequently obtained during ED evaluations. This article reviews the diagnosis and management of non-critical thyroid disorders, with a focus on clinically relevant guidance from endocrinology and primary care literature. It provides emergency physicians with a practical approach to interpreting thyroid function tests, initiating treatment for overt hyper- and hypothyroidism when appropriate, and bridging patients to primary and specialty care follow-up.

articles.title: Missed opportunities for HIV prevention: Low linkage to follow-up care after emergency department initiation of nonoccupational postexposure prophylaxis.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: HIV non-occupational post-exposure prophylaxis (nPEP) utilizes antiretroviral medications to reduce HIV acquisition risk and is commonly initiated in emergency departments (EDs). Little is known about the linkage to follow-up care and related outcomes for patients initiated on nPEP from an ED. We evaluated the linkage to care for patients initiated on nPEP in the ED at University of Nebraska Medical Center (UNMC) and were referred to the Specialty Care Center (SCC) for follow-up screenings.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults prescribed nPEP at the UNMC ED between 1/1/2023-6/30/2024. Patients with prior HIV infection or those seeking occupational post-exposure prophylaxis were excluded. The primary outcome was the completion of a follow-up visit at the SCC within 90 days. Secondary outcomes included documented completion of a 28-day nPEP course, adherence to screening guidelines, and factors associated with successful linkage to care. Outcomes were compared using descriptive statistics, Chi-square, and independent t-tests.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 92 patients, 65 were scheduled for nPEP follow-up visits at SCC, but only 23 attended their visit. Guideline-recommended nPEP regimens were prescribed for 98.7% of patients, but only 2.2% had all guideline-recommended baseline screenings. Overall, only 21 patients had documented completion of nPEP at their SCC follow-up visit. Follow-up attendance was more likely among those with commercial insurance (p = 0.012) and a lower social deprivation index (p = 0.043).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: There was low (25%) nPEP follow-up attendance at SCC visits. Attendance disparities linked to insurance and social deprivation underscore the need for improved processes to improve overall continuity of transitions of care.

articles.title: Comparative preclinical evaluation of an investigational topical hemostatic formulation against an active commercial comparator in rat arterial, venous and liver bleeding models under normal and heparinized conditions.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: An ideal topical hemostatic agent should provide rapid hemostasis, maintain clot stability after manipulation, and preserve a clean operative field. These requirements become particularly relevant under anticoagulated conditions and across different bleeding anatomies.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the preclinical performance of a topical hemostatic agent compared with a commercial comparator and saline control in standardized rat arterial, venous, and liver bleeding models under normal and heparinized conditions.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A total of 144 adult male Wistar albino rats were allocated to 18 groups (n = 8 per group). Standardized abdominal aortic, vena cava, and liver bleeding models were established under normal and heparinized conditions. Vascular injuries were created with a 21 G needle and liver injury with a standardized 6 mm × 5 mm incision. Treatment was followed by a standardized 3-minute compression protocol. The primary endpoint was time to hemostasis. Liver blood loss was assessed gravimetrically. Rebleeding tendency and operative field quality were evaluated qualitatively.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: One-way ANOVA demonstrated overall between-group differences in time to hemostasis in all model-condition combinations (all P < 0.001). Across all anatomical models and coagulation settings, the investigational hemostatic agent consistently showed the shortest mean time to hemostasis, whereas saline-treated controls showed the longest times. Pairwise post hoc comparisons showed significantly shorter time-to-hemostasis values for the investigational agent than for the commercial comparator in four of the six model-condition comparisons; in the remaining two comparisons, the mean time-to-hemostasis values were numerically lower but not statistically significant. In the liver model, mean blood loss was numerically lowest in the investigational groups under both normal and heparinized conditions, although between-group differences were not statistically significant. Descriptive qualitative observations suggested cleaner operative fields and less post-manipulation rebleeding in the investigational groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this standardized multi-model rat study, the investigational topical hemostatic agent showed consistently shorter mean time-to-hemostasis values across arterial, venous, and liver bleeding models under both normal and heparinized conditions. Liver blood loss was numerically lower in the investigational groups, but the between-group differences were not statistically significant. These findings support further confirmatory preclinical evaluation.

articles.title: Neck pain patient with a final diagnosis of bilateral vertebral artery tears: A case report.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The purpose of this case report is to present atypical red flags for vertebral artery tears in a young adult with neck pain.

abstract.label: CLINICAL FEATURES
abstract.text: A 24-year-old female patient presented with acute neck pain 4 days after waterskiing. Pain extended from the suboccipital muscles to the cervicothoracic junction. She had visual disturbances described as "fans" in the peripheral vision bilaterally. Orthopedic and neurological examination was unremarkable except for the inability to reproduce the symptoms and a guarded range of motion.

abstract.label: INTERVENTION AND OUTCOME
abstract.text: Initial chiropractic treatment consisted of gentle manual soft-tissue massage and Kinesio Tape, both over the cervicothoracic junction, and a referral for medical evaluation. Four days later, the patient went to the emergency department, where a computed tomography scan was performed and revealed a tear in the vertebral artery at C3/C4 on the left and C4/C5 on the right. Anticoagulants were administered, and referral to a specialty clinic, where another computed tomography scan was performed to confirm the diagnosis. The specialty clinic prescribed Plavix for 6 months and aspirin for life.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This case report emphasizes that not all patients with vertebral artery tears present with classic stroke symptoms. Using this clinically recommended risk-benefit assessment strategy may help mitigate risk related to the broad differential diagnosis of neck pain.

articles.title: An evidence-informed occupational health curriculum for pre-deployment preparation of aquanauts in underwater habitats: a scenario-based framework development study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Underwater habitats represent emerging extreme workplaces in which pressure exposure, immersion, confined living, external underwater tasks, and delayed access to definitive care create combined occupational health and safety demands. Candidate selection establishes baseline suitability. It cannot, on its own, specify which preventive and response capabilities should be taught, practiced, and documented between selection and deployment.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We developed a scenario-based, evidence-informed occupational health curriculum for the pre-deployment preparation of non-medical research personnel. The design case was deliberately narrow. It placed three to six crew members in a 15-m habitat for 14 days, with topside telemedical support and limited immediate specialist care. Peer-reviewed studies and official manuals were mapped to mission phases, occupational and operational risk events, expected actor actions, and feasible non-medical performance. No Delphi round or validation study was undertaken. Internal project documents only defined the scenario.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The occupational health curriculum specification contains four domains, ten modules, and 28 observable learning outcomes. Emergency preparedness, physical self-maintenance, psychological and team functioning, and underwater operational safety are separated by immediate performance purpose. Together, the domains connect worker protection across routine prevention, acute response, psychosocial risk management, and task-specific safety. Three modules carry the psychological and team content. Sleep and circadian management, emotional self-regulation, and crew communication with conflict management are each specified on their own.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This article offers a preliminary occupational health curriculum for pre-deployment preparation that underwater habitat programs can adapt. It is evidence-informed and unvalidated. The framework addresses worker protection within a bounded underwater workplace while preserving the authority of diving, clinical, and mission-governance systems. Independent stakeholder review, instructor usability testing, pilot training, and analog-mission observation remain necessary before the framework informs any operational readiness decision.

articles.title: Point-of-care lactate in pediatric sepsis: a single-center observational study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Lactate is a key biomarker in the assessment of sepsis, reflecting tissue hypoperfusion and correlating with disease severity and outcomes. However, reliance on standard laboratory testing may delay clinical decision-making in time-sensitive situations. Point-of-care (POC) lactate testing provides rapid bedside assessment, potentially facilitating earlier risk stratification and intervention. This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of POC lactate for pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admission and mortality in pediatric patients with sepsis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a retrospective observational study of children aged 3 months to 14 years presenting to the pediatric emergency department in a tertiary care children's hospital with a diagnosis of sepsis. Data were extracted from electronic medical records.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 149 pediatric patients with sepsis were included, of whom 90 underwent POC lactate testing. Elevated POC lactate levels were observed in 38.9% of tested patients. Elevated POC lactate was significantly associated with PICU admission, as well as the need for mechanical ventilation and inotropic support. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis demonstrated modest but statistically significant predictive performance for PICU admission (AUC = 0.641), whereas no predictive value was observed for mortality (AUC = 0.544).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Point-of-care lactate may serve as a practical supplementary biomarker that can facilitate early risk stratification by identifying children with sepsis at increased risk of PICU admission and requiring advanced interventions. Nevertheless, its modest discriminatory performance necessitates interpretation in conjunction with clinical assessment and additional biomarkers rather than as an independent predictor of sepsis severity.

articles.title: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy in sepsis-associated encephalopathy: pathophysiological rationale, preclinical evidence, and translational challenges.

abstract.text: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a serious neurological complication of sepsis that can cause acute cerebral dysfunction and long-term cognitive impairment. Its pathogenesis involves multiple pathological processes, including blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption, neuroinflammation, microglial and astrocytic responses, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, ferroptosis, and pyroptosis. Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and mitochondrial injury can aggravate cerebrovascular endothelial and BBB damage, promote glial inflammatory responses, and contribute to lipid peroxidation and inflammasome activation, thereby linking neuroinflammation with regulated cell death. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) increases tissue oxygen tension and may exert neuroprotective effects by improving microcirculation and regulating redox homeostasis and inflammatory responses. Available animal studies of SAE suggest that HBOT may attenuate certain aspects of BBB injury and hippocampal neuroinflammation and improve neurobehavioral and cognitive outcomes. Findings from systemic sepsis and other neurological injury models further suggest that antioxidant responses, mitochondrial homeostasis, and signaling pathways associated with ferroptosis and pyroptosis may contribute to these effects. This review summarizes the cellular and molecular processes potentially affected by HBOT within the major pathological mechanisms of SAE and discusses its therapeutic potential and translational challenges based on the available direct and supportive evidence. Current evidence remains predominantly preclinical, and the mechanisms and clinical value of HBOT in SAE require further investigation.

articles.title: Diagnostic challenges in posterior circulation ischemic stroke presenting with acute dizziness and vertigo.

abstract.text: Posterior circulation stroke (PCS) is a common and clinically important cause of acute dizziness and vertigo, accounting for approximately 20-25% of all acute ischemic strokes. Because PCS frequently presents with non-specific, fluctuating, or isolated vestibular symptoms, it is about three times more likely to be initially missed in emergency care than anterior circulation stroke (ACS), with important consequences for acute treatment, secondary prevention, and patient outcomes. Diagnostic evaluation is further complicated by the low sensitivity of prehospital stroke scales for posterior fossa syndromes, the under-representation of PCS deficits on the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), and the limited early sensitivity of non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) and diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (DWI-MRI) in the posterior fossa. In contrast, structured bedside assessment can improve recognition when applied by trained clinicians. However, no single diagnostic pathway covers all patients with PCS presenting with acute dizziness and vertigo: the Head Impulse, Nystagmus, and Test of Skew examination (HINTS) and its extension with bedside hearing assessment (HINTS+) require spontaneous or gaze-evoked nystagmus, gait and posture-based approaches require relevant postural instability, and a clinically relevant subgroup presents with neither. This review outlines the main diagnostic challenges along the care pathway and highlights practical opportunities to improve recognition and reduce missed PCS in patients presenting with acute dizziness and vertigo.

articles.title: Concussion symptom clusters and changes in symptom reporting and severity following multiple concussions in male professional rugby league players.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Symptom reporting remains an important part of the diagnosis and management of concussion. Understanding the patterns of symptoms and symptom clusters in athletes with multiple concussions may be clinically valuable. The purpose of this study was to characterise acute symptom reporting in players with multiple concussions.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: National Rugby League (NRL) players who have sustained multiple concussions between the 2017 and 2022 seasons were included in the study. Data included the symptoms reported on the Sport Concussion Assessment Tool - 5th Edition (SCAT5) during the Head Injury Assessment by players who were subsequently diagnosed with concussion. K-means clustering with k = 6 centres was performed on symptom severity data. Each concussion episode was assigned to one symptom cluster based on the athlete's symptom presentation. Transitions between symptom clusters from initial to subsequent concussions were visualised using a Sankey plot.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 120 players who sustained more than one concussion, including 75 players with two, 23 with three, 15 with four, and 7 players with five or more medically diagnosed concussions. The average duration between concussions was 441 days (SD: 332; Md: 370; range: 11-1435 days). There were 6 different symptom clusters identified. Players were commonly found to transition between clusters for subsequent concussions, most commonly the 'Asymptomatic' cluster. There was no relationship found for days between concussions and symptom count or severity. Symptom severity, but not symptom count, was associated with days until medical clearance.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Acute symptom reporting varies with subsequent concussions, making it difficult to predict post-concussion symptoms in individual players. Acute symptom severity was associated with time to medical clearance, whereas the number of concussions in the preceding two years was not.

articles.title: Climate and air pollution are associated with pediatric respiratory hospitalizations in São Paulo, Brazil.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Environmental and climatic factors have been associated with pediatric respiratory diseases, but these associations may vary across specific clinical outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a hospital-based study in the Metropolitan Area of São Paulo, Brazil, using pediatric emergency department visits and hospitalizations recorded in 2022. Residential addresses were geocoded and individual environmental exposures were estimated through inverse distance weighting (IDW) interpolation of air pollution and meteorological data. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations between environmental factors, seasonality, and two respiratory outcomes: bronchiolitis and unspecified acute respiratory infections.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Higher ozone levels, relative humidity, and spring seasonality were significantly associated with greater odds that a respiratory encounter corresponded to hospitalization for bronchiolitis (O3: OR = 1.012; 95% CI 1.005-1.019; relative humidity: OR = 1.016; 95% CI 1.005-1.027). For unspecified acute respiratory infections, lower temperatures were associated with greater odds that a respiratory encounter corresponded to hospitalization for this diagnosis (OR = 0.887; 95% CI 0.793-0.993), while greater odds were also observed during spring. Other environmental variables showed positive but non-significant associations.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Environmental and climatic factors showed differential associations with pediatric respiratory diseases. Disaggregating outcomes may improve the identification of disease-specific patterns of association and support targeted public health strategies in urban settings.

articles.title: Septic shock in the era of precision medicine: rethinking fluids, vasopressors, and immunomodulation.

abstract.text: Septic shock remains a high-mortality syndrome despite advances in early recognition, antimicrobial therapy, source control, and protocolized resuscitation. A major limitation of current practice is that septic shock is often managed as a single clinical entity, whereas patients meeting the same diagnostic criteria may differ substantially in hemodynamic phenotype, endothelial injury, microcirculatory function, immune state, coagulation activation, fluid tolerance, and vasopressor responsiveness. These differences help explain why biologically plausible therapies frequently fail when tested in unselected populations. This narrative review synthesizes evidence supporting a precision-oriented approach to septic shock across three therapeutic domains-fluid therapy, vasopressor support, and immunomodulation-supported by two cross-cutting precision layers: biological phenotyping and bedside precision tools. We distinguish bedside clinical phenotypes from biological endotypes and explain how this framework can refine resuscitation decisions. Fluid therapy is reframed as a titrated intervention requiring assessment of both fluid responsiveness and fluid tolerance. Vasopressor therapy is discussed beyond a uniform mean arterial pressure target, with emphasis on timing, agent selection, tissue perfusion, and individualized weaning. Immune, endothelial, and coagulation phenotyping are presented as biological bridges between bedside physiology and targeted therapy, while immunomodulation is considered a promising but still investigational frontier requiring patient stratification. Finally, we propose a pragmatic precision-resuscitation framework that integrates lactate kinetics, capillary refill time, point-of-care ultrasound, congestion assessment, and immune/endothelial biomarkers where available. Precision care should not delay time-critical sepsis interventions; rather, it should mature protocolized management into a dynamic process of early treatment, repeated reassessment, and phenotype-directed adjustment.

articles.title: Oxygen-augmented erythrocyte-liposome hybrids to overcome paclitaxel resistance in triple-negative breast cancer metastasis via enhanced ferroptosis.

abstract.text: Paclitaxel (PTX) resistance in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is closely associated with ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters-medicated drug efflux and hypoxia-driven upregulation of hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α), which together promote tumor progression and metastasis. Although blood transfusion or hyperbaric oxygen therapy can partially alleviate systemic hypoxia, neither approach effectively relieves chemoresistance driven by intratumoral hypoxia. To address this challenge, we have developed a biomimetic hybrid delivery system (red blood cell hitchhiking-liposomes encapsulate hemoglobin and paclitaxel, RBC-LEHP) that utilizes red blood cell-hitchhiking technology along with pH-responsive liposomes, to co-deliver hemoglobin (Hb) and PTX to overcome hypoxia-associated chemoresistance. This system achieves dual-stage targeting: passive sequestration in pulmonary metastatic lesions through erythrocyte hitchhiking and active tumor internalization mediated by pH-sensitive DOPE phospholipids. Our study revealed that RBC-LEHP effectively alleviated the hypoxia microenvironment through Hb-mediated oxygenation upon tumor cellular internalization and downregulated HIF-1α and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), while simultaneously enhancing reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated lipid peroxidation to induce ferroptosis. This amplified oxidative stress further triggered mitochondrial dysfunction, suppressed P-glycoprotein (P-gp)-mediated PTX efflux, reversed PTX resistance, and promoted apoptotic cell death. In vivo results confirmed that RBC-LEHP-mediated therapeutic cascade of "lung targeted delivery → hypoxia alleviation → ferroptosis/chemotherapy → tumor suppression" significantly enhanced antitumor efficacy against TNBC. This biomimetic platform provides a promising strategy for overcoming physiological barriers and chemoresistance in metastatic TNBC therapy.

articles.title: Maternal psychological distress, breast milk extracellular vesicles, and infant immunity: A translational study.

abstract.text: Distress during early postnatal life has a potential impact on maternal mental health and related biological systems. However, the potential biological roles of these systems' modifications remain largely unknown. Bronchiolitis represents a life-threatening condition for infants and a possible stressful event for mothers with an impact on maternal breast milk composition and potentially on infants'health. In this framework purposes of the present study were: a) to evaluate the impact of infants' severe bronchiolitis on maternal mental health; b) to examine the correlation between maternal mental health status and extracellular vesicles (EVs) in breast milk; c) to explore the impact of breast milk EVs modification on the infant's innate immunity. We hypothesize that severe infant illness acts as a maternal stressor, which in turn remodels the composition of breast-milk EVs, thereby modulating immune response in the infant affected by bronchiolitis. A prospective, observational study with a case-control design and a longitudinal observation component was conducted. The case group included dyads of mothers and infants, with the infants admitted to the pediatric emergency department for severe bronchiolitis, while the control group consisted of healthy mother-infant dyads. The two groups were evaluated at baseline (admission for bronchiolitis for cases) and after one month. In both the appointments clinical data including mental health status by validated scales and a breast milk sample were collected. Biological analyses included extracellular vesicles (EVs) isolation and characterization, and the use of zebrafish to study the EVs-mediated modulation of innate immunity. Baseline mental health assessment revealed markedly higher scores in the case group for depressive symptoms (p < 0.01) and state anxiety (p < 0.01). These symptoms ameliorated over time in the case group. At baseline, cases showed higher concentrations of CD177+ EVs compared to controls (p = 0.02). Among T cell-derived EVs, CD4+ vesicles were significantly more abundant in cases than controls at follow-up (p = 0.04). At baseline maternal functioning was inversely associated with several EV subtypes. Finally, the treatment of zebrafish embryos with baseline EVs of cases with low level of anxiety resulted in a significant increase in neutrophil recruitment. This study suggests the existence of a complex interplay between stressful events, maternal mental health and innate immune modulation of infants with an acute infectious disease. New studies are needed to confirm the results of the present research.

articles.title: Point-of-care ultrasound in emergency department sepsis and septic shock: a pragmatic framework for source-oriented assessment and physiologic reassessment.

abstract.text: In emergency department (ED) sepsis and septic shock, early management is often dominated by two bedside uncertainties: identifying a clinically plausible infection source and determining whether additional fluid is likely to improve perfusion or worsen pulmonary or systemic congestion. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) may contribute to both questions when it is used as a trigger-based, time-boxed adjunct rather than as a comprehensive screening test or stand-alone diagnostic adjudicator. This article presents a pragmatic narrative review of multiorgan POCUS in adult ED sepsis and septic shock, based on a focused, non-systematic search of major databases and a synthesis of sepsis guidelines, landmark resuscitation trials, and clinically relevant reviews and representative studies addressing source-oriented assessment, shock phenotyping, fluid responsiveness, and congestion assessment. Particular attention was given to separating diagnostic capability and physiologic plausibility from demonstrated clinical utility and patient-centered outcome benefit. Priority was given to adult ED literature; intensive care unit (ICU), perioperative, and physiologic studies were used only when ED-specific evidence was limited and the underlying principles were clinically transferable. The proposed framework is organized around two linked arms. First, a source-oriented scan may support pneumonia or pleural complication as a working source and may identify biliary disease, obstructive urinary infection, urinary retention, or drainable soft-tissue infection when clinical features make these sources plausible. Its intended role is to trigger formal imaging, drainage planning, specialist consultation, or source-control pathways, not to prove the source at the bedside. Second, physiologic reassessment can use focused cardiac ultrasound (FoCUS), dynamic flow-based assessment such as passive leg raise with left ventricular outflow tract velocity-time integral (PLR-LVOT VTI), and serial lung ultrasound to provide context for fluid and vasopressor decisions after the initial resuscitation step. Venous Doppler and the venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) framework are discussed as optional advanced congestion assessments, not as routine ED requirements, because ED sepsis-specific evidence remains limited. Overall, current evidence supports POCUS mainly as an adjunct for bedside clarification, escalation support, and physiologic reassessment; direct evidence that POCUS-guided ED sepsis pathways improve patient-centered outcomes remains limited. POCUS should therefore be used as a decision-support tool, not a stand-alone adjudicator or a reason to delay antimicrobials, CT, formal imaging, or specialist involvement.

articles.title: From invasive to non-invasive: point-of-care ultrasound parameters and a clinical decision algorithm for central venous pressure assessment in critically Ill neonates.

abstract.text: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is increasingly used in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) for hemodynamic assessment, but standardized protocols for central venous pressure (CVP) estimation remain lacking. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on POCUS parameters-primarily the inferior vena cava collapsibility index (IVC-CI), maximum IVC diameter, the inferior vena cava-to-aortic ratio (IVC/Ao), and internal jugular vein (IJV) indices-for non-invasive CVP assessment in critically ill neonates. Key advances include demonstrating that ultrasound-measured IVC diameter correlates with invasively measured CVP in low birth weight infants and the emergence of multi-parameter models. However, major barriers persist: inconsistent neonatal-specific thresholds, operator dependence, limited training infrastructure, and insufficient validation in extremely low birth weight populations. We propose a practical clinical decision algorithm integrating IVC and IJV parameters with adjunctive lung and cardiac POCUS assessment, structured reassessment after every fluid bolus, and objective triggers for transitioning to invasive monitoring. Recent guidelines from the European Society of Paediatric and Neonatal Intensive Care (ESPNIC) and the American Society of Echocardiography (ASE) provide foundational frameworks, but dedicated neonatal training and credentialing standards remain essential. Future directions include artificial intelligence-assisted measurement, multi-parameter scoring systems (e.g., Venous Excess Ultrasound score), and multicenter prospective validation. POCUS serves as a complementary tool to-not a replacement for-invasive monitoring in complex hemodynamic instability. Standardized thresholds, structured training, and quality assurance programs are critical for safe clinical translation, especially in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Persistent disparities despite declining carbon monoxide mortality in the United States: a nationwide analysis, 1999-2023.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning remains a preventable cause of mortality. However, emerging evidence suggests that recent progress in prevention may not be equitably experienced across the population groups in the United States. Long-term national assessments of disparities in CO mortality are inadequate.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study sought to identify trends in CO poisoning mortality, assess disparities, and inform future studies.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a descriptive epidemiological study, using national mortality data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Wide-ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research (CDC WONDER) for 1999-2023. The study population included adults aged 25 years and older, with 47,160 deaths identified. Age-adjusted mortality rates were calculated, and trends were assessed using joinpoint regression to estimate annual and average annual percent change (APC and AAPC), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Analyses were stratified by sex, race and ethnicity, age group, geographic region and urban-rural status. All analyses represent primary use of these data.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: National age-standardized mortality declined over the study period (AAPC -3.02%; 95% CI - 4.58 to -1.43), but the decline slowed after 2010. Mortality among Hispanic adults increased substantially after 2016, with signs of trend reversal among non-Hispanic Black adults. Mortality in non-metropolitan areas remained approximately 1.8 times higher than in metropolitan areas, with evidence suggesting that prior declines may have stalled.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Declines in CO poisoning mortality have slowed in the United States, with some evidence of recurrent annual fluctuations, accompanied by widening racial, ethnic, and geographic differences.

articles.title: Age-Dependent Benefit of ECPR in OHCA: An Interaction Analysis.

abstract.text: ECPR effectiveness in OHCA remains inconsistent, and age-related effect modification is not well defined. This retrospective study analyzed 470 adult patients (2011-2025), comparing ECPR (n=71) to CCPR (n=399). Using multivariable regression and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), we found that increasing age independently associated with higher mortality (aOR: 1.064). Also, a significant interaction between age and treatment strategy was identified (p<0.001). ECPR provided a substantial mortality reduction in younger patients, but this benefit progressively attenuated with age. These findings demonstrate that ECPR effectiveness is strongly age-dependent. Consequently, age should be considered as a continuous effect modifier rather than a rigid eligibility threshold for ECPR selection.

articles.title: Designing and implementing the first national CPR championship in Greece: the "KIDS SAVE LIVES - TA PAIDIA SOZOUN ZOES" experience.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Basic Life Support (BLS) is critical in improving survival following out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), yet survival rates remain low in countries such as Greece. Early education and community engagement are key to increasing bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) rates. The "KIDS SAVE LIVES - TA PAIDIA SOZOUN ZOES (KSL)" initiative aims to address this gap through school-based BLS training and innovative educational strategies.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To describe the implementation and evaluate the effectiveness of the first National CPR Championship for school-aged children in Greece.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This study consisted of two phases. Phase I involved the design and implementation of the KSL CPR Championship - a national, school-based competition assessing CPR skills using objective metrics via QCPR technology. Phase II included a post-event evaluation through a 24-item questionnaire distributed to participants (students, teachers, and parents), assessing perceptions, satisfaction, and educational impact.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In 2025 the CPR Championship accommodated 196 schools, comprising of 432 student participants. High-quality CPR performance was observed across all school levels (mean scores: 95.7-96.3% out of 100%, with 88.2% in special needs schools). A total of 197 respondents completed the questionnaire. Most participants (94%) considered the Championship a reliable method for assessing BLS skills, while 99% agreed it was an effective training approach and should be repeated regularly. All respondents reported improved confidence in CPR skills, and 99% would recommend the program. Strong support was expressed for sustained CPR education, including in-school mannequins (99%), AED availability (96%), and mandatory national CPR training in schools (100%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The KSL National CPR Championship represents an effective, engaging, and scalable approach to BLS education among schoolchildren. The initiative enhances skill acquisition, confidence, and community awareness, supporting the integration of structured CPR training into national educational policy to improve OHCA outcomes.

articles.title: Intranasal dexmedetomidine for procedural sedation in preschool children aged 2-6 years undergoing emergency gastric lavage for acute poisoning: a propensity score-matched single-center retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aimed to evaluate the sedative efficacy and peri-procedural safety of preemptive intranasal dexmedetomidine in preschool children receiving emergency gastric lavage due to acute poisoning. Satisfactory procedural compliance rate was predefined as the primary efficacy outcome, and the total incidence of sedation-related adverse events was set as the primary safety outcome. Other behavioral scores, procedure time, vital signs and individual adverse reactions were regarded as secondary exploratory outcomes, and Bonferroni correction was used to correct multiple test bias for secondary indicators. We further quantified its benefits in enhancing procedural compliance, stabilizing peri-procedural vital signs, shortening rescue duration, and optimizing emergency staffing allocation-key practical challenges in overcrowded pediatric emergency departments.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 200 children undergoing emergency gastric lavage for acute poisoning. After propensity score matching (1:1), 100 children received intranasal dexmedetomidine (2 μg/kg) 10 min before the procedure combined with routine comfort care (observation group), and 100 received comfort care and physical restraint only (control group). Procedural compliance, agitation, hemodynamic and respiratory parameters, procedural efficiency, and adverse events were compared between the two groups. Procedural compliance rate served as the predefined primary efficacy outcome, while total adverse event incidence was the primary safety outcome; all remaining indicators were secondary exploratory outcomes adjusted via Bonferroni correction.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Baseline characteristics were well balanced after matching. The observation group had a significantly higher effective compliance rate (93.0% vs. 60.0%) and first-attempt orogastric tube placement success rate (93.0% vs. 64.0%), and a lower agitation rate (7.0% vs. 40.0%) (all P < 0.001). Intraoperative heart rate, respiratory rate, and mean arterial pressure were significantly more stable and remained within normal physiological ranges in the observation group. This sedation protocol shortened lavage duration by 8.90 min, reduced orogastric tube placement attempts and staffing requirement (2.76-1.82 staff per case) (all P < 0.001), greatly improving rescue efficiency. No serious adverse events were observed in this selected cohort in either group, and all mild events resolved spontaneously.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Preemptive intranasal dexmedetomidine may serve as a safe, non-invasive sedative alternative for emergency gastric lavage among selected young children with acute poisoning. In this cohort, it was associated with improved procedural compliance and more stable peri-procedural vital signs. This regimen was also associated with shortened procedural duration and optimized emergency staffing resources, which may be valuable in overcrowded pediatric emergency departments. Observations of rapid onset, favorable tolerability and low frequency of respiratory-related events in the present cohort warrant further investigation in larger pediatric emergency populations.

articles.title: Automated artificial intelligence-enabled measurement of cardiac structures on point-of-care ultrasonography: a prospective multicenter validation study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Point-of-care ultrasonography (POCUS) enables clinicians to obtain critical diagnostic information at the bedside, especially in resource-limited settings. This information may include 2D cardiac quantitative data, although measuring the data manually can be time-consuming and subject to user experience. Artificial intelligence (AI) can potentially automate this quantification. This study assessed the interpretation of key cardiac measurements on POCUS images by an AI-enabled device (AISAP Cardio V1.0).

abstract.label: METHODS
