articles.title: Isolated Aphasia as an Epileptic Manifestation of Neurosarcoidosis: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Acute aphasia requires urgent evaluation for stroke, but recurrent and stereotyped language disturbances may also reflect focal seizures. We report the case of a 23-year-old man brought to the emergency department (ED) with aphasia that had been present for approximately six hours. Over the preceding week, he had experienced several similar but briefer episodes that had resolved spontaneously. He was concurrently undergoing investigation at another institution for persistent hiccups and near-daily vomiting of more than one month's duration. Chest computed tomography (CT) and positron emission tomography (PET)-computed tomography had already shown mediastinal and mesenteric lymphadenopathy suggestive of sarcoidosis, although other etiologies, including malignancy, could not be excluded. Neurological examination was limited by the language disturbance but showed no obvious motor deficit. Brain computed tomography revealed obstructive hydrocephalus with transependymal cerebrospinal fluid flow and multiple enhancing nodular lesions, predominantly in and around the ventricular system. Electroencephalography demonstrated epileptiform activity, and the aphasia resolved after treatment with levetiracetam and clobazam. Further cerebrospinal fluid analysis, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and pathological investigations supported a diagnosis of probable neurosarcoidosis presenting with lymphocytic meningoencephalitis and obstructive hydrocephalus. This case illustrates an unusual pathophysiological sequence, isolated aphasia as a focal epileptic manifestation of neurosarcoidosis, and is a reminder that unexplained focal neurological symptoms, particularly when fluctuating or recurrent, warrant the consideration of seizures and early electroencephalography.

articles.title: Nighttime human-supervised drone-delivered automated external defibrillators: a quasi-experimental mixed-methods feasibility study.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To evaluate the feasibility, safety, and operational challenges of human-supervised flight drone-delivered automated external defibrillator (AED) operations during nighttime for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), using a convergent mixed-methods design integrating quantitative performance metrics with qualitative human factors analysis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A quasi-experimental study with 24 controlled flights (12 daytime, 12 nighttime) was conducted in a semi-urban area using a DJI M30T drone carrying a lightweight CellAED (480 g) over 877 m. Advanced-rated paramedic drone pilots executed human-supervised flight flights under extended visual line of sight (EVLOS), using automated waypoint navigation and manual final approach and landing. protocols. Quantitative data included flight times and safety incidents, analyzed using paired t-tests. Qualitative data from semi-structured pilot interviews were analyzed thematically using the SHELL (Software-Hardware-Environment-Liveware-Liveware) human factors framework. Integration occurred through convergent triangulation comparing quantitative duration metrics with pilot-reported operational themes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: All 24 flights completed successfully without safety incidents or obstacle-avoidance triggers. Mean flight times were comparable (day: 136.00 ± 8.71 s vs. night: 139.92 ± 14.16 s; paired mean difference 3.92 s, S.D. 16.49, p = 0.43, Cohen's d = 0.24). Qualitative analysis identified eight major themes: night-mode interface challenges, GPS routing reliability, infrared sensor performance, pilot fatigue and stress, communication coordination, cognitive workload, landing zone conditions, and regulatory constraints. Triangulation of quantitative and qualitative findings showed that despite comparable flight performance, pilots reported significantly increased cognitive demands and environmental complexity during nighttime operations.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Under controlled, early-night, open-area conditions, all human-supervised flight drone-delivered AED operations missions were completed without observed safety incidents. However, successful nighttime implementation requires addressing pilot workload, interface design, and operational protocols. These findings support development of 24/7 drone AED services while highlighting critical human factors considerations for sustainable operations.

articles.title: Self-reported acute respiratory illness during the pre-ritual and post-return phases of Hajj among South African pilgrims in 2025: a retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Respiratory illness is common during Hajj, but phase-specific data from sub-Saharan African pilgrims remain limited. We examined self-reported acute respiratory illness (ARI) among South African pilgrims during the pre-ritual period in Saudi Arabia and within 14 days after return and assessed associated factors.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective observational cohort study included South African pilgrims accredited for the 2025 (1446H) Hajj. A structured electronic questionnaire was administered approximately 1 month after Hajj to capture symptoms retrospectively over two predefined recall periods. The primary outcome was modified syndromic ARI, defined as two or more self-reported symptoms from cough, subjective fever, sore throat, rhinorrhea, or nasal congestion during the relevant recall period. Logistic regression estimated unadjusted odds ratios and adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of approximately 2500 accredited pilgrims, 541 (21.6%) completed the questionnaire. During the pre-ritual period, 234/541 reported modified syndromic ARI (43.3%; 95% CI 39.1-47.5). Pilgrims aged ≥60 years had lower adjusted odds of pre-ritual ARI than those aged 18-39 years (aOR 0.47; 95% CI 0.26-0.87). Seasonal influenza vaccination was associated with higher odds of pre-ritual ARI (aOR 1.57; 95% CI 1.10-2.26). Within 14 days after return, 257/541 reported ARI (47.5%; 95% CI 43.2-51.8). Pre-ritual ARI remained modestly associated with post-return ARI in exploratory adjusted analysis (aOR 1.46; 95% CI 1.03-2.07), while influenza vaccination was not associated with post-return ARI.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Modified syndromic ARI was common before the core Hajj rites and after return. Findings should not be interpreted as influenza-like illness, coronavirus disease 2019, pathogen-confirmed infection, or influenza vaccine effectiveness.

articles.title: [Heatwaves and Resilience of Hospital Geriatric Care Pathways: Results of the Repeated National PUGG FLASH-HEATWAVE 2026 survey].
articles.journal_full: Geriatrie et psychologie neuropsychiatrie du vieillissement

abstract.text: Extreme heat disproportionately affects frail older adults and may simultaneously disrupt hospital capacity, working conditions, and geriatric care pathways. We aimed to describe thermal conditions, capacity strain, and organizational adaptations in acute geriatric units (AGUs) during a heatwave and one week later, and to describe conditions in medical rehabilitation units (MRUs). PUGG FLASH-HEATWAVE was a repeated national observational, non-interventional service-level survey. Phase 1 surveyed AGUs on 25-26 June 2026; phase 2 surveyed AGUs and MRUs on 2-3 July 2026. Data were aggregated at the service level. Because no stable unit identifier was available, AGU data from the two survey waves were compared as independent samples using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests. Exploratory Mann-Whitney tests assessed the association between room cooling and reported events in phase 1. One hundred and twelve AGUs, representing 4,268 usual beds, participated in phase 1; phase 2 included 30 AGUs (1,007 beds) and 26 MRUs (1,490 beds). In phase 1, 45.5% of AGUs considered patient-room temperatures to be intolerable, 71.4% reported excessive room temperatures as an operational difficulty, and 88.4% reported staff fatigue. Major or critical emergency-department strain affected 57.1% of units, while 64.3% reported capacity strain with consequences for admissions. Downstream rehabilitation and other care capacity was considered insufficient by 87.5% of AGUs. One week later, the proportion of AGUs reporting at least partly tolerable room temperatures had increased from 53.6% to 100.0% (p < 0.001), while at least moderate emergency-department strain decreased from 91.1% to 63.3% (p < 0.001), capacity strain with operational consequences from 64.3% to 40.0% (p = 0.016), and staff fatigue from 88.4% to 50.0% (p < 0.001). Downstream capacity insufficiency remained unchanged (87.5% versus 86.7%; p = 0.903). Among MRUs, 65.4% reported patient rooms that were intolerable or only partly tolerable, 73.1% had postponed or refused admissions, and 88.5% had adapted rehabilitation activities. In phase 1, units with at least partly cooled rooms reported fewer heat-related complications and heatstroke events in unadjusted exploratory analyses. The heatwave acted as a stress test for an already fragile system. Improvements in several indicators of acute strain did not resolve the persistent downstream bottleneck. A national multi-year policy should integrate thermal adaptation of healthcare facilities, protected seasonal capacity, adequate workforce resources, and regional coordination across geriatric care pathways.

articles.title: Temporal Patterns of Sexual Assault Presentations in U.S. Emergency Departments: Implications for Staffing and Forensic Readiness.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Sexual assault (SA) remains a major public health issue, yet only a fraction of survivors seeks acute medical care in emergency departments (EDs). Although previous studies describe demographic disparities among SA survivors, national patterns of ED arrival timing and their operational implications for emergency care systems remain poorly characterized.

abstract.label: STUDY OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To characterize the demographic and temporal patterns of ED presentations for SA in the United States.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a repeated cross-sectional study using the Epic Cosmos database, including U.S. ED encounters related to SA from January 1, 2016 through December 31, 2024. Demographic characteristics and arrival patterns were compared with those of all other ED visits using odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Temporal distributions by day of week and 6-h arrival intervals were analyzed using chi-square testing and standardized Pearson residuals.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 391,352,267 ED visits, 245,475 (0.06%) involved SA evaluation. Patients presenting with SA were disproportionately adolescents and young adults, female, Medicaid-insured, and from minoritized racial groups. Overnight arrivals (00:00-05:59) had significantly higher odds of SA presentation (OR, 1.45; 95% CI, 1.43-1.47), with peak presentations occurring on Sundays and Saturdays overnight. Morning presentations were consistently below expected levels. In 2016, 16% of patients presenting with SA arrived by ambulance; by 2024, this number had increased to 18%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: SA presentations revealed distinct demographic and temporal patterns with important operational implications for EDs. Young and socially vulnerable populations are disproportionately affected. The concentration of presentations during overnight weekend hours highlights the need for expanded access to trauma-informed forensic services, including SA Nurse Examiner coverage and prehospital education, especially during high-demand periods.

articles.title: Giant Jejunal Diverticulosis Causing Acute Mesenteric Volvulus: a Case Report.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Large jejunal diverticula are usually asymptomatic but can cause rare, life-threatening complications including obstruction, perforation, and bleeding. Secondary mesenteric volvulus caused by jejunal diverticulosis is exceptionally rare. It should be strongly considered when computed tomography (CT) reveals a mesenteric "whirl sign" in an adult presenting with acute obstructive symptoms.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: A 76-year-old female presented to the emergency department with acute, diffuse abdominal pain and clinical evidence of mechanical intestinal obstruction. A CT scan demonstrated the characteristic whirl sign of a mesenteric volvulus. Due to severe bowel distension, an urgent open laparotomy was performed. Intraoperatively, a 180-degree torsion of a 60-cm jejunal segment, located 30 cm distal to the ligament of Treitz, was identified. Five giant, fluid-filled diverticula along the mesenteric border created an asymmetric weight burden and localized dysmotility, acting as a mechanical fulcrum that precipitated the volvulus. Thorough exploration explicitly excluded adhesions, bands, internal hernias, or malrotation. No gross mesenteric ischemia was observed. Primary manual detorsion restored complete bowel viability, safely avoiding resection. The postoperative course was unremarkable and the patient remained asymptomatic at the six-month follow-up.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Giant jejunal diverticulosis can act as a physical fulcrum causing secondary mesenteric volvulus. Early open surgical exploration and primary detorsion can achieve complete bowel salvage, preventing the significant morbidity associated with intestinal resection in elderly patients.

articles.title: Spirometry and end-tidal carbon dioxide changes during chest compressions with PPE: a simulation randomized crossover study.
articles.journal_full: Central European journal of public health

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Personal protective equipment (PPE) use in prehospital emergency care has increased significantly since the coronavirus pandemic onset in 2019. Few studies have been published on the PPE effects on spirometry parameters and end-tidal carbon dioxide (Et-CO2). This study aimed to determine whether PPE use affects spirometric parameters and Et-CO2 during chest compressions.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a randomized crossover simulation study with 35 emergency medical service providers who performed 20 minutes of intermittent chest compressions on a mannikin (five 2 min cycles alternated by 2 min of rest). Two iterations were completed in randomized order: without PPE and with PPE. Spirometry parameters (forced vital capacity, forced expiratory volume in 1 s, peak expiratory flow, and Tiffeneau index) and end-tidal carbon dioxide were measured.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: No spirometry parameter differences were noted between the two groups (p > 0.05). When using PPE with an FFP2 mask, Et-CO2 was higher at the end of the first and fifth chest compression cycles (p ≤ 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: PPE use during simulated resuscitation was not associated with deterioration of spirometric parameters. Although Et-CO2 increased slightly during selected CPR cycles, these changes were unlikely to represent clinically relevant respiratory impairment.

articles.title: Bibliometric analysis of international, English-language publication activity in anesthesiology, pain medicine, and intensive and emergency medicine over a 10-year interval.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The present study aimed to clarify how English-language publication activity in anesthesiology, intensive care medicine, and pain medicine has evolved in publishing countries over a 10-year period, considering not only publication volume but also scientific impact and shifting research methodologies.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A bibliometric analysis of 20,741 publications indexed in PubMed for the time periods 2008/09 and 2018/19 was performed across 30 journals. Journals were selected based on their impact factor (IF) in 2019. Publications were analyzed for total number, cumulative impact factors (CIF) - representing the sum of individual journal impact factors multiplied by the number of publications in each journal - study type, country of origin, and country output per million inhabitants.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: From 2008/09 to 2018/19, total publication volume declined by 6.9% from 10,740 to 10,001, while CIF increased by 25.4% from 42,441.2 to 53,219.1. Clinical (Observational) studies were most frequent; meta-analyses and registry studies rose markedly (216.1% and 125.3%, respectively), while experimental studies and randomized controlled trials (RCTs) declined (-51.9% and -29.7%, respectively). The United States led in both publication count (2008/09: 3,267; 2018/19: 4,250) and CIF (2008/09: 14,256.4; 2018/19: 24,421.9). When adjusted to population, smaller countries including Denmark (2008/09: 31.1; 2018/19: 80.7), Switzerland (2008/09: 23.6; 2018/19: 42.1), and the Netherlands (2008/2009: 26.3; 2018/2019: 34.9) ranked highest. Germany - the only leading country showing declining publication output at 7.0% - demonstrated a concerning trend, while China (+83.6%) and Canada (+69.4%) showed exceptional growth.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This study identifies a decline in publication volume alongside increased citation activity in high impact anesthesiology and intensive care medicine journals, largely driven by the dominance of clinical studies and a growing prevalence of meta-analyses and registry studies, suggesting a shift in research priorities. Reduced publication numbers likely result from increasing journal selectivity and redistribution of research output toward open-access and non-specialty journals. The country ranking is dominated by the USA and other English-speaking nations, which can be attributed to the English-language literature analyzed. However, smaller nations like Denmark and Switzerland lead in population-based ranking, revealing critical insights into research infrastructure and institutional support.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence in ultrasound: divergent pathways, shared challenges.

abstract.text: Artificial intelligence (AI) in ultrasound is often reviewed as a unified field, though in practice it spans 3 distinct deployment environments: clinical radiology (traditional imaging) ultrasound, point-of-care users, and ultrasound education. The 3 environments share the same underlying AI methods but differ in image quality, operator skill, time allotted to scan, regulatory exposure, and acceptable failure modes. In clinical radiology ultrasound, FDA-cleared decision support is routine for breast and thyroid lesion characterization, obstetric biometry, and cardiac quantification, and emerging in liver, vascular, and interventional imaging. In point-of-care ultrasound, AI enables bedside clinicians to acquire diagnostic images under real-time guidance and to document examinations that would otherwise go unrecorded. In education, AI reshapes competency assessment and scales instruction. This article offers the practicing radiologist and imaging specialist a framework for matching AI to deployment context, names the mature applications in each pathway, and addresses cross-cutting challenges (data, validation, regulation, bias, liability, reimbursement, environmental cost) that every deployment must navigate. The recurring message: treating "ultrasound AI" as a monolith is a repeated error, and honest attention to deployment context matters most.

articles.title: The Benefits of Managing Anaphylaxis at Home.
articles.journal_full: Immunology and allergy clinics of North America

abstract.text: Based on current data, immediate activation of EMS in all cases of anaphylaxis does not provide significant benefit. Instead, the option for home management or a "watchful-waiting" approach allowing for increased patient autonomy in anaphylaxis management and emphasizing prompt epinephrine use at home. In this model, patients are instructed to quickly administer epinephrine and monitor for resolution of symptoms. The option to escalate care is available, but in 90% of cases, symptoms will resolve after one dose of epinephrine, rendering EMS/ED involvement unnecessary. Thus, patients can immediately treat their anaphylaxis from the comfort of home while avoiding complications from delayed epinephrine use.

articles.title: The pre-hospital pulse: high responsiveness, deployment, and utilisation of ambulance services in India.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: India's National Ambulance Service, a key component of the public health system, operates through 102, 108, and 112 hotline networks.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To assess ambulance performance in terms of responsiveness, deployment, and utilisation. A descriptive study was conducted using ambulance records from two large states in India, Punjab and Haryana, from January to December 2025.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 626,372 hotline calls (72% from rural areas), 97% resulted in ambulance deployment, and 92% were utilised for patient transfers. 91% of ambulances reached the pickup location within 30 min (response time) and 67% transported patients to health facilities within 60 min (call-to-drop time). Median distance travelled by ambulance (parking to drop location) was 32 km (interquartile range 17-58). In Punjab, 50% of call-to-drop times were within 60 min, while in Haryana this was 74%. There were notable interdistrict variations in call-to-drop times. The most common reasons for hotline calls were maternal and obstetric conditions (37%), medical emergencies (27%), and trauma or accidents (17%). Inter-facility transfers accounted for 61% of ambulance utilisation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Our study demonstrates that ambulance services perform at a high level and provide substantial public health value. However, opportunities remain to further strengthen performance, particularly in reducing call-to-drop times.

articles.title: Diagnostic yield of lung point-of-care ultrasound in children with suspected pneumonia in a resource limited setting: a prospective observational study.

abstract.text: Pneumonia is a leading cause of mortality for children under five worldwide and is often diagnosed using WHO clinical criteria. In resource-limited settings, accurate diagnosis remains challenging. Lung ultrasound (LUS) is an effective, low-cost diagnostic tool, however, its performance in smaller regional hospitals remains underexplored. We conducted a prospective observational study to evaluate the diagnostic yield of LUS among children hospitalized with WHO-defined pneumonia in Eastern Uganda. All children received a systematic 12-zone LUS by a trained operator using a linear probe in the sagittal plane. LUS was remotely interpreted by two blinded reviewers. Chest X-ray (CXR) was performed when feasible. We enrolled 46 patients with a total of 523 lung zones reviewed. The average age was 22 months (± 26.8 months); 67% of patients demonstrated hypoxemia. LUS was adequate in 42/46 (91%) children. LUS identified pneumonia in 25/42 (59%), bronchiolitis in 2/42 (5%), and normal lung in 15/42 (36%). CXR was completed in 40/46 (87%) children and showed pneumonia in 18/40 (45%). For the 36 children with both LUS and CXR, four (11%) demonstrated pneumonia on CXR but not LUS, compared to 11 (30%) who had pneumonia on LUS but not CXR. Our study demonstrated that LUS is feasible and identified features of pneumonia is 59% of LUS studies. While the overall diagnostic yield of LUS is comparable to CXR, a substantial proportion of children had pulmonary findings detected by only one imaging modality. These findings suggest a complementary rather than redundant role for LUS and CXR.

articles.title: Penetrating cardiac injury with no initial radiological findings and negative E-FAST: The critical role of clinical judgment.

abstract.text: We report the case of a man in his forties admitted to hospital after being stabbed in the precordial region. The initial chest X-ray and FAST examination revealed nothing abnormal. Despite apparent haemodynamic stability, the patient developed progressive dyspnoea, diaphoresis and signs of circulatory compromise. Due to clinical deterioration, an emergency exploratory thoracotomy was performed. Intraoperative findings revealed haemothorax, haemopericardium, and a perforation of the right atrium associated with pericardial rupture. The cardiac injury was successfully repaired, and the patient recovered favourably. This case demonstrates that initial negative imaging does not rule out significant cardiac injuries in penetrating chest trauma. Careful clinical reassessment and timely surgical intervention remain critical for patient survival.

articles.title: Prehospital transport prioritization and time-varying selection bias in traffic-related multi-patient incidents: a nationwide retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: In prehospital multi-patient traffic incidents, the first ambulance to depart -priority transport - may reflect underlying injury severity rather than a treatment effect, as more severely injured patients are systematically prioritized. Conventional statistical methods often fail to separate this severity-dependent selection from actual outcomes. We applied a "doubly robust" statistical framework (augmented inverse probability weighting, AIPW), which combines a treatment model and an outcome model, to better account for measured differences, reduce selection bias, and examine whether on-scene time modifies this association.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using emergency medical service transport records from the Fire and Disaster Management Agency of Japan (January 2021-December 2023). Of 13,821,224 records, 143,130 patients from traffic-related multi-patient incidents (TMIs; ≥2 patients per incident) with complete data were included. The exposure was priority transport. The primary outcome was physician-assessed death or critical/severe injury at hospital arrival. Marginal adjusted risk differences (RDs) were estimated using AIPW. Effect modification by on-scene time (5-60 min) was assessed by marginal standardization with cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals. Sensitivity analyses included overlap restriction and E-value quantification of unmeasured confounding.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 143,130 patients (median age 41 years; female, 50.57%), 62,769 (43.85%) underwent priority transport. Severe outcomes occurred in 4.35% of priority and 1.87% of non-priority patients. The overall RDs was 2.2% points (95% CI, 2.01-2.36). A significant interaction with on-scene time was observed (p < .001): the marginal RD was peaked at 5 min (6.4% points; 95% CI, 5.6-7.2), declined to a minimum of 1.4% points (95% CI, 1.3-1.6) at approximately 32 min, and increased modestly to 2.4% points (95% CI, 2.0-2.8) at 60 min. Sensitivity analyses confirmed result robustness, yielding an E-value of 3.76 (lower bound, 3.57).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The association between priority transport and severe outcome was modified by on-scene time, with the largest risk difference at the shortest on-scene times. This U-shaped pattern is consistent with preferential selection of more severely injured patients for rapid transport, rather than a direct effect of transport order. Accounting for prehospital triage selection when interpreting transport-outcome associations in critical care research.

articles.title: Open Fractures in Polytrauma and Non-Polytrauma Patients: Outcomes and Predictive Factors in a Level III Trauma Center.
articles.journal_full: Acta chirurgiae orthopaedicae et traumatologiae Cechoslovaca

abstract.label: PURPOSE OF THE STUDY
abstract.text: Open fractures represent complex injuries characterized by bone exposure, soft-tissue damage, and a high risk of infection, often requiring multidisciplinary management. In polytraumatized patients, these injuries further increase clinical complexity and hospital resource utilization. The purpose of this study was to evaluate adherence to international guidelines in the management of open fractures at a third-level trauma center and to identify clinical and organizational predictors of outcomes, complications, and hospitalization burden in polytraumatized and non-polytraumatized patients.

abstract.label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective, single-center study was conducted including all patients treated for open fractures between January 2020 and December 2023. Demographic data, injury mechanisms, fracture location, Gustilo-Anderson grade, surgical timing, treatment strategy (Early Total Care or Damage Control Orthopedics), ICU admission, complications, and readmissions were collected. Polytrauma status was recorded. Primary outcomes included infection rate, length of hospital stay, number of admissions, and cumulative hospitalization time. Statistical analysis was performed using Student's t-test, Fisher's exact test, and Pearson correlation, with significance set at p < 0.05.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 115 patients were included, of whom 53 (46.1%) were polytraumatized. The mean age was 47.1 years, with a male predominance. Lower-limb fractures were most common, particularly involving the tibia. Grade III injuries accounted for 61.7% of cases. Surgical debridement was performed within 6 hours in 65.2% of patients. External fixation for damage control was used in 73% of cases, with a mean fixation duration of 103 days. Postoperative ICU admission was required in 27.8% of patients. Overall infection rate was 15.7%. Polytraumatized patients experienced significantly longer hospital stays and a higher number of readmissions, but polytrauma status was not associated with increased infection risk. Higher Gustilo-Anderson grade showed a strong correlation with prolonged hospitalization and infection. Damage control strategies were associated with longer cumulative hospitalization and more frequent readmissions but not with higher infection rates.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: These findings indicate that fracture severity and local tissue damage, rather than polytrauma status itself, are the main determinants of infection risk and hospitalization burden. While polytrauma increases overall resource utilization, standardized multidisciplinary management allows comparable orthopedic outcomes. Damage control orthopedics remains essential in severe cases but implies longer and more fragmented care pathways.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In a high-volume trauma center adhering to international guidelines, open fracture outcomes are primarily driven by injury severity. Polytrauma influences hospitalization burden but not infection risk. Awareness of these factors is essential for optimizing trauma pathways, resource allocation, and patient counseling.

articles.title: National Crisis-Induced Psychological Stress and Increased Herpes Zoster Incidence: A 10-Year Retrospective Study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Psychological stress is known to affect dermatological conditions, but its impact during national crises is not well established.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To assess the association between crisis-induced stress and the incidence of infectious and inflammatory skin diseases, focusing on herpes zoster.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective cross-sectional study was performed using emergency room records from Hadassah Medical Center, Israel. Skin-related visits were compared between October and December 2023 (national crisis), and the same months in 2014-2022: between the COVID-19 lockdowns (March-May 2020, December 2020-February 2021) and pre-pandemic years (2014-2022). Logistic regression models, adjusted for age and sex, evaluated disease incidence.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1,644 patients, infectious skin diseases increased significantly during the October-December 2023 crisis (odds ratio (OR)=2.106; P<0.001), mainly due to herpes zoster (OR=2.616; P=0.009). No significant change was observed for inflammatory skin diseases. During COVID-19 lockdowns, no significant difference was found, likely reflecting reduced healthcare utilization.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: National crisis-related stress was associated with higher incidence of infectious skin diseases, particularly herpes zoster, but not with inflammatory conditions. These findings support targeted interventions, including vaccination and stress management, during crises.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes of High-dose Intravenous Nitroglycerin in Sympathetic Crashing Acute Pulmonary Edema.
articles.journal_full: Journal of emergencies, trauma, and shock

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Sympathetic Crashing Acute Pulmonary Edema (SCAPE) is a life-threatening form of acute heart failure requiring immediate management with noninvasive ventilation (NIV) and vasodilator therapy. Although nitroglycerin (NTG) is commonly used, optimal dosing remains uncertain. Emerging evidence suggests high-dose NTG may provide rapid clinical improvement. We aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of high-dose intravenous NTG in patients presenting with SCAPE to the emergency department (ED).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a prospective observational study in a high-volume, busy ED, enrolling adults (>18 years) meeting established diagnostic criteria for SCAPE who received an initial intravenous NTG bolus ≥400 μg. Patients with acute coronary syndrome, trauma, recent phosphodiesterase V inhibitor use, or significant aortic stenosis were excluded. Clinical status and outcomes were assessed at 3, 6, and 12 h, and at ED disposition. The primary objective was clinical outcomes (symptom resolution, need for intubation, and ED disposition) of SCAPE patients.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Sixty-one patients were included. The mean NTG bolus dose was 830 μg. One patient (1.6%) developed hypotension requiring fluids and brief inotropic support. Headache occurred in five patients (8.2%). Symptom resolution was observed in 10 patients (16%) at 3 h, 32 (52.5%) at 6 h, and 55 (90%) at 12 h. Five patients (8.2%) required intubation. Overall, 41 patients (67.2%) were discharged directly from the ED. The mean ED length of stay was 14 h.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: High-dose intravenous NTG may improve clinical outcomes in the acute management of SCAPE, with rapid symptom resolution and reduced need for intubation. Larger studies are warranted to confirm these findings and to standardise dosing protocols.

articles.title: Twenty years in the battle against sudden cardiac death: progress, pitfalls, and prospects for the future.

abstract.text: Sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) is a life-threatening emergency that requires immediate intervention from lay responders. To address this critical need, the national Sudden Cardiac Arrest Foundation (SCAF) was established in 2005 to raise awareness, promote community engagement, and support survivors. The history of cardiopulmonary resuscitation, defibrillation, and public response programs illustrates decades of progress in resuscitation science and has helped lay the groundwork for the creation of SCAF. In addition to serving as a trusted information hub, SCAF leads several key initiatives. The Cardiac Arrest Survivor Alliance™ provides an online community for those affected by cardiac arrest, offering connection, support, and resources. The Call-Push-Shock campaign promotes three lifesaving steps to address out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: call 911, perform CPR, and use an automated external defibrillator (AED). While SCA remains a major cause of death, significant progress has been made in public education and response. Technological innovations such as dispatcher-assisted CPR, the widespread placement of AEDs, and improved EMS and cardiac arrest registries, have all strengthened the chain of survival. Public understanding has also improved, with the media increasingly distinguishing SCA from heart attacks, thanks in part to SCAF's tireless advocacy. As SCAF marks its 20th anniversary, the organization celebrates two decades of progress and looks ahead with optimism. Its mission remains steadfast: to raise awareness, empower bystanders to act, support survivors, and advance innovations that reduce preventable deaths from sudden cardiac arrest.

articles.title: Suicidality-Related Emergency Department Visits Among US Children and Adolescents, 2016-2022.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To examine national trends in suicidality-related (intentional self-harm, self-inflicted injury, and suicide attempt) emergency department (ED) visits among US children and adolescents between 2016 and 2022 and describe demographic and psychiatric correlates across age groups.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: Data were obtained from the 2016 to 2022 Nationwide Emergency Department Sample (NEDS) for patients aged 5 to 19 years with suicidality-related ICD-10-CM codes. Weighted national estimates, demographics, and psychiatric comorbidities were compared across age groups (5-9, 10-14, and 15-19 years). Temporal trends were evaluated using Daniel's test for trend, with p < .05 considered significant.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were an estimated 1,100,785 suicidality-related ED visits (intentional self-harm 61%, self-inflicted injury 39%, suicide attempt 9%). The number of visits increased significantly among age group 10 to 14 for all diagnoses (p ≤ .01) and among age group 15 to 19 for suicide attempts only (p = .003). Female patients (74.7%) accounted for most visits. Depression (45.3%) and anxiety (21.6%) were the most common comorbidities.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Suicidality-related ED visits among US youth remain alarmingly high, especially among young adolescents. The predominance of depression, anxiety, and female patient representation underscores the need for early, community-based mental health interventions and post-ED follow-up care.

abstract.label: CLINICAL GUIDANCE
abstract.text: • Screen earlier and repeatedly. Incorporate routine suicide risk screening beginning in late elementary school (ages 9-10), especially during well-child visits, school physicals, and emergency department encounters, even when presenting complaints are nonpsychiatric.• Treat self-harm as a high-risk signal. Any self-inflicted injury-regardless of stated intent-should trigger a structured suicide risk assessment, safety planning, and close follow-up, as self-harm often precedes suicide attempts.• Address comorbid depression, anxiety, and trauma aggressively. Early identification and evidence-based treatment (eg, cognitive behavioral therapy, dialectical behavior therapy-informed skills, trauma-focused care) should be prioritized, with coordinated family involvement when developmentally appropriate.• Strengthen transitions of care after emergency department visits. Ensure rapid outpatient follow-up (within 7 days), clear communication with caregivers, and linkage to school- and community-based supports, particularly for preteens and adolescents from low-income households.

abstract.label: DIVERSITY & INCLUSION STATEMENT
abstract.text: One or more of the authors of this paper self-identifies as a member of one or more historically underrepresented racial and/or ethnic groups in science. We actively worked to promote sex and gender balance in our author group. We actively worked to promote inclusion of historically underrepresented racial and/or ethnic groups in science in our author group. The author list of this paper includes contributors from the location and/or community where the research was conducted who participated in the data collection, design, analysis, and/or interpretation of the work.

articles.title: Smartphone-Measured Sleep Health Risk Factors Detect Suicidal Thoughts and Behaviors Among Adolescents.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Suicide deaths and poor sleep health in adolescents have significantly increased. Smartphone sensors (eg, accelerometry) provide an unobtrusive and scalable way to monitor sleep health over extended time periods. We hypothesized that poor weekly sleep health (ie, shorter and variable time in bed; late and variable bedtime) assessed through smartphone sensors would associate with weekly suicidal thoughts and behaviors (STB).

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: High-risk adolescents (N = 145, 13-18 years of age, 112 female) oversampled for STB (n = 114) installed the Effortless Assessment Research System application on their smartphones, allowing access to motion data over 6 months. Simultaneously, the app measured weekly suicidal ideation. Clinical interviews measured suicidal events (ie, attempts, specifc psychiatric hospitalizations, and emergency department events related to suicide risk) at 1-, 3-, and 6-month follow-up assessments. Mixed-effects logistic regression models tested whether the weekly average and variability of time in bed and bedtime related to next-week STB.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A 1-SD in weekly time in bed, relative to one's typical weekly time in bed, related to a near 2-fold greater odds of a next-week suicidal event (odds ratio [OR] = 1.85, 95% CI = 1.01, 3.28, p = .045). This was driven by time in bed on weekdays (OR = 2.39, 95% CI = 1.19, 4.44, p = .013). Greater variability of bedtimes (ie, lower bedtime consistency) within a weekend, relative to one's own typical weekend bedtime variability, predicted next-week suicidal ideation (OR = 1.91, 95% CI = 1.28, 2.69, p = .001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Results reveal proximal associations between smartphone-derived sleep measures and STB, highlighting the possibility of developing just-in-time interventions, focusing on which sleep behaviors to modify and when to intervene to reduce suicide risk.

articles.title: Social Prescribing as Strategic Infrastructure: Unlocking Community Capacity for Sustainable Healthcare When Institutions Reach Their Limits.

abstract.text: Canada's healthcare system is approaching structural limits: nearly $400 billion in annual spending, while nearly one in five Canadians is without a regular healthcare provider, emergency departments overflow and health inequities persist that universal coverage alone cannot resolve. This paper argues that social prescribing, a structured referral system connecting people to community resources through trained link workers, offers not merely an additional program but a paradigm shift. By making visible the economic and social value of community-based health work, social prescribing functions as a strategic catalyst for an enabling state model of healthcare: one that redirects public investment toward the community infrastructure where health is actually produced. This paper traces Canada's health system through three historical paradigms: the nation state, the welfare state and the emerging enabling state. It shows how social prescribing bridges the transition, with modelling suggesting a potential return of $4.43 for every dollar invested while building resilience against the compounding disruptions of climate change, trade instability and geopolitical uncertainty. Drawing on Canadian pilots, international evidence and cross-sectoral economic analysis, the paper offers recommendations for community organizations and governments to recognize, resource and protect the resilient future that Canadian communities are already building.

articles.title: Neuroendovascular Interventions and Stroke Care in Tajikistan: A Comprehensive Review of Emerging Capacity, Systemic Challenges, and Regional Implications.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This article evaluates the current state of stroke management and neuroendovascular services in Tajikistan, identifying key barriers, recent advancements, and strategies for improvement within a regional context.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: This narrative review integrates data from peer-reviewed publications, international health repositories (Global Burden of Disease, World Health Organization, World Bank), Tajik governmental policies, and Central Asian health analyses. Sources were chosen for relevance to stroke epidemiology, health care infrastructure, neuroendovascular capabilities, and policy environments.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Tajikistan experiences a high stroke incidence and mortality, primarily attributable to uncontrolled hypertension, environmental pollutants, and suboptimal dietary patterns. Health care limitations encompass prolonged prehospital response times, restricted diagnostic imaging, personnel deficiencies, and nascent rehabilitation frameworks. Neuroendovascular procedures commenced in 2025 with a single case of initial aneurysm embolization and stroke mechanical thrombectomy, thus far, at a single facility in Dushanbe. National initiatives prioritize noncommunicable disease mitigation and primary health care enhancement, while cross-border collaborations and telemedicine present viable options for capacity expansion.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Although Tajikistan's stroke and neuroendovascular sectors are underdeveloped, targeted enhancements in education, equipment, emergency protocols, and global alliances could substantially improve patient outcomes. These insights may also apply to neighboring Central Asian nations.

articles.title: Effect of Fentanyl Added to Bupivacaine for Intrathecal Injection on the Outcome of Neonates Delivered by Caesarean Section under Spinal Anaesthesia.
articles.journal_full: Journal of the West African College of Surgeons

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Addition of fentanyl to 0.5% hyperbaric bupivacaine for subarachnoid block (SAB) enhances the efficacy of bupivacaine and enables the use of reduced doses of the two drugs, thereby minimising their adverse effects. However, fentanyl may cross the placenta and cause chest wall rigidity, cardiovascular and respiratory depression in the foetus, resulting in poor neonatal outcome.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study aimed to determine and compare the effects of 20 and 25 µg fentanyl added to 10 mg 0.5% hyperbaric bupivacaine on the outcome of neonates delivered by caesarean section under SAB.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: Ninety-nine pregnant women, aged 18-45 years and American Society of Anaesthesiologists I and II, were randomly divided into three equal groups: group A, group B, and group C. Each group received 2 mL (10 mg) 0.5% hyperbaric bupivacaine, and in addition, group A received 0.5 mL normal saline, group B received 0.4 mL (20 µg) fentanyl + 0.1 mL normal saline, whereas group C received 0.5 mL (25 µg) fentanyl. Following delivery, the newborn babies' Apgar scores, Neurological and Adaptive Capacity Scores (NACS), umbilical cord arterial blood gas, peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2), and pulse rate were assessed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The mean Apgar scores at 1 and 5 min and the mean NACS at 15 min and 2 h were significantly lower in the fentanyl/bupivacaine groups compared with the bupivacaine only group (P < 0.001). The mean pH and SpO2/PR of the neonates were within normal neonatal range but decreased from group A to group C (P < 0.05).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Neonates whose mothers received bupivacaine only had better outcomes than those who received bupivacaine/fentanyl combination, whereas those who received 20 µg fentanyl had better outcomes than those who received 25 µg.

articles.title: A Pediatric Psychology Bridge Clinic as an Acute Care and Emergency Department Diversion Service.
articles.journal: Evid Based Pract Child Adolesc Ment Health
articles.journal_full: Evidence-based practice in child and adolescent mental health

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The needs of pediatric patients presenting to emergency departments for psychiatric complaints far exceed the capacity of available acute care services. A Pediatric Psychology Bridge Clinic was established to provide short-term care for patients while they await outpatient therapeutic services.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study characterizes the demographics, clinical presentation, and recidivism of patients treated in this Bridge Clinic in an 18-month period.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: Data were gathered from a retrospective chart review of 74 patients referred to the Bridge Clinic. These patients were also compared to a matched sample of patients who were admitted to a psychiatric inpatient unit during the same time frame.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The 74 Bridge Clinic patients ranged from 6 to 17 years old (M = 13.96; SD = 2.57); were predominantly female (61%); and predominantly White (40%) or Black (36%). The most common chief complaints at emergency department presentation were suicide/self-harm (73%) and aggression (20%). 88% of referred patients attended their scheduled Bridge intake appointment, and only 2 patients returned to the emergency department prior to the appointment. The Bridge Clinic and inpatient unit groups did not differ on chief complaint or on emergency department recidivism rates within 6 months. The average emergency department length of stay for Bridge Clinic patients (35 hours) was significantly shorter than for patients who were admitted to the inpatient unit (73 hours).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The current study demonstrates that a Bridge Clinic providing short-term access to mental healthcare is an effective way to reduce emergency department lengths of stay and provide therapeutic support to patients presenting with high levels of psychiatric acuity.

articles.title: Randomized controlled trial of emotion regulation therapy versus cognitive behavioral therapy to address distress in cancer caregivers.
articles.journal_full: Annals of behavioral medicine : a publication of the Society of Behavioral Medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) shows promise for addressing distress in cancer caregivers, though results are mixed. Traditional CBT may not fully address transdiagnostic processes underlying caregiver distress, such as attentional rigidity and perseverative thinking. Emotion Regulation Therapy (ERT), a contemporary CBT targeting these mechanisms, has promise for cancer caregivers (ERT-C). We compared ERT-C to caregiver-adapted CBT (CBT-C) on caregiver- and patient-reported outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a multisite RCT (ERT-C vs. CBT-C) with distressed caregivers of patients with any cancer type or stage. Caregivers completed measures of anxiety, depression, worry, rumination, burden, and quality of life (QOL) at baseline, post-treatment, and 3- and 6-months follow-up. Patients reported outcomes at baseline and 3 months. Linear mixed-effects models with multiple imputation were used to assess group differences.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: From March 2021 to April 2024, we randomized 253 caregivers, of whom 244 were analyzed (ERT-C = 124; CBT-C = 120), and enrolled 95 patients (ERT-C = 47; CBT-C = 48), of whom 87 were analyzed. From pre- to post-treatment and through 6 months follow-up, caregivers in ERT-C did not improve significantly more than in CBT-C. Although there were significant between-group differences in patient physical and mental health, these effects did not persist after multiplicity adjustment. However, caregivers overall demonstrated significant improvements over time in anxiety, depression, worry, and QOL, and patients demonstrated significant improvements in perceived stress and emergency room visits.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Although ERT-C was not superior to CBT-C, caregivers showed meaningful psychosocial improvements overall, and patients improved on 2 outcomes. Future work will examine whether the 2 treatments differentially engage putative mechanisms leading to the observed clinical findings.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: This trial is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (identifier: NCT04802720).

articles.title: Development of a global occupational health and safety management system model for Japanese companies and validation of its effectiveness.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To extend a global occupational health and safety management system model for Japanese companies-a hybrid model integrating the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 45001 standard with company-wide minimum standards set by headquarters and good practices adapted to local conditions-beyond Southeast Asia, the region covered in the original pilot study, and to verify its long-term effectiveness.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: At a large Japanese manufacturer of construction and mining machinery, we examined over 2013-2026 (a net 12 years, excluding a 2-year suspension during the COVID-19 pandemic) the development of headquarters functions, and changes in 13 performance-audit item scores at 8 production sites in North America, Europe, and Asia.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: All 9 headquarters functions were established over approximately 12 years. Total audit scores increased at 6 of the 8 production sites; 2 sites showed no improvement. The largest numbers of sites remained below the target level for risk-reduction measures and risk assessment; together with officer competency, the only item showing no change in mean score, these findings revealed a structural lag in occupational hygiene relative to safety.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The model promoted both headquarters maturation and site-level improvement outside Southeast Asia. Strengthening occupational hygiene will require more direct headquarters interventions, such as expert dispatch and technical support, in addition to standard-setting and auditing.

articles.title: Patient reported outcomes and return to play after arthroscopic hip labral reconstruction in athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract.text: Femoroacetabular impingement is a common cause of labral damage and hip pain in athletes. In severe labral tears with inadequate healthy labrum for repair, labral reconstruction has shown positive clinical outcomes in the general population. This study aimed to conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis on athletes undergoing arthroscopic hip labral reconstruction, focusing on postoperative patient-reported outcomes (PROs) and return to play (RTP). A systematic review of the literature was performed to include studies reporting PROs of labral reconstruction in athletes across multiple databases. Of the initial 430 identified records, four satisfied inclusion criteria of reporting PROs at 1-year minimum follow-up and RTP. Athletes included recreational through professional levels. Three studies analyzed return to same level of play (RTSP). Meta-analysis was conducted by pooling data, creating forest plots, and reporting odds ratios (OR). The four studies included 126 hips with average age at surgery of 32.2 years. All PROs in each study showed significant improvements with postoperative pooled weighted improvements in modified Harris Hip Score by 18.9 (Cohen's d = 1.10), Non-arthritic Hip Score by 19.6 (Cohen's d = 1.10), Hip Outcome Score-Sport by 25.6 (Cohen's d = 1.15), and Visual Analogue Scale-Pain by -3.0 (Cohen's d = -1.81). RTP averaged 81.4%, ranging from 73.3% to 90.0%. RTSP ranged from 40.6% to 81.0% with an overall OR of 83 (I²= 0.00). This meta-analysis found excellent patient-reported clinical outcomes at 1-year minimum follow-up after labral reconstruction in athletes, and a return-to-play rate of 81.4%. These data can help counsel athletes who undergo arthroscopic hip labral reconstruction.

articles.title: Epidemiological Study of Rescue Records in University Karate Competitions in Japan.
articles.journal_full: Journal of plastic and reconstructive surgery

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: In Japan, Karate is widely practiced as a traditional martial art. In a kumite (contact fighting) competition, as in other martial arts, the outcome of the contest is judged by the effectiveness of punches and kicks, which naturally makes it difficult to prevent injuries. The present retrospective observational study aimed to clarify the epidemiology of injuries sustained by Karate athletes to improve the safety of the sport.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Data on sex, university year, injury site (head and neck, face, trunk, upper limbs, lower limbs), injury type, and examination and treatment details of individuals who were injured while performing Karate were extracted from the rescue records of the Karate competitions of the Kanto University Karate Federation between 2000 and 2014.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Records of 67 tournaments and medical interventions for 597 male and 156 female patients were identified. The number of interventions for injuries to the head and neck, face, trunk, upper limbs, and lower limbs was 85, 337, 22, 105, and 164, respectively. Sixty-two patients, with 23 and 25 injuries in total to the head and neck area and the face, respectively, required transport by ambulance.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The present study revealed that male competitors suffered more injuries, that the most common site of injury was the face, and that injuries to the head and neck area and the face were most likely to be severe. The high frequency of facial injuries in combat sports warrants greater involvement of plastic surgeons in their treatment and prevention.
